indeed:5e6713f9ef615246.title: PhD Position in EU Doctoral Network "PANDORA"
indeed:5e6713f9ef615246.desc: PhD Position in EU Doctoral Network "PANDORA" Réf ABG-140512 Sujet de Thèse 13/10/2026 Financement de l'Union européenne Sorbonne Université Lieu de travail Paris - Ile-de-France - France Intitulé du sujet PhD Position in EU Doctoral Network "PANDORA" Champs scientifiques Biologie Santé, médecine humaine, vétérinaire Mots clés Biological sciences, Biology, Medical sciences, Neurosciences, Immunology Description du sujet The position focuses on "Evaluating how complement dysregulation influences mononuclear phagocyte accumulation in AMD" within the MSCA Doctoral Network PANDORA (Discovering Pathomechanisms and Novel Drug Optimization for AMD). Subretinal mononuclear phagocytes (MPs) build up in the photoreceptor cell layer, a zone normally kept free of immune cells by the immunosuppressive retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). This build-up is a key driver of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). MPs include microglia and monocyte-derived inflammatory macrophages (MoMφ). Our team has shown that activated MPs evade RPE-mediated clearance. We have also shown that the AMD-linked CFH 402H variant impairs the removal of subretinal MPs independently of its role in the complement system. How complement dysregulation contributes to immune cell accumulation in the subretinal space in AMD remains poorly understood. The PhD student will first map where complement cascade components are found in the human retina. Using multiplexed immunohistochemistry on post-mortem retinal sections from AMD donors and age-matched controls, the student will localise components of the classical, lectin and alternative pathways, their activation products, regulators (CFH and Factor H-related proteins) and receptors. These components will be mapped relative to subretinal MPs, the RPE, photoreceptors and drusen. The student will then study how the Chromosome 1 (Chr1) AMD risk haplotype affects RPE, microglia and MoMφ and their interactions. They will use control and Chr1-risk iPSC-derived cells in a well-defined co-culture system developed in our laboratory. The student will also study the role of plasma-derived Factor H-related proteins (FHR1-5) using depleted human plasma and purified complement factors. Using single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing and proteomics, the student will analyse how complement dysregulation affects: microglia and MoMφ polarisation the interaction of these cells with the immunosuppressive RPE key inflammatory pathways and immune functions in the subretinal microenvironment, in health and in AMD Finally, the student will test whether complement inhibitors (anti-C5, anti-C3) can restore immune balance. The project is supervised by Dr. Florian Sennlaub (Institut de la Vision, Paris) It is carried out in close collaboration with other PANDORA doctoral candidates. Techniques and Training Include: Multiplexed immunohistochemistry on human donor retinal sections (AMD and age-matched controls), whole-slide/confocal imaging and quantitative image analysis Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived RPE, microglia and macrophage models, and immune cell/RPE co-cultures Primary human monocyte isolation and differentiation, and work with human plasma and purified complement factors Single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, and proteomics Flow cytometry, qPCR, western blot, ELISA/multiplex cytokine assays Functional immune assays (phagocytosis, migration, survival/clearance) Prise de fonction : 01/02/2027 Nature du financement Financement de l'Union européenne Précisions sur le financement Horizon Europe – MSCA (Marie Curie Actions) Présentation établissement et labo d'accueil Sorbonne Université Founded by Professor José-Alain Sahel, the Institut de la Vision is an international research centre dedicated entirely to research into eye and vision diseases. It brings together researchers, doctors, patients and industry on the same site to discover innovative treatments for eye diseases and improve the quality of life of visually impaired people. It is being built on a site that brings together l’Hôpital national de la vision des 15-20 and its Clinical Investigation Centre (CIC), as well as the Centre for Rare Retinal Diseases. Designed as a place where people can come together and exchange ideas, the Institut de la Vision enables ideas to be shared, new questions to emerge and the transfer of research findings to patient care to be accelerated. Its innovative organisation, based around hospital patients, enables new therapeutic or technological solutions to be discovered, tested and developed in order to prevent eye diseases or limit their effects. More than 300 researchers are working in the 5 research departments of the Institut de la Vision: developmental biology of the visual system, genetics, visual information processing, pathophysiology and therapeutics, photonics. All the Institut de la Vision's activities and projects are coordinated by its Foundation (Foundation Institut de la vision), in conjunction with its three supervisory bodies: Sorbonne University, Inserm and the CNRS. Site web : http://www.institut-vision.org Profil du candidat Education Level: Master's Degree or equivalent in life sciences, biology, immunology, neurobiology or biomedical sciences Essential Skills/Qualifications: Solid knowledge of cellular and molecular biology and/or immunology Excellent written and oral English proficiency Strong motivation for research on retinal degeneration and neuroinflammation Ability to work both in a team and independently Preferred Qualifications: Hands-on experience in cell culture (ideally primary immune cells or iPSC-derived cells) and flow cytometry Experience with immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence and image analysis Background in innate immunity, macrophage/microglia biology and the complement system Interest in, or basic experience with, omics data analysis Language: Excellent English (French not required) Applicants must meet these requirements: They must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in France for more than 12 months in the 36 months before the recruitment date. Compulsory national service and time spent in refugee status procedures are excluded. They must not already hold a doctoral degree. They can be of any nationality. Date limite de candidature 30/11/2026

indeed:6c9ad7ce59d04bb6.title: PhD: Impact evaluation of climate policies in agricultural and forest landscapes
indeed:6c9ad7ce59d04bb6.desc: Your job Have you ever wondered how we can ensure that climate mitigation and adaptation policies are fair, coherent, and effective? Are you interested in applying state-of-the-art impact evaluation techniques to analyze how climate policies affect land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity? Do you good communication skills in Spanish? Then this might be your next step! Climate change mitigation and adaptation in agriculture and forestry represent a “wicked problem”, shaped by uncertainty, conflicting objectives, institutional fragmentation and time pressure. While the EU has set ambitious climate targets for 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050, progress in agriculture and forestry remains insufficient and current policy frameworks have not yet resulted in significant climate mitigation and adaptation results, or generated the systemic transformation needed. This PhD position is part of the EU-Horizon project “ Evidence-based pathways towards fair, coherent and effective climate policies for Europe’s agriculture and forestry (PolicyForClimate) ”, which will develop tools and frameworks to enable policymakers and other stakeholders to design fair, coherent, and effective climate mitigation and adaptation policies in the EU. The project will use AI-assisted evidence synthesis, a policy-lab approach, and embedded case studies to offer a continuously updated evidence base on policy impacts, trade-offs, synergies, and spillovers. Your research will focus on developing, applying, and validating a novel mixed-methods framework for ex-post impact evaluation of climate policies in forestry and agricultural landscapes. By combining state-of-the-art econometric techniques with qualitative participatory approaches, you will empirically analyze how climate policies have affected land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity metrics. This will require conducting systematic reviews on existing impact evaluation frameworks, run workshops and focus group discussions with various stakeholders, collect, combine, and analyze farm-level primary data and secondary spatially explicit data. Start date: February 2027. Your duties and responsibilities include: Conduct systematic literature reviews and workshops to develop a mixed-methods ex-post impact evaluation framework for climate policies; Apply rigorous econometric methods together with qualitative assessments , particularly from policy sciences, to evaluate the impact of specific climate policies on land cover, carbon, and biodiversity metrics; Conduct focus group discussions with various stakeholders in the EU to validate the proposed impact evaluation framework and results from the empirical analyses; Write research papers and present research findings at international academic conferences; Collaborate with our research partners and contribute to the dissemination of project results . You will work here You will be based at the Forest and Nature Conservation Policy Group (FNP) at Wageningen University . The FNP group focuses on the political, socio-economic and cultural dimensions of forests and nature. Our research addresses major challenges including biodiversity conservation, deforestation, forest transitions, climate change and landscape management in both the Global North and Global South. You will be jointly supervised by Dr. Jorge Sellare and Prof. Bas Arts from Wageningen University (WU-FNP), and by Dr. Dario Schulz (EFI) in the research group headed by Sven Wunder. Your qualities We are looking for a researcher with a strong interest in climate adaptation and mitigation policies and in exploring the underlying causal mechanisms through which they affect land, GHG emissions, and biodiversity. You enjoy working with both quantitative and qualitative data and are motivated to conduct research that combines rigorous econometric analysis with qualitative assessments and with real-world challenges facing farmers and forest owners. Fieldwork in Spain will be an important component of the PhD project, so Spanish language skills are critical. You should be enthusiastic about working with farmers and able to spend time in rural areas of Spain under fieldwork conditions. You also possess: a successfully completed MSc degree in agricultural economics, environmental economics, environmental policy, forestry or a closely related field; affinity with applied econometrics and / or qualitative mixed methods and an interest in developing your skills in both; knowledge of GIS and spatial data analysis is an asset; good skills with statistical software such as R, Stata or Python; very good communication skills in Spanish (min. level B2); For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level. Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here. We offer Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment. A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include: Partially paid parental leave; working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance; there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee; a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%; excellent pension scheme. In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team. The gross salary for the first year is € 3.204,- per month rising to € 4.051,- in the fourth year in according to the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (scale P). This is based on a full-time working week of 38 hours. We offer a temporary contract for 18 months which will be extended for the duration of the project if you perform well. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help. You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment. Coming from abroad Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees. Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. indeed:762a4493fab66793.title: PhD in Acoustic Performance of Timber Structure Connections
indeed:762a4493fab66793.desc: Sustainability, in its broadest definition, is the cornerstone of research and education in the Department of Built Environment. We take the lead in (re)shaping the built environment to be future-proof, safe, healthy, inclusive and respectful of planetary boundaries. We house the entire spectrum of technology, engineering, design, and human behavior disciplines in the built environment, with world-class experimental facilities at all scales. This allows us to address societal challenges from a uniquely integrated perspective. Introduction Are you fascinated by improving the acoustic performance of timber buildings? Help develop advanced numerical models that predict sound transmission and bridge the gap between sustainable construction and high acoustic performance. Join this joint PhD project between TU/e and DTU! Job Description Buildings made from timber and other biobased materials generally have a significantly lower carbon footprint than conventional concrete or masonry constructions. However, lightweight timber structures often exhibit high variability in sound insulation, and poor acoustic performance remains a barrier to their wider adoption in the construction industry. A still poorly understood source of this variability lies in the connections between structural components, such as screws, nails, steel brackets, and adhesive joints. Whether a floor is screwed or glued together, and how widely spaced the fasteners are, can significantly affect how sound travels through a building. Current prediction methods largely ignore these details, while more detailed models are often too computationally expensive for practical use. Developing methods that are both physically accurate and computationally efficient is therefore the central challenge of this project. We offer a PhD position (4-year contract) within the QUIET-ARC project, a collaboration between Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as part of the EuroTech Universities PhD programme. As a PhD candidate in the QUIET-ARC project, you will investigate how different connection types and layouts influence sound transmission in timber buildings, develop efficient numerical simulation methods to model these effects, and quantify the uncertainty introduced by construction variability into acoustic predictions. Noise is recognised by the World Health Organisation as a major public health concern. By improving the predictive capability of computational models for timber buildings, this research supports more reliable prediction tools for sustainable constructions and contributes to the wider adoption of low-carbon building materials. The project will take place under joint supervision of dr.ir. Cédric Van hoorickx (TU/e, specializing in numerical modelling of sound transmission) and dr.ir. Jonas Brunskog (DTU, with expertise in the acoustics of lightweight structures). You will be based in the Building Acoustics research group (https://building-acoustics.net/) in the Department of the Built Environment at TU/e, and will spend approximately six months at DTU’s Acoustic Technology group in Denmark. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in acoustics, building physics, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, or related disciplines. A research-oriented attitude. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). The following experience could be considered an advantage and may be highlighted in your motivation letter: Affinity for building acoustics, vibro-acoustics, or structural dynamics Previous experience with/affinity for computational methods Previous publications and scientific communications Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here. indeed:836c4d0d5125de9c.title: PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on ML-methods in climate modelling
indeed:836c4d0d5125de9c.desc: The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain. We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic. The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment. You can read more about us here: the Department of Meteorology. Project description Clouds and their responses to varying environmental conditions are particularly important determinants of current climate and future climate change. However, the resolution of a typical climate model is far too coarse to explicitly represent processes of relevance to cloud formation. Those processes therefore need to be parameterized, or represented as functions of large-scale state variables. Such sub-grid scale parameterizations are associated with large uncertainties, and are also computationally expensive. This project focuses on novel ways to bridge between micro- and global scales, to improve climate model accuracy, efficiency and generalizability, and leverage modern computer architecture. We will explore the use of machine learning (ML) models trained on combinations of observational data and high-resolution simulations, as alternatives to empirical parameterizations of essential, unresolved sub-grid scale processes related to turbulence, cloud formation and aerosol-cloud interaction. The tasks will include deriving and training data-driven models, coupling them to a large-scale climate model, evaluating the results against observations and traditionally parameterized models, and using the ML-enhanced model to estimate climate-relevant quantities like cloud radiative effects and forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with data scientists within the Swedish e-Science Research Centre, and contribute to development of methods with applicability also beyond climate science. The successful candidate will thereby develop their skills in atmospheric science and climate modelling, but also in data science and machine learning, and in communicating and collaborating within and across disciplines. Qualification requirements In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be fulfilled before admission to the programme. You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. The specific entry requirements additionally require a minimum of 90 higher education credits in any of the fields of meteorology, oceanography, physics or chemistry; and at least 15 higher education credits in mathematics as well as a degree project of at least 15 higher education credits. At least 60 higher education credits of these courses must be on the second-cycle level. In addition, proficiency in English language, equivalent to English B in Swedish high school, is required. The specific entry requirements may also be fulfilled by a person who has otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. General syllabus for doctoral studies in atmospheric science and oceanography. Selection The selection between candidates who meet the entry requirements will be made with reference to their ability to benefit from the training. However, the fact that an applicant is deemed able to transfer credits from previous training or professional experience may not alone give the applicant priority over other applicants in the selection process. Admission decisions are made in accordance with current delegation policies. The assessment criteria for admission to the postgraduate programme in atmospheric sciences and oceanography are familiarity with the theory and applications of the subject, subject knowledge relevant to the research project, the ability to express oneself orally and in writing, proficiency in English, analytical ability, creativity, initiative, independence and the ability to work collaboratively. The assessment of the applicant’s ability in these respects are based on the relevance and results of completed higher education courses, the quality and scope of the independent project, references, interviews and a personal statement from the applicant describing their expectations of, and intentions regarding, the programme. Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University. About the employment Starting date as per agreement. We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %). A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. Stockholm University strives to be a workplace free from discrimination and with equal opportunities for all. Contact For more information about the project, please contact professor Frida Bender, frida.bender@misu.su.se. For more information about the PhD programme, please contact the study director, Associate Professor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. For information about the recruitment process and terms of employment, please contact Head of Administration Sara Engström, sara.engstrom@misu.su.se. It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the job advertisement, and that it is submitted before the deadline. We kindly ask applicants to refrain from submitting AI-generated applications. The instructions for applicants are available at: How to apply for a position. indeed:34c148809c6ab21b.title: Industrial PhD Student in AI
indeed:34c148809c6ab21b.desc: INDUSTRIAL PHD STUDENT IN AI, Sundsvall Would you like to turn deep research into real impact in the factory, in our products and in the lives of the people who use them? At Permobil, we’re looking for game-changers to join us as we innovate for individuals and develop the world’s most advanced assistive solutions. At Permobil , the people who use our products come first. Our purpose is to create advanced assistive solutions that make the lives of adults and children living with disabilities more enriching. Our people are passionate about pushing the boundaries of technology to deliver innovations that improve lives. We are a sustainable and responsible business committed to continuous improvement, and our customers can trust us to provide market-leading solutions driven by insights-based clinical data. At Permobil in Sundsvall, we design and manufacture power wheelchairs and Panthera manual wheelchairs. Sundsvall is one of our largest and most modern sites, with production, R&D and clinical research side by side. About the role Permobil is now establishing an industrial PhD position in artificial intelligence , in close collaboration with Mid Sweden University (Mittuniversitetet) . The position is part of a four-year research project and gives you the chance to do doctoral research with one foot in academia and one foot in a real industrial environment. As Industrial PhD Student, you will be employed by Permobil in Sundsvall and admitted to the doctoral program at Mid Sweden University. You will work with the large amounts of operational and product data that our organization generates every day, and build deep knowledge about how AI can create value from it for our operations, our products and the people who use them. The research problem is deliberately open. Rather than a narrowly defined task, you get room to explore, ask deeper questions and shape the research direction together with your academic supervisors and your colleagues at Permobil. Key responsibilities: Plan and carry out doctoral research in applied AI, and complete your doctoral studies and thesis within the project period, Define and refine the research questions together with your supervisors as the project evolves, Work with real operational and product data from Permobil and turn it into new knowledge, Develop, test and evaluate AI methods, and show how they perform in a real industrial setting, Take part in doctoral courses and in the research environment at Mid Sweden University, Publish and present your results at conferences and in journals, in dialogue with Permobil and in line with the project agreement, Share insights and build competence with colleagues in Operations, R&D, Clinical and other functions at the site. Skills & Qualifications: Basic eligibility for doctoral studies: a degree at advanced level, or completed course requirements of at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits at advanced level, or equivalent knowledge acquired in Sweden or abroad, Specific eligibility: at least 90 credits in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science or closely related subjects, Good command of English, spoken and written. Swedish is an advantage, Experience in machine learning, data analysis or industrial applications of AI is an advantage, but not a requirement, Comfortable working in an international company and in a cross-functional context. Who Are You: You are curious, driven and goal-oriented, with a strong interest in turning research into practical value. You like to ask the deeper question rather than settle for the first answer, and you are comfortable moving between the data, the shop floor and the clinic. You create an environment where people feel safe to share ideas, challenge assumptions and learn together. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively with others and take ownership of your work. You share our belief in respect for people and continuous improvement. What we offer: A rare opportunity for both technical and personal development: doctoral education at Mid Sweden University combined with work on real industrial and product data at one of Permobil’s most modern sites. You get close support from supervisors at both the university and Permobil, and the chance to see your research put to use in a company with a clear purpose and a strong belief in the future. Application Process We will conduct selection continuously so send us your application today or before 20th of November at the latest! The position is based in Sundsvall, with a project period of four years. Permobil is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals. For more information about the position, please contact Mikael Boija, Senior Director Operational Excellence, mikael.boija@permobil.com For information about the recruitment process, please contact Zivile Mitkute, Talent Acquisition Partner, zivile.mitkute@permobil.com Please respect that we do not wish recruitment assistance or advertising, we decline calls from recruitment and advertising providers. More about Permobil Permobil founder Dr. Per Uddén believed that helping people achieve the greatest level of independence is a basic human right and, for over 50 years, Permobil has held fast to that belief. Permobil is a global leader in advanced rehabilitation technology, passionate about better understanding our users’ needs and improving their quality of life through state-of-the-art healthcare solutions. Today, those solutions include power wheelchairs, seating and positioning products, power assist, and manual wheelchairs. Permobil is part of Patricia Industries, a subsidiary of Investor AB, and is headquartered in Sweden. Permobil has 2 000 team members in 18 countries around the world. For more information regarding the company’s storied history and complete product line, visit permobil.com.

indeed:ecde12e4668e51b6.title: PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on mixed-phase cloud processes
indeed:ecde12e4668e51b6.desc: The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain. We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic. The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment. Read more about us here: the Department of Meteorology. Project description Clouds regulate how much sunlight reaches the Earth’s surface and how much thermal radiation escapes to space, which ultimately influences how hot or cold the planet is. How much each cloud cools or warms the Earth depends in part on its composition. Is it made up of liquid particles, ice particles, or both? How densely spaced and how large are these particles? The answers to these questions lie partially in the dynamics occurring within the cloud. Even clouds that look calm from the ground may generate motions strong enough to shake an airplane. These motions can form new cloud particles and combine or shatter existing ones. However, these motions are difficult to represent completely in computer models of the atmosphere and in laboratory experiments, and we have yet to understand their full impact. The PhD student will build this understanding using over 800 hours of wind and cloud particle measurements that have been recorded by specialized research aircraft during field campaigns run by government agencies in the US and Europe. Data have been collected over the midwestern US and the Caribbean, off the northwestern coast of Africa, between Australia and Antarctica, and in the vicinity of Svalbard. Quality-controlled versions of all data are already available, so analysis can begin at the project start.The PhD student will develop a detailed understanding of aircraft instrumentation through literature review and apply that expertise to the analysis of measurements from dozens of different aircraft-mounted instruments. All analysis will be done in Python. The scientific scope initially spans micrometer-scale cloud particles to the dynamical processes that affect clouds, including turbulent eddies and kilometer-scale atmospheric waves. Initial science questions are well defined and focus on identifying statistical relationships between cloud particle properties and cloud-scale dynamics, and investigating how these vary across cloud types and geographic regions. After the initial stage, the project is more open-ended. The PhD student may choose to focus on the same micrometer–kilometer scales, or to make connections between these scales and the regional or global climate. They may also choose to branch into atmospheric modelling and/or to use machine learning to model observed relationships between cloud dynamics and cloud particles. indeed:84fade98880e45d1.title: PhD student in Geophysics
indeed:84fade98880e45d1.desc: PhD student in Geophysics: Enhancing exploration drilling efficiency through integrated analyses rock formation and drilling data Are you interested in working with sustainable and responsible exploration drilling of critical raw materials, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University. The Department of Earth Sciences is Sweden's most comprehensive academic environment for research and education in geoscience. It offers a broad range of expertise that can contribute to solving important societal issues. Earth is a dynamic and constantly changing planet. To understand how this planet works, our researchers seek answers in the field, through laboratory experiments and advanced models. Our research and education cover a wide range of disciplines, including rocks and minerals, weather and climate, the evolution of life, natural disasters, wind power and energy, environmental and water engineering, and sustainable development. Our research combines natural sciences and technology with social sciences and is often interdisciplinary. More than 300 people from over 30 countries work at the department, both in Uppsala and at Campus Gotland. Our six research divisions: Geophysics • Air, Water and Landscape Science • Mineralogy, Petrology and Tectonics Natural Resources and Sustainable Development • Palaeobiology • Wind Energy For more information see: www.uu.se/earthsciences Geophysics is about "looking into" and understanding the Earth’s structure, its history and processes-based on measurements of the Earth’s physical properties. In geophysics we use quantitative physical methods to investigate the Earth and its environment. In addition, physical property measurements, rock mechanical field testing, scientific drilling and numerical modelling are employed to investigate the subsurface structures and processes. The Geophysics program currently runs several national and international projects and has a wealth of world-class infrastructures. It also leads the Smart Exploration Research Center (SERC) (www.smartexploration.se). SERC is funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research, with members from four Swedish universities, three mining companies, four technology companies, and one development company. The PhD project will be conducted in close collaboration with Epiroc, Nordic Iron and Lund University. In this PhD project, you will be enrolled as a PhD student at Uppsala University in close collaboration with Epiroc Rock Drills AB in Örebro. You will mainly be placed at Uppsala University, Uppsala. During shorter periods, you will also be placed at Epiroc Rock Drills AB in Örebro and participate if field work. Access to certain technology or data associated with industry partners within the project may be subject to applicable export control legislation and will be managed in accordance with current regulations. Duties The PhD candidate will conduct research within SERC, focusing on sustainable and responsible exploration of critical raw materials. The overarching aim of the PhD project is to develop a framework for integrating rock formation and drilling data to improve exploration drilling efficiency, thereby contribute to more sustainable and responsible exploration drilling. The project combines geoscience and drilling technology, with a focus on diamond core drilling in crystalline rock. The PhD candidate will develop advanced theoretical, technical and practical expertise in the technical and operational challenges of the drilling process, as well as geoscientific methods for subsurface characterization. The work involves data acquisition in connection with exploration drilling, borehole logging, in-situ testing, drill core analyses, and laboratory testing. Separate and integrated analyses of these datasets will be used to investigate potential relationships between rock formation properties, drilling data, and exploration drilling efficiency. The doctoral student will work in close collaboration with academic and industry research groups contributing to stronger collaboration and knowledge exchange between these communities. The PhD candidate is expected to combine theoretical and practical work, work both independently and collaboratively, spend parts of the project period with industry partners, and participate in field and laboratory work. Requirements To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must: hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in geophysics, geology, rock mechanics, drilling technology, physics, earth sciences or a similar field, or have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way. We are seeking a candidate with strong interests in exploration drilling in crystalline rocks and methods for subsurface characterisation, both in-situ and in the laboratory. Good oral and written proficiency in English is required. Additional qualifications Experience in various types of data acquisition and analysis, such as measurement while drilling (MWD), logging while drilling (LWD), borehole logging, rock stress measurements, drill core logging, and rock mechanic laboratory testing, is considered a merit. Experience in integrating and analysing different types of drilling data, rock formation data, or a combination of these is also considered a merit. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively is considered a merit. Proficiency in spoken and written Swedish is a merit, because communication in Swedish may be required during fieldwork and collaboration with industry partners. A driving license is a merit, as it may be required for fieldwork. indeed:ada7e4f49ab7e67f.title: PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on clouds in the atmospheric boundary layer
indeed:ada7e4f49ab7e67f.desc: The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain. We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic. The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment. Read more about us here: The Department of Meteorology. Project description The project focuses on understanding boundary layer cloud processes through Large Eddy Simulation (LES). A novel aspect is to represent cloud microphysics using a Lagrangian technique implemented in the turbulence solver Neko. The successful candidate will contribute to code development work and simulate cloudy marine boundary layers observed in detail over the Baltic Sea. The project, funded by the Swedish e-science Research Centre, is a collaboration between the Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University, KTH Center for Scientific Computing and KTH Engineering Mechanics. Qualification requirements In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be met by the deadline for applications. You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. The specific entry requirements comprise a minimum of 90 higher education credits in one of the subjects meteorology, oceanography, physics or chemistry, at least 15 higher education credits in mathematics, as well as an independent degree project of at least 15 higher education credits. Furthermore, English language proficiency equivalent to English 6/English Level 2 at upper secondary school is required. The specific entry requirements may also be met by those who have acquired equivalent knowledge through other means, either in Sweden or abroad. General syllabus for doctoral studies in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography. Selection Selection from among applicants who meet the entry requirements shall be made with regards to their ability to benefit from the programme. That fact alone that an applicant is assessed to be able to receive credits for previous educational or professional/vocational activities to be credited to the educational programme may not give the applicant priority over other applicants in the selection process. Decisions on admission are made in accordance with the applicable delegation regulations. The assessment criteria for admission to the postgraduate programme in atmospheric sciences and oceanography are familiarity with the theory and applications of the subject, subject knowledge relevant to the research project, the ability to express oneself orally and in writing, proficiency in English, analytical ability, creativity, initiative, independence and the ability to work collaboratively. The assessment of the applicant’s ability in these respects are based on the relevance and results of completed higher education courses, the quality and scope of the independent project, references, interviews and a personal statement from the applicant describing their expectations of, and intentions regarding, the programme. Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University. About the employment Starting date as per agreement. We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %). A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. Stockholm University strives to be a workplace free from discrimination and with equal opportunities for all. Contact For more information about the project, please contact Professor Gunilla Svensson, gunilla.svensson@misu.su.se. For more information about the PhD programme, please contact the study director, Professor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. For information about the recruitment process and terms of employment, please contact Head of Administration Sara Engström, sara.engstrom@misu.su.se. Application Apply for the PhD student position at Stockholm University's recruitment system. Attach a personal letter and CV as well as the attachments requested in the application form. It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the job advertisement, and that it is submitted before the deadline. We kindly ask applicants to refrain from submitting AI-generated applications. The instructions for applicants are available at: How to apply for a position. indeed:4a346af1a51b441b.title: PhD Student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on aerosol-cloud-climate interactions
indeed:4a346af1a51b441b.desc: Meteorologiska institutionen vid Stockholms universitet (MISU) bedriver forskning och utbildning som rör atmosfären, oceanen, och fysikaliskt-baserad klimatvetenskap. MISU erbjuder utbildningsprogram på kandidat-, master- och forskarnivå. Vår forskning söker svar på grundläggande frågor om atmosfärens och havens dynamiska, fysiska, kemiska, och biogeokemiska egenskaper av relevans för väder och klimat. Vi strävar efter en bred forskningsverksamhet inom vårt vetenskapliga område. Vi studerar frågor som sträcker sig från djuphavet till den övre atmosfären och från tropikerna till polerna. I vår forskning utnyttjar och utvecklar vi teori, statistiska metoder och numeriska modeller i nära samspel med observationer. Dessutom utvecklar och leder institutionen observationsbaserad forskning med stöd av satelliter, arktiska isbrytarexpeditioner och landbaserade instrument. MISU har cirka 60 anställda och ingår i en större forskningsmiljö som inkluderar Bolincentret för klimatforskning, Östersjöcentrum och Swedish e-Science Research Centre. Institutionen har stark internationell prägel, över hälften av medarbetarna har en bakgrund utanför Sverige och både svenska och engelska används som arbetsspråk. Vi välkomnar och värdesätter mångfald i vår arbetsmiljö. Mer information om oss finns att läsa på: Meteorologiska institutionen. Projektbeskrivning Samspelet mellan aerosolpartiklar och moln utgör en potentiellt betydande, men fortfarande mycket osäker, faktor i klimatförändringarna. Projektet syftar till att öka förståelsen för hur aerosolföroreningar påverkar moln som består av vattendroppar. Inom projektet ges möjlighet att undersöka detta genom att testa en ny teori som förutspår att aerosolföroreningar förstärker uppvindarna i konvektiva moln, vilket kan göra molnen tjockare och mer reflekterande. Det finns även möjlighet att studera trender i jordens strålningsbudget kopplade till aerosol-moln-interaktioner under satelliteran. Forskningsarbetet kan omfatta både numeriska simuleringar och analys av satellitdata. Behörighetskrav För att bli antagen till forskarutbildning krävs att den sökande har grundläggande och särskild behörighet. Behörigheten ska vara uppfylld senast sista ansökningsdag. Grundläggande behörighet har du, om du avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng (hp), varav minst 60 hp på avancerad nivå, eller på annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. För särskild behörighet krävs minst 90 hp i något av ämnena meteorologi, oceanografi, fysik eller kemi, minst 15 hp i matematik och ett självständigt arbete om minst 15 hp. Av detta skall minst 60 hp vara på avancerad nivå. Vidare krävs språkkunskaper i engelska motsvarande engelska B på gymnasiet. Allmän studieplan för studier på forskarnivå i atmosfärsvetenskap och oceanografi. Urval Urval bland de sökande som uppfyller behörighetskraven ska göras med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig utbildningen. Enbart det förhållandet att en sökande bedöms kunna få tidigare utbildning eller yrkesverksamhet tillgodoräknad för utbildningen får inte vid urval ge sökanden företräde framför andra sökande. Beslut om antagning fattas enligt gällande delegationsordning. Vid bedömningen tas hänsyn till förtrogenhet och skicklighet inom ämnet, förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på engelska, analytisk förmåga, kreativitet, initiativförmåga och självständighet, och samarbetsförmåga. Till grund för bedömningen ligger tidigare studiers relevans, betyg på genomgångna högskolekurser (särskilt de på avancerad nivå), kvalitet och omfattning på det självständiga arbetet, referenser, intervjuer samt skriftlig avsiktsförklaring. Antagningsordning för utbildning på forskarnivå vid Stockholms universitet. Om anställningen Tillträde den 1 januari 2027 eller enligt överenskommelse. Vi erbjuder en tidsbegränsad anställning som doktorand enligt 5 kap. högskoleförordningen (1993:100). Anställningstiden får inte vara längre än vad som motsvarar utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid under fyra år. Som doktorand ska du främst ägna dig åt din egen utbildning på forskarnivå, men i anställningen kan arbete med utbildning, forskning och administration ingå i begränsad omfattning (högst 20 %). En ny anställning som doktorand gäller för högst ett år, anställningen förnyas därefter med högst två år i taget. Stockholms universitet värnar om att vara en arbetsplats som är fri från diskriminering och ger lika rättigheter och möjligheter för alla. Kontakt För mer information om projektet, kontakta biträdande lektor Casey Wall, casey.wall@misu.su.se. För information om forskarutbildningen, kontakta studierektor, professor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. Upplysningar om rekryteringsprocessen och anställningsvillkor lämnas av administrativ chef, Sara Engström sara.engstrom@misu.su.se. Ansökan Du söker doktorandplatsen via Stockholms universitets rekryteringssystem. Bifoga personligt brev och CV samt de bilagor som efterfrågas i ansökningsformuläret. Du som sökande ansvarar för att ansökan är komplett i enlighet med annonsen och att den är universitetet tillhanda senast sista ansökningsdag. Vi ber att du som sökande avstår från att skicka in en AI-genererad ansökan. Anvisningar för sökande finns på webbsidan: att söka en anställning. Stockholm University contributes to the development of sustainable democratic society through knowledge, enlightenment and the pursuit of truth. indeed:5e26872f4b0558c7.title: PhD position in biomineralization of digitally fabricated granular materials
indeed:5e26872f4b0558c7.desc: Mission We are offering a challenging position as a full-time (100%) PhD Student in the Laloui Group at EPFL inLausanne. The group brings expertise in geomaterials and their mechanical behaviour to research at theinterface of material science and engineering applications. You will work on the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)-funded project “DFabuLis: Digital FabricationUsing Living Systems”, conducted in collaboration between Dr. Dimitrios Terzis, Senior Scientist in the LalouiGroup at EPFL, and co-PI Prof. Benjamin Dillenburger of the Chair of Digital Building Technologies at ETHZurich. The project investigates how biologically driven mineralization can transform demolition and excavationmaterials into materials suitable for digital fabrication under ambient conditions. Digital fabrication methods, including extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying, offer opportunities to controlmaterial placement and curing, create complex geometries and reduce material consumption. Integratingbiomineralization into pumpable, extrudable and sprayable granular materials remains largely unexplored. ThisPhD will investigate the coupled biogeochemical, rheological and mechanical mechanisms governing particledeposition, mineral precipitation and hardening. Main duties and responsibilities As a PhD Student, you will be expected to: Take full responsibility for your dissertation and the progress of your research. Conduct research in close collaboration with project partners at EPFL and ETH Zurich and, whereapplicable, industry partners. Design and execute experiments, and analyze and interpret experimental results. Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present your findings at internationalconferences. Participate in teaching and supervise student projects. More specifically, within this project, you will: Investigate the rheology and processability of granular materials, including yield stress, plastic viscosity,thixotropy, water content, ageing and particle interactions. Study microbial activity and biologically driven mineral precipitation, and determine how evolving mineralphases affect mechanical hardening and material performance. Characterize the coupling between biogeochemical reactions, rheological properties and mechanicalbehaviour over space and time. Connect experimental findings to extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying in collaboration with thedigital fabrication team at ETH Zurich. Profile An MSc degree in Civil Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering or aclosely related discipline. A background in mechanics and the strength of solid materials, or materials science applied to the builtenvironment, is particularly welcome. Experience in rheology, granular or cementitious materials, experimental mechanics, materialcharacterization, geomechanics, mineralogy, or organic and inorganic chemistry is an advantage.Expertise across all these fields is neither expected nor required. Interest in experimental and interdisciplinary research, and in translating fundamental physical andchemical understanding into new construction technologies. Good communication skills and willingness to work as part of a team across disciplines and institutions. Enthusiasm, scientific curiosity, eagerness to learn, good organizational skills and rigor in experimentalwork. A high level of motivation for academic research. Fluency in English is essential. indeed:965d2ab12942936f.title: SNSF-funded PhD position in lipid metabolism
indeed:965d2ab12942936f.desc: Dysregulation of lipid metabolism plays a key role in development and progression of metabolic disorders including obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). We are seeking a highly motivated and talented PhD candidate to join our multidisciplinary research team to investigate underlying mechanism associated to dysregulation of lipid metabolism in MASLD. What you can expect This research will provide multi-disciplinary training as require a combination of complementary approaches, including molecular biology, biochemistry, analytical chemistry and computational biology Your Profile Master's degree or equivalent in biochemistry, system biology or analytical chemistry Experience working with mass spectrometry is essential and knowledge of working with mass spectrometry imaging in plus Highly organized and capable of working both independently and within the team Good interpersonal and communication skills as well as fluency in both spoken and written English is essential What we offer A supporting and state-of-the-art research environment to develop scientifically and professionally The opportunity to work and get training on a multi-disciplinary research project; with pre-clinical models as well as clinical studies The position is fully-funded by Swiss National Science Foundation and available from November 2026 (or upon agreement) Please send your CV, motivation letter, reference letter with name and contact of two referees. indeed:8db930dffab9e8e2.title: PhD Position SNSF Project"Beyond the Gig Economy:Exploring the New Frontiers of Algorithmic Control"
indeed:8db930dffab9e8e2.desc: Introduction UNIL is a leading international teaching and research institution, with over 5,000 employees and 17,000 students split between its Dorigny campus, CHUV and Epalinges. As an employer, UNIL encourages excellence, individual recognition and responsibility. unil.ch/work Presentation The Swiss Graduate School of Public Administration (IDHEAP) at the University of Lausanne invites applications for a PhD position in the "Information Management" research unit headed by Prof. Tobias Mettler. IDHEAP is the largest university institute in Switzerland dedicated entirely and exclusively to the public sector. We offer excellent research support in a dynamic public policy and public administration research community and are committed to promoting the careers of young scholars. Are you interested in the future of AI and the algorithmic state? Are you enthusiastic about developing research at the crossroads between Public Management and Information Systems? Join our research team in the project “Beyond the Gig Economy: Exploring the New Frontiers of Algorithmic Control”. The project examines the implications and different design alternatives of algorithms gradually replacing human decision-making. A core problem we will explore is how social norms can be encoded into algorithmic control while enabling meaningful exception handling. The ideal candidate is therefore sensitive to technical and social questions and interested in conducting challenging empirical work in a fast-moving environment. Job information Expected start date in position : November 1, 2026 / to be agreed Contract length : 1 year, renewable 2 x, maximum 4 years Activity rate : 100% Workplace : Lausanne, IDHEAP building Your responsibilities Their tasks will involve field research, design research, and publication in the field of Information Systems and related. They will spend between 10% and 20% of their time on administrative tasks. linkedin:4476472225.desc: INDUSTRIAL PHD STUDENT IN AI, Sundsvall Would you like to turn deep research into real impact in the factory, in our products and in the lives of the people who use them? At Permobil, we’re looking for game-changers to join us as we innovate for individuals and develop the world’s most advanced assistive solutions. At Permobil , the people who use our products come first. Our purpose is to create advanced assistive solutions that make the lives of adults and children living with disabilities more enriching. Our people are passionate about pushing the boundaries of technology to deliver innovations that improve lives. We are a sustainable and responsible business committed to continuous improvement, and our customers can trust us to provide market-leading solutions driven by insights-based clinical data. At Permobil in Sundsvall, we design and manufacture power wheelchairs and Panthera manual wheelchairs. Sundsvall is one of our largest and most modern sites, with production, R&D and clinical research side by side. About The Role Permobil is now establishing an industrial PhD position in artificial intelligence , in close collaboration with Mid Sweden University (Mittuniversitetet) . The position is part of a four-year research project and gives you the chance to do doctoral research with one foot in academia and one foot in a real industrial environment. As Industrial PhD Student, you will be employed by Permobil in Sundsvall and admitted to the doctoral program at Mid Sweden University. You will work with the large amounts of operational and product data that our organization generates every day, and build deep knowledge about how AI can create value from it for our operations, our products and the people who use them. The research problem is deliberately open. Rather than a narrowly defined task, you get room to explore, ask deeper questions and shape the research direction together with your academic supervisors and your colleagues at Permobil. Key Responsibilities Plan and carry out doctoral research in applied AI, and complete your doctoral studies and thesis within the project period, Define and refine the research questions together with your supervisors as the project evolves, Work with real operational and product data from Permobil and turn it into new knowledge, Develop, test and evaluate AI methods, and show how they perform in a real industrial setting, Take part in doctoral courses and in the research environment at Mid Sweden University, Publish and present your results at conferences and in journals, in dialogue with Permobil and in line with the project agreement, Share insights and build competence with colleagues in Operations, R&D, Clinical and other functions at the site. Skills & Qualifications Basic eligibility for doctoral studies: a degree at advanced level, or completed course requirements of at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits at advanced level, or equivalent knowledge acquired in Sweden or abroad, Specific eligibility: at least 90 credits in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science or closely related subjects, Good command of English, spoken and written. Swedish is an advantage, Experience in machine learning, data analysis or industrial applications of AI is an advantage, but not a requirement, Comfortable working in an international company and in a cross-functional context. Who Are You You are curious, driven and goal-oriented, with a strong interest in turning research into practical value. You like to ask the deeper question rather than settle for the first answer, and you are comfortable moving between the data, the shop floor and the clinic. You create an environment where people feel safe to share ideas, challenge assumptions and learn together. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively with others and take ownership of your work. You share our belief in respect for people and continuous improvement. What We Offer A rare opportunity for both technical and personal development: doctoral education at Mid Sweden University combined with work on real industrial and product data at one of Permobil’s most modern sites. You get close support from supervisors at both the university and Permobil, and the chance to see your research put to use in a company with a clear purpose and a strong belief in the future. Application Process We will conduct selection continuously so send us your application today or before 20th of November at the latest! The position is based in Sundsvall, with a project period of four years. Permobil is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals. For more information about the position, please contact Mikael Boija, Senior Director Operational Excellence, mikael.boija@permobil.com For information about the recruitment process, please contact Zivile Mitkute, Talent Acquisition Partner, zivile.mitkute@permobil.com Please respect that we do not wish recruitment assistance or advertising, we decline calls from recruitment and advertising providers. More About Permobil Permobil founder Dr. Per Uddén believed that helping people achieve the greatest level of independence is a basic human right and, for over 50 years, Permobil has held fast to that belief. Permobil is a global leader in advanced rehabilitation technology, passionate about better understanding our users’ needs and improving their quality of life through state-of-the-art healthcare solutions. Permobil is part of Patricia Industries, a subsidiary of Investor AB, and is headquartered in Sweden. Permobil has 2 000 team members in 18 countries around the world. linkedin:4479026574.title: PhD Scholarship in Machine Learning for Non-Stationary and Non-Static Nano-Tomography - DTU Compute
linkedin:4479026574.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
linkedin:4479026574.desc: Job Description Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial resolution, even minute positioning errors, mechanical drift, and sample deformations become sources of image degradation. The central challenge is to reconstruct accurate 3D and 4D representations of samples while accounting for positional uncertainties during image acquisition and changes in sample shape over time. The project will bring together neural representations, inverse problems, geometric modeling, and computational imaging to address fundamental challenges in nano-tomography. Rather than correcting acquisition errors and sample deformations as separate preprocessing steps, you will investigate how to model and estimate the sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation jointly from the measured data. The position is based at DTU Compute and conducted in close collaboration with EPFL and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland, one of the leading centers for synchrotron X-ray imaging. As a PhD student, you will work in an international research environment spanning DTU, EPFL, and PSI, combining expertise in both machine learning and computational imaging with access to experimental data and advanced imaging facilities. Research visits to Switzerland are planned as part of the project. Responsibilities Develop novel machine learning and deep learning methods for X-ray nano-tomography, which jointly reconstruct sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation fields from inconsistent projection data. Investigate neural field representations for 3D and 4D imaging, including models that capture changes in sample geometry over time, and explore hybrid approaches combining learning-based methods with physical models of image formation and tomographic reconstruction. Validate and evaluate the developed methods using experimental nano-tomography data, initially focusing on integrated circuits. Collaborate with researchers at DTU, PSI, and EPFL, and participate in international research visits and scientific activities. Publish research results in leading journals and conferences in machine learning, computer vision, and computational imaging. Contribute to research-based teaching and supervision of MSc and BSc student projects. Participate in activities within the Center for Quantification of Imaging Data from MAX IV (QIM), including workshops, training courses, and interdisciplinary research collaborations. Qualifications You are curious and motivated by developing new machine learning methods to solve challenging problems in computational imaging. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning is particularly important. We welcome candidates from computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, and related disciplines who are interested in combining modern learning methods with mathematical modeling and real-world experimental data. The candidate should be able to work independently, contribute effectively to an interdisciplinary research team, and communicate scientific ideas clearly in written and spoken English. To succeed in this position, you are expected to have: A master's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning, including experience developing, implementing, or evaluating learning-based models. Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, and familiarity with relevant machine learning frameworks. A solid understanding of mathematical modeling, optimization, or numerical methods. Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: Neural representations, implicit neural fields, or other coordinate-based representations. Computer vision, 3D vision, geometric modeling, or structure-from-motion. Inverse problems, image reconstruction, or physics-informed machine learning. Image registration, motion estimation, or deformable modeling. Image processing, image analysis, or tomographic reconstruction. Knowledge of X-ray imaging and tomography is beneficial but not required. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation. At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 March 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Hans Martin Kjer, hmkj@dtu.dk . You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 16 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time) . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file . The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. DTU Compute DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk . DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.
