linkedin:4478406768.title: Research Scientist, Doctoral Researcher, tree breeding
linkedin:4478406768.desc: We are looking for a doctoral researcher for a project "Thousand Ways to Die - evolutionary and molecular background of excessive early developmental mortality in Scots pine” realized jointly by the University of Helsinki and Luke. Job description The Doctoral Researcher will carry out doctoral research in accordance with the project’s research plan. The aim is to investigate the reproductive system of Scots pine and the high mortality of seed embryos during early developmental stages. The main research topics are inbreeding depression and possible self-incompatibility mechanisms affecting embryo viability. We will use advanced methods, such as spatial transcriptomics, to investigate gene expression in seeds under different conditions and at different developmental stages. We will also compare natural embryo development with somatic embryogenesis, as well as the factors affecting these. The aim is to understand how mutation, purifying selection and adaptive evolution influence embryo viability, which may improve seed quality and enhance forest regeneration. The Doctoral Researcher’s role in the project’s sub-studies will be determined partly by the person's skills and interests, as the project will employ also Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Helsinki. The project is being carried out jointly by the University of Helsinki and the Natural Resources Institute Finland. The Postdoctoral Researcher will be employed by Luke, while supervision related to the doctoral degree will be provided by the University of Helsinki (Professor Pyhäjärvi, https://www.helsinki.fi/en/researchgroups/forest-genomics). The selected person will apply separately to the university’s doctoral programme. The position requires regular on-site presence and participation in field and laboratory work. Field trials will be conducted at Haapastensyrjä in Loppi and at seed orchards, while laboratory work will take place in Helsinki and, for somatic embryogenesis, at Savonlinna. Our expectations of the applicant We expect applicants to hold a Master’s degree in a relevant field (for example, agriculture and forestry, biology or genetics). The position requires knowhow and/or an interest in evolutionary biology and molecular genetics, as well as laboratory skills. Experience with molecular biology methods, microscopy and plant tissue culture is an advantage. Bioinformatics and computational skills are also considered an asset. Due to the collaborative nature of the project, strong teamwork and communication skills are essential. Excellent written and spoken English is required. The position also requires the ability to participate in field measurements and sampling; therefore, a category AB driving licence is an advantage. Additional information Tuija Aronen Group Manager, Luke +358 29 532 4233 tuija.aronen@luke.fi Tanja Pyhäjärvi Professor, University of Helsinki +358 29 415 7976 tanja.pyhajarvi@helsinki.fi Apply by 27.10.2026 at 16.00 (4 pm EET)

linkedin:4472090457.title: PhD Position Continuum Two-Phase Flow Modelling of Piping in Dikes
linkedin:4472090457.desc: Develop advanced models to understand and predict piping and internal erosion in dikes. As a PhD researcher at TU Delft, you will connect fundamental fluid–soil interaction physics with computational modelling to contribute to safer flood defences. Job Description Internal erosion and piping are among the main failure mechanisms of clay–sand layered dikes and remain important challenges in flood risk management. Reliable numerical models can improve our understanding of how piping develops and help engineers assess and design safer, more reliable flood defence systems. In this PhD project, you will contribute to this challenge by advancing the modelling of particle transport and fluid–soil interaction in dikes. A key scientific challenge is to represent the complex interaction between soil particles and flowing water across different spatial and temporal scales, while keeping the models computationally efficient. The research builds on an Eulerian two-phase modelling approach previously applied to backward erosion piping. You will investigate how this approach can be further developed to capture the physical processes that govern pipe formation and progression, while connecting detailed modelling with larger-scale analyses. The goal of the project is to develop a robust and computationally efficient modelling framework that improves the prediction of piping in layered dikes. Your research will contribute to a better understanding of internal erosion and support the development of safer flood defence systems and more reliable flood risk assessments. Your Responsibilities As a PhD researcher, you will: Develop continuum-based two-phase models to predict internal erosion and pipe progression in clay-sand layered dikes. Derive constitutive modelling approaches from high-fidelity DNS-DEM data generated within the broader project consortium. Capture the multi-scale nature of pipe formation while maintaining computational efficiency, including the exploration of adaptive mesh refinement strategies. Disseminate research outcomes through scientific publications, conference presentations, and collaboration with researchers from relevant disciplines. Your work environment You will join the Offshore and Dredging Engineering group within the department of Maritime and Transport Technology of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. You will receive supervision and guidance while having the freedom to shape and develop your research. You will have access to well-equipped facilities, including: The hydraulic circuit. You will work in an open and collaborative environment where interdisciplinary teamwork, curiosity and scientific excellence are valued. The group works closely across fluid mechanics, soil mechanics, hydraulic engineering and ocean engineering, using various computational and experimental techniques, sharing knowledge and expertise to develop innovative solutions with meaningful societal impact. Please see our work for more information: Offshore and Dredging Engineering. Job Requirements You are highly motivated to translate fundamental flow and erosion physics into practically relevant scales through two-phase flow modelling. You are well organised, manage your time effectively and take initiative in a multidisciplinary research environment. You are results-oriented and enjoy working with researchers from different disciplines. Furthermore, you meet the following requirements: You have an MSc degree in a relevant field (Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Applied Physics, Process Technology, Civil Engineering or a closely related discipline) You have received training in multiphase flow physics, numerical methods, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), ideally complemented by application in your MSc thesis, research projects, or internships. Have excellent communication skills and command of English. Have affinity with teaching and guiding MSc students. Familiarity with Euler–Euler multiphase flow modelling and/or automatic mesh adaptation techniques is considered an advantage. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context. At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. We believe this makes our work more innovative, the TU Delft community more vibrant and the world more just. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration. Challenge. Change. Impact! Faculty Mechanical Engineering Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. linkedin:4479244418.title: Industrial PhD student: Kinetic modelling of catalytic hydrogen oxidation for hydrogen engines
linkedin:4479244418.desc: Industrial PhD student: Kinetic modelling of catalytic hydrogen oxidation for hydrogen engines TRATON is a group of strong brands with a shared mission: transforming transportation together to create the future of sustainable transport solutions. Within TRATON, we include MAN, Scania, Volkswagen Truck & Bus, and International. As part of a global team of industry experts, you get to think bigger, experience more, and reach further. Together, we have the power to transform transportation - Let´s make a difference together. Find out more: www.traton.com Our values – customer first, respect, team spirit, responsibility, and elimination of waste – are at the heart of everything we do. Introduction Join us as an industrial PhD student and contribute to the development of future hydrogen-fuelled heavy-duty vehicles by developing predictive kinetic models for catalytic hydrogen combustion. The research will bridge fundamental catalysis, experimental studies and engine-level simulations, with the long-term aim of enabling efficient hydrogen powertrains with ultra low emissions. Hydrogen internal combustion engines (H₂-ICE) with high-pressure direct injection offer high efficiency and power density but face challenges related to cold start and the need of carbon-based pilot fuels for ignition. Catalytic hydrogen oxidation over noble metals such as platinum could improve cold-start performance and enable hydrogen-only ignition concepts. Role Summary This role is a part of TRATON Group R&D, located in Södertälje, Sweden. The main focus of this Industrial PhD is the development and validation of kinetic models for hydrogen oxidation over noble-metal catalysts across a broad range of operating conditions and applications, including cold-start and in-cylinder conditions. You will also work closely with other PhD students and researchers to design and conduct relevant experimental studies supporting kinetic model development and validation, providing opportunities for hands-on experimental work in catalysis. The position will be part of PtHICE – Innovative ways to use platinum for zero emission hydrogen vehicles, a joint research project involving TRATON, Chalmers University of Technology, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Christian-Albrechts-University of Kiel, AVL List GmbH and Johnson Matthey. You will be employed by TRATON AB and affiliated with the Division of Chemical Engineering at Chalmers University of Technology, and work in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners. Job Responsibilities The work will involve all parts of a research project, from developing scientific hypotheses and analysing experimental data to kinetic model development, validation and application. Your main responsibilities will include: Develop and validate kinetic models for catalytic hydrogen oxidation based on experimental data, and apply them in 1D and 3D simulations under engine-relevant conditions, including cold start and catalytic-assisted hydrogen ignition. Collaborate with academic and industrial partners across experiments and modelling, and communicate research results through scientific publications and international conferences. Who You Are We welcome applicants from all backgrounds – your unique experience and perspectives is valuable to us. You should have an M.Sc. degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Engineering Physics, Applied Physics, or a related field, preferably with a background or strong interest in catalysis, chemical kinetics, reaction engineering or numerical modelling. You should be interested in understanding physical and chemical phenomena from experimental data and translating this knowledge into mathematical and numerical models. As a person, you are curious, energetic and collaborative, with a proactive mindset and a strong interest in learning and exploring new ideas. You enjoy working in a multidisciplinary team and contributing to a positive research environment. You should have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Swedish language skills are considered a merit but are not required. TRATON Offers We offer a dynamic and engaging workplace where collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement are part of everyday life. You will be part of a strong team environment that encourages knowledge sharing and close cooperation across functions. With a structured development plan and a wide range of training opportunities, TRATON supports your professional growth both locally and internationally. Benefits include access to our health center in mapor a wellness allowance, bonus, flexible working hours, and company car leasing. The group also arranges events for employees and their families, and for those living in Stockholm. We offer an inspiring and inclusive workplace with respect for the individual and great opportunities to shape your work and your future. linkedin:4479283647.desc: Job Description How can the distribution grid be made more resilient? You have the opportunity to investigate how island operation of the distribution grid can mitigate severe incidents in the power system. Your project will be one of three PhDs in collaboration with DTU Space and DTU Electro. Your project will focus on how improved situational awareness can improve supply of prioritized loads by operating of parts of the distribution grid in island mode during interruptions. Responsibilities And Qualifications You will in the PhD project develop methods for enhancing the ability of microgrids and distribution systems to dynamically transition to and operate as islanded grids that are controlled robustly in a no-single-point-of-failure architecture. The research will investigate how conventional grid measurements can be combined with non-traditional information sources, including information from distributed energy resources or physical surveillance data to maintain a continuously updated understanding of system state, resource availability, and network topology. Operating strategies that can accommodate continuously changing resource situations and stability threats will be devised. To afford manageability of this ever-changing system situation and communication with grid operators and non-grid emergency procedures, a self-representing explainable data model for the coordination with grid operators and other entities. The outcomes will contribute to the development of resilient distribution system operation concepts and intelligent energy management systems capable of supporting secure islanded operation, faster system recovery, and improved security of electricity supply. You will be part of a dynamic working environment that will support the growth of your personal and academic skills. You will be part of an international group and will have the opportunity to collaborate with industry and international research groups. You will be involved in our teaching and assist in co-supervision of MSc and BSc students. A successful candidate will have a solid background in: Power system engineering and optimization Data science Programming tools such as Python Power system simulation such as PandaPower, PowerFactory Excellent use of English language Strong ability to communicate scientific results orally and through scientific publications in international journals You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . The assessment of applications will be ongoing and will start before the application deadline. We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. The desired start date is 1 January 2027 depending on academic approval. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. indeed:e89ae10894a8d965.desc: The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field. Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The Electrical Engineering department takes its inspiration from contacts with high-tech industry in the direct surrounding region and beyond. The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed. Introduction Are you passionate about building an entanglement-based routing in quantum optical networks? Join us to develop an innovative entanglement-based routing architecture and protocol, and set up an experimental testbed to route entangled photons in the presence of classical telecom traffic in multi-node quantum optical fiber networks. Job Description Efficient distribution and routing of entanglement are indispensable for quantum‑secure communication (e.g., advanced QKD networks), distributed quantum computing, quantum‑secure enterprise connectivity and quantum teleportation services across metropolitan or regional distances. However, unique features of quantum information, such as non-amplification, no-cloning, or measurement without altering the quantum states, make it difficult to re-use the architecture and protocols of classical telecom networks for quantum communication and networking. In contrast to classical optical signals, quantum states are extremely fragile and degrade rapidly due to loss, noise, and decoherence, especially over long distances. As a result, conventional telecom solutions such as optical amplification, regeneration, and routing cannot be directly applied to quantum networks. Nevertheless, recent advances in quantum state generation and measurement have opened new opportunities for developing quantum network architectures and protocols for routing and teleportation, a critical enabler for quantum networks. In this PhD project, you will set up an experimental testbed for a multi-node quantum optical fiber network that enables entanglement generation and detection, frequency conversion, and entanglement routing of quantum-classical packets between nodes connected by optical switches. Additionally, you will investigate the coexistence of classical telecom traffic and quantum signals and the effects of impairments such as noise and crosstalk. The project will combine theoretical and simulation studies and validate them with experimental studies. The project will leverage KPN’s expertise to address real‑world constraints—including scalability, interoperability, reliability, and manageability—while developing the telecom‑grade quantum networks. The PhD position is fully funded by our industry partner (KPN) in Smart Optical Networks Lab (SONL) of the Electro-Optical Communication group. The research activity of SONL covers a wide range of topics, including network design and software control, reconfigurable interconnects for telecom, datacenters, AI clusters, and quantum networks, down to heterogeneous photonic integrated circuits and systems for enabling low-latency, fast network reconfiguration in real systems. Additionally, we focus on innovative solutions for switching and routing in secure quantum-optical networks. The ECO group covers a wide range of topics from the Photonic layer to the Application layer of the communication system, and we also play a key role in the Casimir Institute at TU/e, and within the PhotonDelta and QuantumDelta growth fund program. indeed:87ac11e739b56f5c.title: Doctoral student in Risk and Safety of Heterogeneous Swarm Systems
indeed:87ac11e739b56f5c.desc: Lund University was founded in 1666 and is repeatedly ranked among the world’s top universities. The University has around 46 000 students and 8 500 staff based in Lund, Helsingborg and Malmö. We are united in our efforts to understand, explain and improve our world and the human condition. Lund University welcomes applicants with diverse backgrounds and experiences. We regard equality, equal opportunities and diversity as a strength and an asset. Description of the workplace The Department of Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences strives to be a leading center for aeronautics research, development, and education. The department operates a certified commercial flight school (ATO) and an authorized drone school (ADS) under the name of Lund University School of Aviation, Sweden's only state-run civilian flight school. The department’s research facilities are based at Campus Ljungbyhed, providing a unique setting that integrates research, development, and education with access to airport infrastructure, including a runway system and controlled airspace. We seek to understand, innovate, and advance aviation through collaborative efforts, making it more accessible, sustainable, and safe in the digital age. The research emphasizes three primary areas: sustainable aviation, unmanned aviation, and aviation safety, with safety being a central theme across all initiatives. This doctoral student position is at the Department of Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences and will work at the intersection between unmanned aviation and aviation safety, as part of the Center for Heterogeneous Adaptive Swarm Systems (CHASS) funded by Stiftelsen för Strategisk Forskning* (SSF). CHASS includes three dual-use relevant large industrial partners (Saab, Sectra Communications and BAE Systems Hägglunds) and societal participation from the Swedish Defence Research Institute (FOI), the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency (MCF) and the Swedish Civil Aviation Administration (LFV). The duty station is Ljungbyhed. More about SSF Being a doctoral student As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree. More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se Subject and project description The research area is Risk and Safety of heterogeneous swarm systems. The multi-disciplinary center for heterogeneous adaptive swarm systems, CHASS, is a national effort funded by the Swedish Strategic Research Foundation (SSF) to bring together leading researchers in AI, autonomous systems, robotics, and swarm intelligence to develop novel solutions for autonomous heterogeneous swarm systems for the benefit of Swedish industry and society. The vision is to make Sweden a leader in intelligent, adaptive, and trustworthy swarm systems by pioneering autonomous heterogeneous collectives of space, aerial, ground, surface, and underwater platforms that can operate as a unified intelligent entity with minimal human intervention. The research program focuses on six key themes: Drone Design, Adaptation, & Production; Perception, Sensing, & Communication; Autonomy, Localization, Mapping & Navigation; Coordination, Self-Governance, & Self-Improvement; Human Swarm Interaction; and Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects. CHASS is led by Linköping University and besides Lund University also includes Örebro University, each with CHASS-affiliated doctoral students, as well as a large number of industry and government stakeholders, providing a stimulating research environment. CHASS will drive world-class research in autonomous swarm systems through a strong, stimulating, and well-connected international research environment. Research outcomes will be validated in real-world scenarios with industry and public-sector partners. CHASS will also serve as a national hub for autonomous swarm systems, promoting education, knowledge sharing, innovation, and policy development. The doctoral student position in this announcement will work within the theme of Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects. It develops and evaluates risk assessment and safety management methodologies (for the phases before, during, and after operations) for heterogeneous swarms, including frameworks for risk assessment, adaptive capacity and control, and accountability and responsibility. The position will include interaction with other doctoral students and researchers within this theme, as well as the Human Swarm Interaction theme and the other technological development themes. Work duties You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences. The work duties include: You will work in a multi-disciplinary research project focused on socio-technical aspects of control, risk, and safety of heterogeneous swarms resilience. You will likely combine qualitative (e.g. interviews) and quantitative (e.g. modelling, statistics) methods. You will travel in Sweden and abroad to interact with fellow researchers to collaborate and present research findings at scientific conferences. As parts of the research may be conducted in collaboration with defence-related organisations, a security screening will be carried out if applicable. The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours). Qualifications To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below. Admission requirements A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Risk and Safety (TEVBRF11) if the applicant has: at least 90 credits in subjects of relevance to the field, including at least 60 second cycle credits, or a BSc in Fire Protection Engineering amounting to 210 credits. Additional requirements In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: good knowledge in risk, system safety, design, and governance of socio-technical systems in complex settings, good ability to take initiative and solve research challenges with drive, creativity, and persistence, good ability to work in a structured way in a collaborative and inter-disciplinary environment, good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems, good written and oral communication skills, good ability to cooperate with other researchers and practitioners, very good knowledge of English, spoken and written. Other qualifications For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as meriting qualifications: knowledge of aeronautical engineering, human-computer interaction, human factors engineering, cognitive science, human control of AI, unmanned aviation, critical infrastructure resilience, interaction design, industrial design engineering, and related disciplines, skills and experience in modelling and simulation, skills and experience in relevant software and programming environments, such as Matlab, Python, C++, UAS communication protocols (MAVLink), ROS2, git. skills and experience in statistical analysis and quantitative research methods, skills and experience relating to relevant qualitative research methods, such as interviews, driving licence B, practical experience of operations in manned or unmanned aviation. Consideration will also be given to how the applicant, through his or her experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme. We offer Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. More about working at Lund University on lu.se About the employment The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting on 1 January 2027 or as agreed. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§. More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages Other The recruitment process will include interviews and your reflections on work samples. Interviews will be conducted either online or in person at Lund university. How to apply Applications shall be written in English and include: CV and a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the doctoral programme/employment and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background. Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral programme project. Other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.) We welcome your application. About the Faculty of Engineering LTH is Lund University’s Faculty of Engineering. At LTH we educate people, build knowledge for the future and work hard for the development of society. We create space for brilliant research and inspire creative advancements in technology, architecture and design. We have nearly 12,000 students. Every year, our researchers – many of whom work in world-leading profile areas – publish around 100 theses and 2 000 scientific findings. In addition, a number of research results and degree projects are transformed into innovations. Together we explore and create – to benefit the world. We kindly decline all sales and marketing contacts. linkedin:4434741253.title: PhD Researcher: AI-driven Employee-Customer Relationship Management in the Service Sector
linkedin:4434741253.desc: Please note that Dutch at the B2 level is required for this vacancy. Do you have a passion for business-relevant research and the ambition to obtain your PhD on the hot topic of creating business value with data analytics and AI? Do you have the right academic background and are you ready to start this 4-year journey in our open, international and collegial environment? Let’s meet! PhD Researcher: AI-driven Employee-Customer Relationship Management in the Service Sector Vlerick Business School is an innovative, top-ranked and sustainable international business school in the heart of Europe. Our purpose is to transform people for a better world! We want being at Vlerick to be a transformative experience where you discover the knowledge, mindset and confidence you need to take your next leap – and become the entrepreneurial leader our world needs. Glowi is a dynamic group offering innovative services across multiple domains to make life easier for individuals and businesses. Its business units include Het Poetsbureau & Easy Life (Glowi Home); Friends of Cartel (Marketing Solutions), Glowi Jobs and Motmans & Partners (HR Solutions). Together, they combine expertise and passion to create solutions that truly make a difference. As a Belgian company, Glowi is at the forefront of innovation in the cleaning services sector, combining operational excellence with data-driven insights to transform how clients and cleaners connect. With a strong focus on decentralised communication, performance tracking, and human-centric consultancy, Glowi empowers its teams to deliver measurable impact across cleaner acquisition, client retention, and administrative efficiency. The company’s commitment to continuous improvement and smart technology integration makes it a catalyst for change in a traditionally manual industry. Their main office in Beringen . At Glowi, data is an important asset that can be transformed into business value through innovative AI-based methodologies. In a collaboration with Vlerick Business School, Glowi wants to research these opportunities. We are looking for a business-oriented data scientist to develop and research AI opportunities in the service sector with academic rigour. As part of our close-knit team, you’ll bring Vlerick’s strategy and purpose to life. Are you excited to join our Area Marketing & Sales team as a PhD Researcher? Here’s what you need to know! Your Mission You will combine academic research with direct business impact, translating data and AI insights into real-world applications. Academic focus Complete a 4-year PhD on data analytics and AI. Conduct academic and applied research, including data collection, modelling, AI agent development, evaluation and reporting. Disseminate insights through papers, reports, workshops, presentations and social media for both academic and business audiences. Collaborate with faculty, researchers and support the activities of the research area. Business impact Work with client and employee data from Glowi. Develop predictive models and AI-driven solutions that are operationalised within the organisation. Design and evaluate genAI-supported workflows and AI agents embedded in existing processes. Work closely with Glowi’s Data & AI team and business stakeholders to improve key business KPIs. The Research Your PhD research will focus on employee-customer relationship management (acquisition, development and retention) within the cleaning services sector , exploring how machine learning and AI agents can generate insights and improve processes. The exact research topic will be defined together with the PhD candidate and may include: AI-driven employee and customer acquisition Consultant coaching effects on development and churn Skills, knowledge and behaviour (KSB) matching in recruitment and retention Employee absenteeism and performance modelling Pricing and price sensitivity analysis Hyper-personalised employee and customer communication using genAI Process automation using genAI and reinforcement learning All research is conducted in close collaboration with the business and combines state-of-the-art technology, real-world data, advanced modelling, and academic and managerial reporting. You Obtained a master’s degree in business analytics, business engineering, artificial intelligence, data science, business administration, economics, computer science, civil engineering, statistics, mathematics, or equivalent. Have excellent qualifications during your studies, such as distinctions (cum laude or higher) at the bachelor's and master's levels. Have good communication skills and a business mindset, which allows you to easily switch between different stakeholders at all levels. Can take up responsibilities and work independently. Are passionate about the topic, have a research mindset and great analytical skills. Have a good knowledge of data analytics and machine learning. Can program and have experience with Python and SQL. Preferably have experience with Microsoft Fabric and Azure. Are fluent in Dutch and English and have excellent writing skills. Have a proactive attitude and don’t shy away from presenting your findings to an academic and business audience. Will be based on one of our Vlerick campuses (Ghent or Brussels) and the office of Glowi at #ProudtobeVlerick Autonomy and responsibility in an engaging work environment. A dynamic, open, and international company culture. Opportunities for professional and personal growth. A team of enthusiastic, driven colleagues, passionate about learning. Opportunities to build your network, both in academics and in business. You’ll have a real impact and inspire people to live, learn and leap! At Vlerick, openness to the world is part of our DNA. We are continuously working towards being a truly diverse, equitable and inclusive place to work and learn at. So, no matter who you are, where you come from, or what your dreams are, we are looking forward to receiving your application. Vlerick Business School is the hosting institute for this PhD journey with Philippe Baecke as your promoter. Your salary will be in line with the salary scales at Ghent University. More information on the salary can be transparently accessed via this link. Take the leap! In case you are interested in this PhD journey and meet the mentioned criteria, please apply with your resume, motivation letter and transcripts from both your bachelor’s and master’s degree via our website. If available, please also add the results of your TOEFL or IELTS and your GRE score . We look forward to hearing from you! Happy to give you more information on the job content: philippe.baecke@vlerick.com. For more information on the selection process, please reach out to charlotte.mahieu@vlerick.com.

linkedin:4478474476.title: PhD position – Electromagnetic Compatibility & AI (all genders)
linkedin:4478474476.desc: Silicon Austria Labs (SAL), in collaboration with the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), is seeking a motivated PhD candidate to work on the AI-assisted modelling and prediction of radiated electromagnetic emissions from power electronics converters. The PhD project will be co-supervised by SAL and SDU. The candidate will spend most of the project period at SAL in Austria, working closely with SAL researchers to develop power electronics use cases for industry. The candidate will also receive academic supervision and scientific guidance from SDU, nevertheless the workplace is Graz. The PhD project combines the fields of power electronics, electromagnetic compatibility, radiated emission measurements, electromagnetic simulation, and AI-based modelling. The project aims to develop practical methods to help identify dominant radiation mechanisms, predict emission levels, and support EMC-aware converter design. Your Future Tasks Include Research topic Possible Research Directions Include Physics-informed AI models for predicting radiated emissions. Data-driven surrogate models for fast electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) assessment of converter designs. Modelling of dominant radiation sources, current loops, switching nodes, cables, heat sinks and PCB structures. Use of simulation and measurement data for AI model training and validation. Development of practical workflows for the early-stage design of EMC-aware power electronics. The project will not primarily focus on conducted emissions, but may consider source and coupling mechanisms where they influence the behaviour of radiated emissions. Main Tasks Develop AI/ML and physics-informed modelling methods for predicting radiated emissions. Work with power electronic converter models, electromagnetic simulations and measurement data. Analyse dominant radiation mechanisms in converter systems. Build and validate surrogate models for fast radiated emission estimation. Compare AI-assisted methods with conventional EMC simulation and measurement approaches. Develop benchmark and validation cases based on realistic converter structures. Publish results. Your Profile A Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Electromagnetics, Applied Physics or Computer Science. Very good understanding of power electronics, EMI/EMC, electromagnetic fields and circuit/system modelling. Programming experience, preferably in Python, MATLAB or similar tools. Interest in machine learning, surrogate modelling, scientific machine learning, or physics-informed AI. Ability to work independently and in an interdisciplinary research environment Experience with one or more of the following is advantageous: Radiated emission measurements or EMC testing Power converter modelling and high-frequency switching behaviour Electromagnetic simulation tools Near-field scanning Machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow Physics-informed neural networks or hybrid physics-AI modelling Signal processing and data analysis Important Facts About SAL Diverse research activities with many technical challenges. State-of-the-art laboratory facilities and equipment. Location in the heart of Europe in Austria – relocation support for non-European nationalities. Internal and external training opportunities for career development. Family & children friendly - actively shaping the compatibility of family and career. “Vital4SAL” to promote a healthy workplace (e.g. SAL coaching pool, trainings on mental health, physical activities, healthy snacks, 24/7 accident insurance) € 4 per day meal allowance in restaurants or € 2 per working day in supermarkets. Public transport initiative (subsidy for the “Klimaticket”) Our values: Open door policy, flexibility in working hours, casual dress code, diverse teams, working with people of different nationalities, informal communication, lifelong learning, compatibility of family and career, sustainability, personal growth, and collective advancement. This position is advertised in accordance with the collective agreement for employees in non-university research (Research CA). For this position, we offer a 3 years limited contract with the focus on pursuing the PhD. For this position, your monthly salary will be EUR 3.651, paid 14 times a year (based on an All-in contract). About Us Silicon Austria Labs (SAL) is a top research center for Electronics and Software Based Systems (ESBS). At three locations (Graz, Villach, Linz), SAL is conducting research along the entire ESBS value chain in the areas of sensor systems, power electronics, intelligent wireless systems, microsystems and embedded systems to develop future-oriented solutions for industrial production, health, energy, mobility, safety and more. SAL brings together key players from industry, science and research and thus valuable expertise and know-how and conducts cooperative, application-oriented research along the value chain. Cooperative projects are co-financed by SAL and enable a fast and unbureaucratic project start. SAL is thus shaping the high-tech location Austria and Europe and developing the future. Innovation is our top priority and so are our employees. We are a family-friendly company and support the compatibility of work and family as much as possible. That is why we have been awarded the Work and Family Certificate until 2026. But we are constantly working on new measures to offer our employees an environment where they feel good, healthy and motivated.

linkedin:4470973916.title: PhD Candidate in Explainable Machine Learning for Studying Biology at Single-Cell Resolution
linkedin:4470973916.desc: Are you a MSc graduate with background in data science, computer science, biostatistics, bioinformatics or a related field? Do you have a solid foundation in machine learning? Are you passionate about biology and interested in building new machine learning and AI to accelerate biological discoveries? Then this position is for you! Working at the UvA Join Us! We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop novel methodology for the analysis of single-cell (multi)-omics data by incorporating existing biological knowledge into machine learning models. You will join a collaborative and internationally-oriented team working at the interface of computer science, mathematics, and biology in the Biosystems Data Analysis group at the Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences at the University of Amsterdam. We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. If you recognise yourself in the role but do not meet every listed preference, we encourage you to apply. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do Interpretable machine learning is a growing research area, with important applications in the biological sciences, such as understanding how different genes regulate each other within biological pathways. However, the current common practice is first to build complicated, “black-box” models and try to understand what they learned afterwards. This has the disadvantage that a) interpretation is still not always possible and b) it is inefficient as the model must re-discover patterns that are already well-known from scratch every time it is trained. Recent technological advances have allowed us to study DNA and RNA not only in a “bulk” tissue, but also at a single-cell resolution, giving us unprecedented insights into how organisms form, how diseases develop, and how cells communicate with each other inside a tissue. In this project, you will build interpretable-by-design machine learning models for biological data that offer biological insights in a direct way. Such models will be applicable to a variety of single-cell datasets and experiments in different fields of biology. Tasks and responsibilities: complete a PhD thesis within the official appointment duration (four years); develop novel algorithms for analyzing single-cell (multi)-omics data and design and perform in silico experiments to test them; be an active and responsible member of the research group and collaborate closely with fellow group members; discuss work with group members and at departmental meetings, and incorporate feedback; take a leading role in writing manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and conferences; participate in the PhD training programme of the University of Amsterdam; assist with teaching and supervision of Bachelor’s and Master’s students. You will have the opportunity to: work at the interface of machine learning and biology; collaborate closely with biologists from a variety of disciplines including immunology and cancer biology; present results at national and international scientific conferences; expand academic, professional and personal skills; use high-end compute infrastructure via the national ICT cooperative (SURF) What We Ask Of You You are passionate about research and want to develop into an independent scientist. You have a background in machine learning and artificial intelligence and like to build novel methods for the analysis of biological data. You are methodical, curious and able to take initiative, while also valuing close collaboration in an interdisciplinary and international research environment. Your Experience And Profile You hold a MSc in Bioinformatics, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Biostatistics or a closely related discipline; have demonstrable experience with training machine and deep learning models, preferably using Python; have a basic understanding of biology and/or are interested in using computational methods to understand biology; are fluent in English, written and spoken. Your place at the UvA About The Faculty Of Science Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, whether it concerns elementary particles, the birth of the universe, or how the brain functions. The Faculty has a student population of approximately 8,000 students, as well as 1,800 staff members working in education, research, or support services. Important to know Your application & contact If you feel the profile fits you, and you are interested in the job, we look forward to receiving your application. You can apply online via the apply button. We accept applications until and including 31 October 2026. Do you have any questions, or do you require additional information? Please contact: dr. ir. Stavros Makrodimitris, s.makrodimitris@uva.nl prof. Dr. Aalt-Jan van Dijk, a.d.j.vandijk@uva.nl. Applications should include the following information (all files besides your cv should be submitted in one single pdf file): a detailed CV including the months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience; a letter of motivation; the names and email addresses of two references who can provide letters of recommendation. A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure. (for details: national knowledge security guidelines) Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion As an employer, the UvA maintains an equal opportunities policy. We value diversity and are fully committed to being a place where everyone feels at home. We nurture inquisitive minds and perseverance and allow room for persistent questioning. With us, curiosity and creativity are the prevailing culture. Studies show that women and members of underrepresented groups only apply for jobs if they meet 100% of the qualifications. Do you meet the educational requirements but not yet all of the requested experience? The UvA encourages you to apply anyway.

linkedin:4478449998.title: Doctoral Researcher in Predictive Modelling of Reused Concrete Elements
linkedin:4478449998.desc: About Us The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character. The Faculty of Science, Technology and Medicine (FSTM) at the University of Luxembourg contributes multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences and Medicine. Through its dual mission of teaching and research, the FSTM seeks to generate and disseminate knowledge and train new generations of responsible citizens in order to better understand, explain and advance society and the environment we live in. The Sustainable Concrete Structure Laboratory is looking for 3 new Ph.D. candidates based on the ERC project RESCUE. In this fully-funded position, the Ph.D. candidates will work on using developing new modelling frameworks for predicting the remaining life of reused concrete elements. linkedin:4479507406.desc: Introduction Are you fascinated by improving the acoustic performance of timber buildings? Help develop advanced numerical models that predict sound transmission and bridge the gap between sustainable construction and high acoustic performance. Join this joint PhD project between TU/e and DTU! Job Description Buildings made from timber and other biobased materials generally have a significantly lower carbon footprint than conventional concrete or masonry constructions. However, lightweight timber structures often exhibit high variability in sound insulation, and poor acoustic performance remains a barrier to their wider adoption in the construction industry. A still poorly understood source of this variability lies in the connections between structural components, such as screws, nails, steel brackets, and adhesive joints. Whether a floor is screwed or glued together, and how widely spaced the fasteners are, can significantly affect how sound travels through a building. Current prediction methods largely ignore these details, while more detailed models are often too computationally expensive for practical use. Developing methods that are both physically accurate and computationally efficient is therefore the central challenge of this project. We offer a PhD position (4-year contract) within the QUIET-ARC project, a collaboration between Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as part of the EuroTech Universities PhD programme. As a PhD candidate in the QUIET-ARC project, you will investigate how different connection types and layouts influence sound transmission in timber buildings, develop efficient numerical simulation methods to model these effects, and quantify the uncertainty introduced by construction variability into acoustic predictions. Noise is recognised by the World Health Organisation as a major public health concern. By improving the predictive capability of computational models for timber buildings, this research supports more reliable prediction tools for sustainable constructions and contributes to the wider adoption of low-carbon building materials. The project will take place under joint supervision of dr.ir. Cédric Van hoorickx (TU/e, specializing in numerical modelling of sound transmission) and dr.ir. Jonas Brunskog (DTU, with expertise in the acoustics of lightweight structures). You will be based in the Building Acoustics research group (https://building-acoustics.net/) in the Department of the Built Environment at TU/e, and will spend approximately six months at DTU’s Acoustic Technology group in Denmark. indeed:ad72dbebe07cb661.title: Doctorant CIFRE en intelligence artificielle (H/F)
indeed:ad72dbebe07cb661.desc: Projet de thèse CIFRE — Apprentissage de stratégies de mémoire et de décision pour des systèmes d’IA locaux Mots-clés : Agentic systems, LLMs, persistent memory, sequential decision-making, reinforcement learning, model routing, model specialization, sovereign AI. Contexte scientifique USTS développe un projet d’IA souveraine, entièrement exécuté sur une infrastructure locale, pour permettre aux entreprises de garder le contrôle de leurs données et de leurs systèmes, tout en préservant la précision et la qualité des résultats. La thèse s’intéresse aux systèmes fondés sur des modèles de langage capables d’accomplir des tâches séquentielles : exploiter des informations, interagir avec des outils, conserver des connaissances et adapter leurs actions aux résultats obtenus. Dans ce cadre, la réussite dépend de décisions prises à différents moments de l’exécution, dont les conséquences peuvent être différées. Le choix d’une information à conserver influence les actions futures. Le choix d’un modèle détermine le coût et la qualité d’une étape. Une vérification peut éviter la propagation d’une erreur, mais consomme des ressources supplémentaires. La mémoire, les actions et l’utilisation des modèles constituent ainsi des composantes interdépendantes du processus de décision. Le problème étudié sera celui de l’apprentissage de stratégies coordonnées pour ces composantes, dans un environnement où les informations évoluent et où le calcul disponible est limité. Question scientifique et hypothèses Comment apprendre conjointement des stratégies de mémoire, d’action et d’utilisation des modèles qui maintiennent la fiabilité des tâches séquentielles lorsque les informations évoluent et que les ressources de calcul sont limitées ? Une hypothèse centrale est que l’apprentissage de ces stratégies à partir de la réussite des tâches complètes peut améliorer le compromis entre fiabilité et coût de calcul par rapport à des stratégies optimisées séparément. Cette hypothèse conduit à plusieurs questions : comment estimer l’utilité future d’une information ? Comment attribuer un échec à une décision de mémoire, à une action ou au choix d’un modèle ? Comment répartir les ressources entre génération, recherche d’information et vérification ? Dans quelles conditions les stratégies apprises restent-elles efficaces sur de nouvelles tâches ? Ces questions seront étudiées à travers des hypothèses explicites et des expériences permettant de les confirmer, de les réfuter ou d’en préciser les conditions de validité. Programme de recherche Les premiers travaux porteront sur la formalisation du système comme un problème de décision séquentielle, éventuellement partiellement observable. Il s’agira de définir les observations accessibles, les opérations de mémoire, les actions possibles et les contraintes de ressources. Cette formulation permettra d’étudier des objectifs d’apprentissage combinant réussite de la tâche, erreurs et coût d’exécution. L’apprentissage de la mémoire La recherche portera sur la sélection, la représentation, la mise à jour et la récupération des informations en fonction de leur utilité pour les décisions futures. Une attention particulière sera accordée aux informations corrigées ou devenues obsolètes, ainsi qu’aux conséquences différées des opérations de mémoire. L’attribution des erreurs et l’apprentissage des décisions Lorsque l’évaluation porte sur le résultat final, il peut être difficile d’identifier les décisions responsables d’un échec. Les travaux pourront étudier des signaux intermédiaires, des objectifs auxiliaires ou des méthodes d’attribution permettant d’améliorer l’apprentissage sans réduire l’évaluation à la qualité de chaque étape prise isolément. L’allocation adaptative du calcul Le système devra choisir quand mobiliser un modèle spécialisé, solliciter un modèle plus coûteux, rechercher une information ou vérifier un résultat. L’objectif sera d’apprendre ces choix en fonction de l’état de la tâche, de l’incertitude et des ressources restantes. Ces volets contribueront à une même problématique. Leur articulation et leur priorité seront précisées à partir de l’état de l’art et des premiers résultats expérimentaux. Recherche sur les modèles Les modèles constituent le moteur du système étudié. La thèse comprendra donc des travaux sur les modèles génératifs, les modèles de décision et leurs modalités d’apprentissage. Les recherches pourront porter sur la spécialisation de modèles locaux, la distillation de comportements ou la conception d’objectifs d’entraînement tenant compte de la réussite de trajectoires complètes. Elles examineront également la répartition des capacités entre un modèle unique et un ensemble de modèles coordonnés par une politique de routage. L’enjeu sera de déterminer quelles capacités doivent être apprises dans les modèles et quelles décisions doivent être prises au cours de l’exécution. Les architectures seront comparées en intégrant le coût de leur coordination et les interactions entre spécialisation, mémoire et décision. Évaluation et contributions attendues L’évaluation reposera sur des tâches séquentielles permettant de faire varier la durée des trajectoires, l’évolution des informations, la disponibilité des outils et les budgets de calcul. Des comparaisons avec des méthodes de référence, des études d’ablation et des évaluations sur des tâches non utilisées pendant l’apprentissage permettront d’identifier l’origine des gains et leurs limites. Les mesures porteront notamment sur la réussite des tâches, les erreurs critiques, la stabilité des résultats, la latence et les ressources consommées. Les expériences étudieront également la propagation des erreurs et la capacité du système à récupérer après une décision incorrecte. Des connaissances en apprentissage par renforcement, en décision séquentielle, en statistiques ou en optimisation seront appréciées. indeed:57a20bba0b7ef518.title: Wissenschaftliche MitarbeiterIn – DoktorandIn (PhD)
indeed:57a20bba0b7ef518.desc: Die Process and Data Science Gruppe (PADS) sucht kontinuierlich nach talentierten neuen MitarbeiterInnen, die an der Schnittstelle von Data Science und Process Science arbeiten möchten. Es gibt offene Stellen auf allen Ebenen (PhD, Postdoc, Software Engineer, etc.). Bei Interesse senden Sie Ihre Bewerbung bitte direkt an applications@pads.rwth-aachen.de Wenn Sie sich bewerben, geben Sie bitte relevante Informationen an und begründen Sie, warum Sie zu unserer Forschung im Bereich Process Mining beitragen können. Generische Bewerbungen werden aussortiert. Zeigen Sie, dass Sie wissen, was die Gruppe tut und was Sie zum Stand der Technik im Process Mining beitragen wollen. Bitte beachten Sie, dass das PADS-Schwerpunktkolloquium für Personen gedacht ist, die sich auf PADS-bezogene Themen spezialisieren möchten, d.h. auf Process Mining oder andere Ansätze, die Prozess- und Datenwissenschaft miteinander verbinden. Lesen Sie unbedingt das Springer-Buch "Process Mining: Data Science in Action" (ISBN: 978-3-662-49850-7) ausführlich und seien Sie darauf vorbereitet, technische Fragen zu den von Ihnen belegten PADS-Kursen zu beantworten (z.B. konkrete Modelle anhand von Daten zu erstellen). Der beste Zeitpunkt für das mündliche PADS- Schwerpunktkolloquium ist kurz vor der Masterarbeit. Studierenden mit schlechteren Noten in den BPI/APM/IDS-Kursen wird dringend empfohlen, ein anderes Schwerpunktkolloquium zu wählen oder sich sehr gut vorzubereiten. Es ist gewünscht, dass sich StudentInnen bewerben, welche Ihre Masterarbeit in unserer Gruppe schreiben möchten. Alle Stellen sind grundsätzlich Vollzeitstellen, es besteht aber auch die Möglichkeit, in Teilzeit zu arbeiten. Die Vergütung erfolgt in Anlehnung an den Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst (TV-L) unter Berücksichtigung Ihrer Berufserfahrung. Die RWTH ist ein Arbeitgeber der Chancengleichheit. Wir freuen uns daher über Bewerbungen von allen qualifizierten Bewerberinnen und Bewerbern, insbesondere aus derzeit benachteiligten Personengruppen. Ihre Ansprechpartnerin Frau Mara Nitschke Tel.: +49 (0) 241 8021902 E-Mail: applications@pads.rwth-aachen.de Wissenschaftliche MitarbeiterIn – DoktorandIn (PhD) Als DoktorandIn haben Sie die Möglichkeit, in einem Bereich mit vielen offenen wissenschaftlichen Herausforderungen zu forschen. Sie werden eine begrenzte Lehraufgabe haben und Bachelor- und MasterstudentInnen betreuen. In einem Zeitraum von vier Jahren erhalten Sie ausreichend Zeit, um Spitzenforschung zu betreiben und Ihre Arbeit auf den führenden Konferenzen in diesem Bereich zu präsentieren. Sie werden in einer starken und fokussierten Forschungsgruppe arbeiten, in der Sie die erforderliche Unterstützung und Rückmeldung erhalten. Nach einem PhD in PADS können Sie wählen, ob Sie eine Karriere in der Industrie oder in der Wissenschaft anstreben wollen. Der Grund dafür ist, dass Process Mining herausfordernde Forschungsprobleme bietet und gleichzeitig ein großer Bedarf an Experten besteht, die an der Schnittstelle von Prozessen und Daten arbeiten. Anforderungen Ein Master-Abschluss in Informatik oder Data Science (oder einer benachbarten Disziplin wie Operations Research, Elektrotechnik und Statistik) Sie verfügen über ausgezeichnete Sprachkenntnisse in Englisch und sind bereit, Ihre Ideen zu präsentieren. Sie sind in der Lage, Forschungsprototypen (z. B. in Java oder Python) zu entwickeln, um groß angelegte Experimente durchzuführen. Sie legen Wert auf Präzision, d. h. Sie sind bestrebt, Ihre Ideen rigoros zu präsentieren und zu prüfen. Sie kennen sich mit Process Mining aus (lesen Sie z. B. die process mining book oder den Coursera MOOC besucht "Process Mining: Data science in Action"). Sie haben ein echtes Interesse und/oder Erfahrung in den Bereichen Data Science, Process Science, Process Mining, maschinelles Lernen, Prozessmanagement und/oder Operations Research.

indeed:66e7fe5af708655a.title: PhD Researcher / Doctoral Researcher (m/f/d) Bioinformatics & AML
indeed:66e7fe5af708655a.desc: Department of Internal Medicine II, Research Group: Functional Genomics of Acute Leukemia (Heads: Dr. Lorenz Bastian / Prof. Dr. Claudia Baldus) The position is part of the newly established research project “LUCID-AML – Learning-based Unsupervised Clustering of transcriptomIcs to Detect developmental, functional and prognostic subtypes in AML across age”, funded by the Deutsche José Carreras Leukämie-Stiftung. It is closely linked to our DFG-funded Clinical Research Unit “CATCH-ALL: Towards a Cure for Adults and Children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia”, where clinical and basic researchers work together to define mechanisms of leukemogenesis and treatment resistance across age groups. Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) affects people of all ages, but its incidence increases steeply in older adults, while survival decreases sharply with age. AML can be classified into transcriptomic groups that reflect cytogenetic lesions, reveal developmental origins and link leukemias to normal hematopoietic states. However, consistent subtype definitions and robustly validated tools for applying them across cohorts are lacking. The project builds on ALLCatchR and our work on machine-learning frameworks for disease classification and the identification of novel molecular subtypes in acute lymphoblastic leukemia. LUCID-AML will integrate more than 8,000 bulk AML gene-expression profiles from multiple cohorts with single-cell data, molecular genetics, diagnostic classifications, drug-response data and clinical outcomes. The project aims to establish reproducible, gene-expression-based AML subtypes while accounting for age and treatment. Further aims are to define their developmental origins and make the resulting models available as transparent, open-source tools for research and clinical diagnostics. For further reading: Beder et al., HemaSphere, 2023; Bastian et al., Blood, 2024; Beder et al., bioRxiv / HemaSphere, 2026. Join our team Join our team as soon as possible . indeed:1f22aaa5b32719ae.title: Doctoral Researcher in Interactive and Immersive Simulation of Animal Navigation in the Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group
indeed:1f22aaa5b32719ae.desc: Paygrade E13 TV-L Working Hours 100% (suitable for part-time) Institution Institute of Physics (School of Mathematics and Natural Sciences) Location Oldenburg (Oldb) Application Deadline 30.10.2026 First day of work 01.01.2027 Limited for 3 years About us The Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group at the University of Oldenburg invites applications for a three-year doctoral research position at the interface of computer science, physics, and biology. The project investigates how interactive and immersive simulation can help scientists explore, experiment with, and reason about computational models of animal navigation. Animals navigate using multiple environmental and sensory cues. Computational models allow researchers to investigate possible mechanisms, test hypotheses, and predict movement patterns. This PhD will develop and scientifically evaluate interactive approaches that make such models more accessible to systematic exploration, comparison, and interpretation. Virtual and mixed reality are promising approaches, alongside conventional desktop and potentially web-based interfaces. Research questions How can researchers interactively vary model parameters, assumptions, sensory cues, and competing navigation hypotheses? Under which conditions do immersive interfaces (VR/MR) offer advantages over conventional interfaces for exploring complex navigation simulations? How can interactive representations help connect individual simulated decisions and trajectories with population-level or large-scale movement patterns? How can the scientific value of different interaction techniques be evaluated in realistic research tasks? Your tasks Develop a research framework for visualizing and interacting with computational models of animal navigation. Design and implement methods to explore parameters, manipulate assumptions, compare hypotheses, and inspect simulated outcomes. Integrate existing or newly developed navigation models and simulation data into interactive environments, potentially using Unity, Unreal Engine, or other appropriate technologies. Design and conduct evaluations with researchers to assess how different interfaces support scientific exploration, interpretation, and reasoning. Collaborate closely with scientists in physics, biology, and computer science; document and disseminate results through scientific publications and presentations. Pursue an independent doctoral research project leading to a PhD. Your profile Required qualifications: Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Physics, Computational Biology, Engineering, Human–Computer Interaction, or a closely related discipline. Strong programming skills, for example in Python, C++, C#, or comparable languages. Experience in interactive software development, simulation, scientific computing, visualization, or related areas. Interest in computational modelling and in investigating scientific questions through software and empirical evaluation. Excellent written and spoken English; ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team. Advanced experience with machine learning methods Desirable qualifications Experience with VR/MR, Unity or Unreal Engine, 3D interaction, or immersive visualization. Knowledge of human–computer interaction, user studies, usability evaluation, or visual analytics. Experience with agent-based modelling, animal movement, navigation, ecological simulation, or trajectory analysis. Familiarity with reproducible research software, data pipelines, or scientific visualization. Possible additional application: science communication Methods developed for scientific research may also be adapted into accessible interactive demonstrations for public outreach, for example through VR/MR or web-based experiences at science events. This is a secondary opportunity rather than a separate educational-software development objective. We offer The Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group (www.quantbiolab.com) develops computational approaches to biological and physical systems and works in an international, interdisciplinary research environment. The position offers collaboration across disciplines, access to modern computational and immersive-visualization infrastructure, doctoral supervision, and opportunities for scientific publication and professional development. Employment conditions and benefits follow the applicable collective agreement (TV-L) and university policies, including annual leave, flexible working arrangements, and university health and sports programmes. Our standards The University of Oldenburg is dedicated to increase the percentage of female employees in the field of science. Therefore, female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply. In accordance to § 21 Section 3 NHG, female candidates with equal qualifications will be preferentially considered. Applicants with disabilities will be given preference in case of equal qualification. Apply now Please send your application via e-mail by 30.10.2026 to ilia.solovyov@uni-oldenburg.de Please submit a single PDF with the following reference number QBL10 containing a cover letter explaining your research motivation and relevant experience, a CV, academic transcripts, a brief statement of research interests, a list of publications or software projects (if applicable), and contact details of at least two referees. Applications should be sent to Prof. Dr. Ilia Solov’yov. The application deadline and anticipated starting date will be announced in the final advertisement. Benefits at University of Oldenburg 30 days vacation Secure remuneration according to collective agreement Company pension scheme Further education opportunities Flexible working hours Health management Remote working Compatibility of career and family Support with childcare University Sports Centre Certificate Bicycle-friendly employer Corporate Benefits
