indeed:b6dd9f7887240a5d.desc: Job description Company and benefits Social Impact & Sustainability Job ID 41745 Join the leader in entertainment innovation and help us design the future. At Dolby, science meets art, and high tech means more than computer code. As a member of the Dolby team, you’ll see and hear the results of your work everywhere, from movie theaters to smartphones. We continue to revolutionize how people create, deliver, and enjoy entertainment worldwide. To do that, we need the absolute best talent. We’re big enough to give you all the resources you need, and small enough so you can make a real difference and earn recognition for your work. We offer a collegial culture, challenging projects, and excellent compensation and benefits, not to mention a Flex Work approach that is truly flexible to support where, when, and how you do your best work. Internship: Development and On-Device Deployment of an Autoregressive Model for Real-Time Speech Restoration and Dialog Enhancement Start: Open Duration: 3 months (full-time) or 6 months (part-time) Location: Stockholm Speech restoration and dialog enhancement are critical components in modern audio experiences, especially in noisy environments or legacy content with degraded quality. Current systems often rely on non-causal, server-side models that require full audio context, limiting their use in real-time or on-device applications. With recent advances in autoregressive language modeling and efficient deep learning deployment, there is growing potential to develop low-latency, high-quality speech enhancement systems that operate in real time and even on consumer devices. This internship aims to design and implement an autoregressive, large language model (LLM)-based architecture for speech restoration and dialog enhancement. The model will be trained to reconstruct clean speech from degraded inputs by leveraging both acoustic and linguistic context. It will be evaluated against Dolby’s current best multimodal system, focusing on perceptual quality, intelligibility, and latency. A key objective is to explore the feasibility of deploying the model on-device through techniques such as model compression, quantization, pruning, and compilation using modern inference frameworks. Candidate requirements Master’s or Ph.D. student in Machine Learning, Signal Processing, Computer Science, or a related field. Hands-on experience with PyTorch. Interest in model optimization for edge deployment using tools such as Triton Inference Server, ONNX, TensorRT, or similar frameworks. Prior experience in this field is a plus. Experience fine-tuning LLMs is a plus. Knowledge of audio-language modeling is a plus. Dolby Hiring Entity: Gävlegatan 12A 113 30 Stockholm, Sweden

indeed:3f0926cce4ced4b9.title: Doctoral student in Industrial Design with focus on strategic design
indeed:3f0926cce4ced4b9.desc: Lund University was founded in 1666 and is repeatedly ranked among the world’s top universities. The University has around 46 000 students and 8 500 staff based in Lund, Helsingborg and Malmö. We are united in our efforts to understand, explain and improve our world and the human condition. Lund University welcomes applicants with diverse backgrounds and experiences. We regard equality, equal opportunities and diversity as a strength and an asset. Description of the workplace The position is located in the division of Industrial Design at the Department of Design Sciences at LTH, Lund University. Design Sciences is an interdisciplinary department that integrates design, technology, and people in its research and education. As a doctoral student you will become part of an interdisciplinary research environment and work alongside doctoral students, senior researchers and teaching staff within Industrial Design and the wider Department of Design Sciences. Being a doctoral student As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. You will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree. More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. Subject and project description Research in Industrial Design investigates how design shapes and responds to technological, environmental and societal change. It develops and critically examines design knowledge, methods and practices, with the aim of understanding how design can contribute to meaningful and responsible transformation. Our research combines scientific and artistic approaches and is often conducted in collaboration with academic, industrial and public-sector partners as well as communities and third-sector organizations. The research environment encompasses sustainable design; emerging technologies and AI; design strategy, management and innovation; design practice and methods; and critical and participatory perspectives on design and design education. This doctoral position has a particular focus on strategic design. The research will investigate how design can operate as a strategic capability in organizations and society and contribute to processes of innovation, transformation and value creation. Possible areas of inquiry include how design capabilities are developed and embedded in organizations; the role of design and design approaches in enabling organizational change; design in complex settings; systemic design; and user and citizen engagement in strategic design processes. The research may also investigate futures-oriented approaches, including designerly ways of navigating complex and uncertain societal, technological and environmental conditions. Within this overall research area, the doctoral student will develop and refine the specific research direction and project in dialogue with the supervisors. The project is expected to combine theoretical inquiry with empirical research and may incorporate experimental, participatory or practice-based design approaches where relevant. Work duties You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme. You will develop and conduct an independent doctoral research project. Your work will include formulating research questions, reviewing and developing relevant theoretical perspectives, designing and conducting empirical studies, analysing research material, communicating findings through academic publications and conferences, and completing a doctoral thesis. You will also be expected to participate actively in the research environment of the Division of Industrial Design and the Department of Design Sciences and to engage with relevant academic and external research partners. Additional duties include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours). The position requires regular on-site presence at Lund University in Lund to carry out the work and participate fully in the research environment. Qualifications To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below. Admission requirements A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Industrial Design if the applicant has: at least 30 higher education credits relevant to the subject area, of which at least 15 credits must be at an advanced level, or an in-depth study of at least 20 higher education credits at an advanced level relevant to the subject area, or a degree in fine arts, engineering, Master's or Magister's degree relevant to the subject area. Additional requirements In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: Knowledge and skills relevant to industrial design and to the proposed area of doctoral research. Ability to to independently formulate and address research problems. Analytical skills and the ability to engage critically with theoretical perspectives and empirical material. Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. Other qualifications (advantages) For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications: Experience of conducting empirical, practice-based or participatory research. Experience of interdisciplinary or multidisciplinary work. Experience of managing complex projects involving multiple actors or perspectives. Experience of using design methods and practices as part of research or inquiry. Experience of collaboration with academic, industrial, public-sector or other societal actors. Experience of communicating research or complex design work to different audiences. Consideration will also be given to the applicant's ability to take initiative, work independently, collaborate with others, and develop and complete a long-term research project. We offer Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. More about working at Lund University on lu.se. About the employment The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting on 2027-01-01 or soon after. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§. More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages. Other This doctoral position is funded by the Ingvar Kamprad Design Foundation (IKDF). How to apply Applications must be written in English and include: CV A cover letter describing your reasons for wishing to undertake a PhD in Industrial Design, your interest in this position, and how your academic, professional and/or personal experiences have shaped your research interests and prepared you for doctoral studies. Copies of degree certificates and transcripts confirming that you meet the general and specific admission requirements; A research statement (maximum 1,500 words) describing the research questions, problems or phenomena within Strategic Design that you are interested in exploring, why you consider them important, and how you might approach investigating them. The statement is intended to demonstrate your research interests and ability to formulate a potential direction for doctoral research; it is not expected to constitute a fully developed research proposal. A portfolio or selection of work samples demonstrating relevant design, research, or professional work. These may include design projects, research projects, publications or other written work, collaborative or community-based projects, or other work relevant to the position. For collaborative work, clearly describe your own role and contribution. Contact information for three references and Any other documents you wish to be considered. We welcome your application. LTH is Lund University’s Faculty of Engineering. At LTH we educate people, build knowledge for the future and work hard for the development of society. We create space for brilliant research and inspire creative advancements in technology, architecture and design. We have nearly 12,000 students. Every year, our researchers – many of whom work in world-leading profile areas – publish around 100 theses and 2 000 scientific findings. In addition, a number of research results and degree projects are transformed into innovations. Together we explore and create – to benefit the world. We kindly decline all sales and marketing contacts. En tant qu’employeur, elle encourage l’excellence, la reconnaissance des personnes et la responsabilité. unil.ch/travailler Présentation Un poste de doctorant·e en modélisation spatio-temporelle d'événements extrêmes (incendies de forêt) financé par le Fonds national suisse de la recherche scientifique (FNS) est à pourvoir dans le laboratoire de la Dre Marj Tonini à l'Institut des dynamiques de la surface terrestre (IDYST), Faculté des géosciences et de l'environnement (GSE), Université de lausanne (Unil), en collaboration avec la prof. Valérie Chabez-Demoulin (co-requérante principale), professeure de statistique à la Faculté des hautes études commerciales (HEC Lausanne), Unil. Le laboratoire développe des approches innovantes en apprentissage automatique et en statistique pour l'analyse de données environnementales complexes présentant des dimensions spatiales et temporelles. Nous recherchons un·e candidat·e pour rejoindre ExtFire, un projet financé par le FNS qui vise à développer le premier cadre paneuropéen combinant la théorie des valeurs extrêmes (TVE) non stationnaire, l'inférence causale et l'apprentissage profond sensible aux queues de distribution, afin de quantifier et de prédire le risque d'incendies extrêmes de manière reproductible et transférable. Outre les deux requérantes principales, l'équipe d'ExtFire réunit trois partenaires externes aux compétences complémentaires : le prof. Marco Turco (Université de Murcie, Espagne) apporte une expertise spécialisée dans les interactions entre feux et climat ; Le Dr Paolo Fiorucci (CIMA Research Foundation, Italie) apporte son expertise en simulation de la propagation des feux ; et le Dr Erwan Koch (Expertise Centre for Climate Extremes, Unil) fournit son expertise en TVE spatiale et en champs aléatoires max-stables. La personne retenue rejoindra le laboratoire de la Dre Tonini à l'IDYST et travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le·la postdoctorant·e recruté·e dans le cadre du projet ExtFire, bénéficiant de l'expertise et du soutien de l'ensemble de l'équipe ExtFire. Le·la doctorant·e contribuera à ExtFire en développant le coeur du projet. Les tâches principales comprennent : Harmoniser et intégrer de grands jeux de données ouverts sur les incendies, la météorologie et la surface terrestre au sein d'une infrastructure de données paneuropéenne cohérente ; Développer des modèles statistiques et spatio-temporels pour caractériser les incendies extrêmes, tels que ceux présentant de très grandes surfaces brûlées ou une propagation rapide ; Constituer les jeux de données et les modèles d'apprentissage automatique de référence utilisés pour évaluer les prédictions d'événements extrêmes ; Appliquer des méthodes d'IA explicable (p. ex. SHAP) pour identifier les principaux facteurs environnementaux des incendies extrêmes selon les régions ; Rédiger des articles scientifiques, présenter les résultats lors de conférences internationales et participer à l'enseignement en tant qu'assistant·e (environ 10% du temps). Votre profil Nous recherchons un·e candidat·e motivé·e présentant le profil suivant : Volonté d'élaborer une thèse en modélisation spatio-temporelle d'événements extrêmes (incendies de forêt) ; Master en sciences de l'environnement, géosciences, statistique, mathématiques appliquées, physique, informatique ou dans un domaine quantitatif étroitement apparenté, avec de solides résultats académiques ; Expérience pratique de l'apprentissage automatique, idéalement de l'apprentissage profond (p. ex. PyTorch, TensorFlow), et familiarité avec l'IA explicable ; Solides bases en statistique et en analyse de données (p. ex. probabilités, régression, séries temporelles ou statistique spatiale). La connaissance de la théorie des valeurs extrêmes est un atout ; Solides compétences en programmation en Python et/ou R, attestées par une expérience du traitement et de l'analyse de grands jeux de données (p. ex. données climatiques ou de télédétection maillées, formats NetCDF/raster) ; Maîtrise de l'anglais, à l'écrit et à l'oral, avec la capacité de rédiger des rapports scientifiques. La connaissance du français est un atout ; Une expérience avérée en analyse quantitative ou en modélisation des dangers naturels (p. ex. incendies de forêt, inondations, glissements de terrain, séismes) attestée par un mémoire, un projet ou une publication, est un atout. Vos avantages Nous offrons un environnement de travail dynamique et inclusif, favorisant un fort esprit de communauté et offrant un soutien dédié au développement d'une carrière académique. indeed:fa75a4e8504b1c03.title: AstraZeneca-Funded Non-Clinical PhD Studentship (Fixed Term): Physics-Guided Representation Learning for Drug Discovery
indeed:fa75a4e8504b1c03.desc: Applications are invited for a four-year, AstraZeneca-funded PhD studentship in the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics, commencing in October 2027. The successful candidate will be jointly supervised by Prof Sergio Bacallado (University of Cambridge), Dr Dino Oglic (AstraZeneca), and Dr Jon Paul Janet (AstraZeneca). The studentship offers an opportunity to conduct cutting-edge research at the interface of statistical machine learning, molecular simulation and drug discovery. Project description The project, entitled Physics-Guided Representation Learning from Free Energy Perturbation Data for Affinity Prediction and Candidate Down-Selection , aims to develop novel machine-learning methods for predicting molecular binding affinities and supporting decision-making in drug discovery. Free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations provide valuable information about how strongly candidate drug molecules bind to their biological targets, but these calculations are computationally expensive. This project will investigate how machine-learning models can extract richer information from FEP data and experimental measurements, combining physical principles with modern representation-learning techniques. The research will involve developing and evaluating new statistical and machine-learning methods, with access to both public benchmark datasets and AstraZeneca's industrial drug-discovery expertise and data. Candidate requirements Applicants should have, or expect to obtain, a first-class or upper second-class honours degree (or equivalent), normally following four years of university study. We welcome applicants with backgrounds in Mathematics, Statistics, Machine Learning, Scientific Computing, or any closely related discipline. Experience with computational chemistry would be desirable but is not essential . We particularly welcome applications from candidates with strong mathematical or machine-learning backgrounds who are interested in applying their expertise to problems in drug discovery. Funding The studentship provides funding for four years , covering a maintenance stipend and University tuition fees at the UK/Home rate. The studentship is open to candidates eligible for Home-fee status. International candidates may also be considered, provided that additional funding can be secured through scholarships or other approved funding schemes to cover the difference between Home and international tuition fees. This difference cannot be covered through student self-funding. Training and supervision The student will benefit from joint academic and industrial supervision, participating in the research activities of the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics and collaborating closely with AstraZeneca researchers to gain exposure to industrial applications of artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical development. How to apply Applications must be submitted through the University of Cambridge Postgraduate Applicant Portal , selecting the course PhD in Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics : https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/mapmpdpms/apply Applicants should indicate Dr Sergio Bacallado as their proposed supervisor and use the following project title: Physics-Guided Representation Learning from Free Energy Perturbation Data for Affinity Prediction and Candidate Down-Selection. Applications should include the supporting documentation required by the University, including academic transcripts, a CV, two references, and the relevant research summary and reasons for applying. The deadline for applications is 6 January 2027 (23:59 UK time) . Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview in January 2027 . Informal enquiries about the project are welcome and may be addressed to Dr Sergio Bacallado at sb2116@cam.ac.uk . The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

Your immediate leader is the Head of the Communication Technology Unit at the department of Information Security and Communication Technology. The workplace will be located in Trondheim. About The Project Future 6G and beyond communication systems are expected to integrate terrestrial cellular networks with non-terrestrial platforms, including Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellites, High Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS), and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). While such integrated networks can provide ubiquitous connectivity and improved resilience, they also introduce significant challenges due to highly dynamic radio environments, heterogeneous backhaul infrastructures, mobility, resource constraints, and service disruptions. The core research focuses on the MAC layer and its techniques – the candidate will design, implement and evaluate an AI-driven MAC-control framework that self‑heals in integrated terrestrial-NTN (LEO, HAPS, UAV) 6G networks. The work will be hands-on and system-oriented; a closed-loop, verifiable prototype will be built, tested under realistic degradations and examined for different metrics such as latency, reliability, fairness and SLA‑violation. For example, the candidate will do some of the tasks including: AI-driven Link Adaptation and MAC control – develop AI-based mechanism that proactively anticipate and respond to rapidly changing conditions in integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (LEO satellites, HAPS, and UAVs) and to cascading radio access networks (RAN) failures/degradations. AI-Driven self-healing MAC – develop algorithms and techniques at the MAC layer for fast anomaly detection, failure prediction, autonomous recovery, and performance resilience. Service-aware MAC layer techniques – develop novel MAC-layer mechanisms that integrate queueing theory, traffic modelling, machine learning, and network-performance prediction for improving latency, reliability and fairness to support mission‑critical services. The proposed algorithms and mechanisms will be implemented and validated on the B5G Lab infrastructure at the IIK department, NTNU. The lab provides industry‑grade 5G equipment, open‑source RAN stacks, programmable OpenFlow/P4 switches and AI‑Boxes for fast inference, together with NetFPGA/DAG hardware for sub‑millisecond failure detection and a Timeseries‑DB/Grafana monitoring platform for closed‑loop testing. linkedin:4480963636.title: PhD Position in Accountable and Responsible AI
linkedin:4480963636.desc: Are you eager to conduct high-impact research spanning computer science, economics, law, and the creative industry—while living in Amsterdam, a dynamic city renowned for its high-quality life and its thriving AI and creative sectors? Working at the UvA Join Us! A fully funded four-year Ph.D. position is available in the Complex Cyber Infrastructure research group at the University of Amsterdam. As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes deeply embedded in our society, the urgency to warrant its responsible and accountable use is increasing. Examples include the control that creative industry actors need to manifest when using AI pipelines in the (moving) image industry. This PhD project aims to focus on the emerging field of Accountable and Responsible AI, with the goal of advancing knowledge and practice at the intersection of AI research, creative industry practices, and societal regulatory expectations. Two projects underpin this position: SafeGenAI – a creative industry endeavour to enable creative industry actors to safely use GenAI tools; and LLM4LM – a large consortium addressing the legal-tech challenges in cross-organisational multi-domain agentic solutions. The candidate will not only have a chance to contribute to shaping the next generation AI systems within the creative industry and logistics practices, but also potentially to design more transparent, fair, and compliant ones with evolving societal and regulatory expectations. The successful candidate will be embedded in a team that will help transfer fundamental research results into the creative industry and legal practices, respectively. Moreover, they will be working closely with the supervision team, as well as the other PhD students and postdocs in the research group. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do In this context, you will investigate the following key challenges: Opacity in GenAI inferencing: How can the inferencing and reasoning processes of GenAI systems be made sufficiently transparent and traceable to support accountability in high-stakes professional contexts? AI legal compliance-by-design: How can GenAI systems be built to satisfy the requirements of the regulations such as the EU AI Act — including transparency, human oversight, and risk management — while remaining practically useful in domain-specific workflows? SMEs lack the expertise to navigate complex regulatory environments: How can domain-specific structured knowledge be integrated into GenAI systems to ground their outputs, reduce hallucination, and support trustworthy decision for non-expert users? What We Ask Of You Your experience and profile: MSc in CS, AI or a closely related field. Strong interest in Interest in finance and financial services is a plus.; previous experience in these fields is a plus. Enthusiasm for the research process: studying research papers, solving complex problems, applying creative thinking, evaluation, reflection and disseminating findings via writing and oral presentations. The ability to critically analyse abstract models as well as concrete implementations. The ability to work individually as well as effectively in a team Fluency in written and spoken English This Is What We Offer You A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3,204 to € 4,051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD Candidate is applicable.. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable. We also have an extensive secondary benefits package. Your place at the UvA You will work in this team The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain. The mission of the Informatics Institute (IvI) is to perform curiosity-driven and use-inspired fundamental research in Computer Science. The main research themes are Artificial Intelligence, Computational Science and Systems and Network Engineering. Our research involves complex information systems at large, with a focus on collaborative, data driven, computational and intelligent systems, all with a strong interactive component. The Complex Cyber Infrastructure (CCI) group is part of the Informatics Institute at the University of Amsterdam. CCI focuses on the complexity of human-made systems on all scales. Cyber Infrastructure is rapidly evolving from relatively simple fixed components to programmable and virtualized objects with many degrees of freedom, owned, operated and governed by different entities in multiple administrative domains interacting on the Internet. Harnessing this complexity in a transparent, trustable way for safe and secure data processing is a major research topic that defines the focus of CCI research. The challenges are addressed by combining methods and results from research into sustainable and sovereign distributed data processing, programmable networks, policy reasoning and normative control, and software (language) engineering. Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam. About The Faculty Of Science Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, whether it concerns elementary particles, the birth of the universe, or how the brain functions. linkedin:4481203114.title: PhD Position in Foil Drone
linkedin:4481203114.desc: Pioneering the future of maritime surveillance? Join as a PHD to research and advance autonomous, wind-powered drones, featuring tethered hydrofoils for indefinite ocean monitoring. Job Description Are you ready to shape the future of autonomous maritime security? We are looking for a highly motivated and talented PhD Candidate to spearhead advanced research on the FoilDrone system—an innovative, future-proof maritime surveillance concept. Project Context & Mission Maritime domain awareness is a critical global priority. Traditional surveillance options face major trade-offs: airborne drones offer high speed but suffer from critically low endurance (6 to 22 hours), while unmanned surface vessels (like the Saildrone) boast long endurance but travel at very low speeds (3 to 5 knots) and cannot see over the horizon. The FoilDrone system bridges this market gap by combining an aerial Vertical Take-Off and Landing (VTOL) rotating-wing sailplane with a submerged, tethered hydrofoil. completely eliminating propulsion power consumption during operations. Key Responsibilities & Research Focus As a PhD candidate, you will take ownership of the next phase of FoilDrone research. You will take the design from conceptual idea towards physical implementation through independent research, simulation and experimentation. Your core duties will include: Advanced Multi-Body Dynamics & Control: Deepen and expand simulation models linking the aerial vehicle to the submerged hydrofoil via a flexible tether. Refine independent controllers to ensure stability during critical transitions (transit, deployment, sailing, and recovery). Aerodynamic & Hydrodynamic Optimization: Investigate the complex interactions of fixed wing drone, cabels, and hydrofoils. Optimize aerodynamic and hydrodynamic efficiencies across varying sea states and wind disturbances. Experimental Validation: Translate theoretical models into physical hardware. Collaborate with technical staff and student teams to design wind-tunnel experiments, tow-tank tests, and open-water flight trials to validate structural integrity, deployment mechanisms, and control strategies. Academic Contribution: Publish high-impact scientific papers in leading international journals, present findings at global aerospace and marine conferences, and assist in supervising Master's and Bachelor's student thesis projects. What We Offer A fully funded, multi-year PhD position within a world-leading aerospace research environment. Access to state-of-the-art simulation tools, testing facilities, and prototyping equipment. Opportunities to collaborate closely with pioneers in UAV technology, maritime sensors, and renewable energy systems. A vibrant, international, and inspiring workplace dedicated to creating innovative drone solutions that work in the real world. If you are eager to push the boundaries of aerial-marine robotics and make a tangible impact on global maritime safety, we invite you to submit your application Job Requirements Educational Background: Hold a Master of Science degree in Aerospace Engineering, Robotics, Control Systems, or a closely related discipline. Technical Expertise: Strong background in flight dynamics, multi-body system modeling, guidance, navigation, and control (GNC). Simulation Skills: Demonstrated proficiency in numerical simulation environments (such as MATLAB/Simulink, Python) for aerial or underwater systems. Research Drive: Passion for academic research, experimental verification, and autonomous systems, with a proven ability to publish findings in peer-reviewed journals. Collaboration & Communication: Excellent English written and verbal communication skills, with a collaborative mindset to work alongside interdisciplinary academic and industrial partners. Practical Experience: Demonstrated hands-on experience in building, assembling, or maintaining (fixed-wing) unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and/or marine hydrofoil systems, including composite manufacturing and mechanical integration. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Our support and scientific staff, including PhD candidates, postdocs, and students, largely work together on three main themes: the energy transition, sustainable aerospace, and safety and security, with the aim of tackling climate change and contributing to the independence and security of Europe. When you join us, you become part of a diverse, collaborative, and forward-thinking environment where your ideas and perspectives are valued. Our work extends beyond the lab—into field labs, innovation hubs, and partnerships with other faculties, research institutes, governments, and industry, both locally and globally. International applicants are eligible to apply, with international tuition Preferred Education Master Application deadline 6 January 2027 Posted 19 October 2026 Job Description PROJECT HIGHLIGHTS Work directly with the UK Met Office on next-generation operational pollen forecasting Develop novel AI and machine-learning methods to predict pollen season magnitude months in advance Join an interdisciplinary team spanning environmental science, mathematics and artificial intelligence Overview Understanding and forecasting airborne pollen is essential for improving operational environmental prediction across the UK. While daily pollen forecasts have improved substantially in recent years, one of the greatest remaining challenges is predicting the overall magnitude of each pollen season. For example, total birch pollen concentrations can vary by a factor of eight between consecutive years, driven by complex interactions between previous-season pollen production, meteorological conditions during the preceding summer, and weather during the flowering season itself. These processes remain poorly understood and are not currently represented within operational forecasting systems. This project will harness a unique UK-wide pollen reanalysis (2000–2025), developed by the UK Met Office under the stewardship of Co-I Lucy Neal, together with long-term pollen observations and meteorological datasets, to develop next-generation machine learning approaches for predicting seasonal pollen magnitude. The resulting models will improve understanding of the environmental drivers of interannual variability while providing practical tools to enhance the operational Met Office NAME pollen forecast. With only 8 active regulatory-grade pollen monitoring sites across the UK, equivalent to approximately one site per eight million people, long-term pollen observations are extremely sparse. The pollen reanalysis provides an unprecedented spatially and temporally complete dataset for developing and validating artificial intelligence methods. The student will investigate how biological memory, antecedent weather conditions and environmental variables combine to determine pollen production, developing interpretable machine learning models capable of predicting seasonal severity months in advance. This PhD will be embedded in a vibrant interdisciplinary research environment at the University of Birmingham, combining expertise in environmental science, artificial intelligence and applied mathematics. Joint supervision from Environmental Sciences, the School of Mathematics, and the UK Met Office will provide outstanding training in machine learning, environmental modelling and operational forecasting. The research will directly address a major limitation in current pollen forecasting systems, delivering new scientific understanding alongside AI tools with clear operational impact for the UK Met Office and wider environmental forecasting community. linkedin:4478618248.desc: Temporary contract | 14+22(+12) months | Belval Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a Research and Technology Organization (RTO) active in the fields of materials, environment and IT. By transforming scientific knowledge into technologies, smart data and tools, LIST empowers citizens in their choices, public authorities in their decisions and businesses in their strategies. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/ How will you contribute? You will be part of the LIST Materials Research and Technology department, where you will carry out your work in the Quantum Materials Group, led by Dr. Florian Kaiser. Quantum technologies have the potential to revolutionise the world in many aspects. Quantum colour centres in in wide bandgap semiconductors have recently emerged as a promising platform, since they can incorporate quantum systems, which can be scaled up by industrial processing. Along these lines, we have recently shown that individual colour centres can be integrated into silicon carbide nanophotonic waveguides with little-to-no degradation of spin-optical coherences. These finding define the strategy for developing a scalable quantum technology architecture. Our strategy is to use multiplexed and integrated colour centres for quantum communication tasks. Key here is to generate entanglement between colour centres based on spin-photon entanglement, as well as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. With this milestone demonstration, we strive to kickstart subsequent developments towards a quantum internet architecture. The objective of this PhD thesis is to support our work towards optical interference between colour centres, i.e., Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. The initial part of this thesis comprises setting up our new optical cryostat platform, which is based on a combination of standard confocal microscopy, and interferometry. In the second step, you will benefit from our ongoing activities towards quantum photonic silicon carbide chips in which we generate colour centres in fibre-coupled waveguides. You will determine the ideal pulsed excitation schemes for colour centres, considering spectral, temporal and polarization filtering. Subsequently, you will characterise the photon quality depending on experimental parameters, and implement initial two-photon inteference experiments outside of the cryostat, followed by a fully-on-chip demonstration inside the cryostat. If time permits, this project can be further extended to the generation of entanglement between two colour centre chips located in two different cryostats. Is Your profile described below? linkedin:4480265095.desc: About The Position A fully-funded PhD position in modelling marine larval dispersal and spatial population genetics and demography is available at the Department of Biology, Norwegian University of Science & Technology (NTNU) under the supervision of Associate Professor Scott Burgess. NTNU’s Department of Biology hosts internationally leading research activity in ecology, evolutionary biology, physiology, marine science and technology, and cell & molecular biology. As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia. About The Project The PhD position is aligned with a research program that has the overall aim of providing new understanding of the processes that affect marine larval dispersal and gene flow, how we measure it with genetic data, and how we use that information to predict the genetic and demographic responses of spatially structured marine populations to environmental variation and change. Specifically, the primary focus of the PhD will be to understand how complex coastlines, ocean circulation, and biology (e.g., reproductive systems and phenology, larval behavior and survival) interact to affect the spatial structure of the genetic and demographic properties of marine populations. There is flexibility, and an expectation, for candidates to develop their own line of research within this broad scope. For example, projects could focus on combining simulations using spatial-genetic-demographic individual based models (e.g., using the software SLiM), machine learning approaches, and genomic data to estimate larval dispersal distances from the spatial structure of genetic genealogies across the genome, and the genetic relatedness among individuals; or develop and use biophysical models (hydrodynamics + particle tracking) to understand the demographic and genetic dynamics of marine metapopulations and adaptation to environmental change. It will provide broad training in research skills, and will suit a candidate who is curious and is motivated to undertake high-level research to gain skills in computational methods and software tools to understand large, complex biological data. The position will be hosted within a dynamic international research group based at NTNU, with strong links to local and international collaborators. There will be opportunities for conference and workshop participation. The project supervisor will be Associate Professor Scott C. Burgess (Department of Biology, NTNU). linkedin:4473616098.desc: Main tasks Over the past decades, neuroscience has made remarkable progress in characterizing the architecture of biological neural networks. We now possess increasingly detailed descriptions of synaptic connectivity, cellular composition, laminar organization, mesoscale topology, and large-scale connectomes across multiple species. Across these diverse levels of organization, common structural principles have begun to emerge, including modularity, core-periphery organization, asymmetric reciprocity, and multi-scale network organization. Yet, despite this wealth of anatomical knowledge, a fundamental question remains unresolved: how do these structural features shape neural computation? Which aspects of biological connectivity are essential for flexible, robust, and adaptive information processing, and which are simply byproducts of development or evolution? This PhD project aims to bridge this gap by combining computational and network neuroscience with artificial intelligence to investigate how biologically inspired connectivity principles influence computation in recurrent neural networks. Research Environment The Institute of Computational Neuroscience is a small, active and internationally diverse group working at the interface of computational neuroscience, network science, neuro-inspired artificial intelligence and clinical neuroscience. The successful candidate will be jointly supervised by Prof. Claus C. Hilgetag and Dr. Fatemeh Hadaeghi. About The Project A central methodological framework will be recurrent neural networks and reservoir computing models. Our goal is to uncover how biological wiring and functional organization can inform artificial neural network design and to translate these insights into models that operate effectively with low-precision (binary or ternary) weights. Main Aims Are To Explore bio-inspired backbones for unimodal temporal learning Develop modular and core-periphery architectures for multimodal learning Explore Scalability and real-world application. The work will involve close interaction with a strong computational and network neuroscience team at our institute. The position provides substantial scope for scientific initiative and intellectual ownership. The successful candidate may also contribute to the development of related research proposals and future funding applications. The position is funded through third-party research funding, comprises 65% of the regular weekly working hours, and provides the opportunity for obtaining the academic qualification of a PhD. linkedin:4480247952.desc: About The Position Digitalization and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming society, and the integration of AI into the maritime industry represents a digital shift that will redefine today’s operations. The maritime industry is increasingly embracing AI, enabling a broad digital transformation. At the same time, the use of AI introduce new cybersecurity challenges that need to be understood and addressed to enable secure and trustworthy AI technology. This PhD project will investigate cybersecurity challenges associated with the development and use of AI in the maritime domain. The project will have an interdisciplinary approach, combining insights from information security, artificial intelligence, maritime operations, and data engineering. The research may address cybersecurity risks related to the data used to develop AI models, the models themselves, or their integration and use in maritime applications. Relevant research topics may include cybersecurity risks related to training data and AI models, data poisoning and manipulation, privacy and confidentiality, secure data sharing, and methods for assessing the security and trustworthiness of maritime AI technology. The specific research questions and methodological approach will be further developed based on the candidate’s background and interests, relevant maritime AI use cases, and collaboration with industry partners. This position offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of cybersecurity, AI, and maritime operations in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners. The research is expected to contribute new knowledge and approaches for understanding and addressing cybersecurity challenges associated with the development and use of AI in the maritime domain. linkedin:4480984531.title: PhD Position – Linking Above-Ground Plant Function to Root Dynamics
linkedin:4480984531.desc: Plant roots are essential for water and nutrient acquisition and play a key role in how crops respond to environmental stress. Yet, because roots are hidden in the soil, their development and activity remain difficult to observe – particularly under field conditions. Advances in plant phenotyping, on the other hand, allow us to characterize above- and belowground plant structure and function with increasing temporal resolution. Physiological measurements provide information about photosynthetic carbon assimilation, while sensor-based phenotyping captures dynamic changes in plant growth and stress responses. To what extent can available above-ground traits be related to root structure and function? At the Institute of Bio- and Geosciences – Plant Sciences (IBG-2) at Forschungszentrum Jülich, we are looking for a doctoral researcher to address this question within the PhenoRob – Robotics and Phenotyping for Sustainable Crop Production – research environment. Your Job The aim of your PhD project is to relate root dynamics to above-ground physiological and phenotypical measures and traits. You will investigate how photosynthesis, carbon allocation, shoot development and root growth are connected over time and how these relationships change in response to environmental conditions. To achieve this, you will combine experiments done under controlled conditions with field experiments. Complementary experiments will provide direct and non-invasive information about shoot and root structure and function. Using advanced imaging approaches such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Positron Emission Tomography (PET), you will follow root development and physiological processes over space and time. Together with measurements of photosynthetic performance, these experiments will help reveal how carbon assimilation and allocation are related to source-sink dynamics and subsequent root and shoot growth. By combining these complementary datasets, you will investigate whether measurable changes above ground can serve as indicators – and ultimately predictors – of dynamic processes in the hidden root system. Your tasks will include: Design and conduct plant experiments under controlled and field conditions Quantify temporal changes in plant structure and function using non-invasive approaches Investigate relationships between photosynthetic carbon assimilation, carbon allocation, and subsequent root and shoot growth Develop quantitative approaches to relate root development and stress responses to above-ground measurements Contribute experimental data to the parameterisation and validation of functional-structural plant models Present your results at international conferences and publish them in peer-reviewed scientific journals The project will be highly collaborative and will connect expertise in plant physiology, root biology, phenotyping, sensing, imaging, data analysis and plant modelling within IBG-2 and the interdisciplinary PhenoRob research environment. Your Profile We are looking for a highly motivated candidate who combines scientific curiosity with an interest in experimental and quantitative plant science. Excellent Master's degree in plant sciences, biology, agricultural sciences, crop science, environmental sciences, bioengineering or a related discipline Motivation to combine controlled experiments with field-based plant research Interest in linking physiological processes with imaging and sensor-derived plant traits Experience in quantitative data analysis and statistics Experience with R, Python or comparable tools is advantageous Very good command of written and spoken English is required (at least B2 level according to the CEFR ), ideally supported by a certificate confirming the language level Experience with photosynthesis measurements, root phenotyping, plant imaging, MRI, PET, field phenotyping, remote sensing, image analysis, machine learning or plant modelling is an advantage, but not a prerequisite. Our Benefits for You Team & Environment: You will work in a motivated team with an international and interdisciplinary focus – at one of the largest research institutions in Europe Research & Infrastructure: You will have access to excellent scientific and technical facilities for your work Networking & Exchange: You will participate in (international) conferences and project meetings and actively build your scientific network Supervision & Support: We will accompany your doctoral studies with continuous, expert guidance from your academic supervisor Work-life balance: We offer flexible working hours to help you balance your professional and personal life. You also have the option of flexible working (in terms of location), which is generally possible after consultation and in line with upcoming tasks and (on-site) appointments Annual Leave: You get 30 days of annual leave Knowledge & Development: Your professional development is important to us – we support you specifically and individually e.g., through training and networking opportunities specifically for doctoral candidates (JuDocS) Successful start: It is important to us that you quickly settle into the team and are given structured training for your tasks. We also support you from the very beginning and make your start easier with our Welcome Days and Welcome Guide Support for international employees: Our International Advisory Service makes it easier for international employees to get started In addition to exciting tasks and a collegial working environment, we offer you much more: https://go.fzj.de/benefits We welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds, e.g. in terms of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation / identity, and social, ethnic and religious origin. A diverse and inclusive working environment with equal opportunities in which everyone can realize their potential is important to us. linkedin:4474319446.title: PhD Position in Decoding Environmental History from Microorganisms for Living Sensors and Memory
linkedin:4474319446.desc: Help pave the future for living sensing systems by decoding microorganisms' encoding of environmental history. Job Description Background: Living microorganisms could transform how we sense and store information, replacing single-use electronics with inherently biodegradable systems that track environmental conditions over time. Even basic electronic sensing systems today require sensors, microcontrollers, memory, and batteries, and are often disposable. For example, temperature and humidity dataloggers used during food and vaccine transport become e-waste within weeks. Meanwhile, many species of microorganisms, such as the iridescent Flavobacteria, integrate environmental signals and store history structurally, all with minimal energy. Readout may be as simple as taking a photograph. Could these organisms replace conventional electronics and enable fully degradable, battery-less dataloggers? What's missing in realizing this future is our ability to interpret this biological record: we do not yet understand what the visual characteristics of organisms represent quantitatively, or how reliably we can recover that information. This PhD: We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to play a formative role in understanding how to decode environmental information from living microorganisms, in pursuit of living sensing and memory systems. This effort is truly trans-disciplinary, drawing on biodesign/biotechnology, machine learning, and interaction design. This project builds on groundwork already underway in our group but is meant to be shaped substantially by the candidate's own interests and expertise. The candidate will cultivate the living organism itself, characterize and model its visible responses to different environmental conditions, and develop and validate computational decoders that recover environmental history from an image of the living organism. Based on the found capabilities, the candidate will also design prototypes that incorporate living sensors, such as fully compostable, smart packaging for temperature and humidity monitoring for food, vaccines, or archival documents. The PhD candidate will be situated at the intersection of the Knowledge and Intelligent Design group and the Materializing Futures group in Sustainable Design Engineering (SDE), a department within the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering. Job Requirements We look for candidates who have: A Master's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Biodesign, Design Engineering, or a related field Experience in building and deploying machine learning or computer vision models Technical competencies in one or more of the following: bio-digital systems, biodesign, applied machine learning, computer vision, computational biology, and/or physical prototyping Experience or strong interest in biodesign and hands-on interaction with living organisms Experience or interest in conducting research with sound experimental design Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team, communicate effectively, and take initiative Prior publications and experience presenting at international conferences are assets but not requirements Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Industrial Design Engineering Matching the evolution of people with the speed of the revolution of technology. This is the focus of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering (IDE). Delft designers act as a bridge between advances in technology and the needs of people, organisations and society to create products, services and systems with purpose. IDE is a leader in design research across the application areas of mobility, sustainability and health, as well as its development of design tools and methods. A 350-strong research team and over 2,000 students work together in our inspiring hall, labs and studios. In close cooperation with industry, the public sector and NGOs we rehearse possible futures in research and education to design for a complex future. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , increasing from Promovendus gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information For more information about this vacancy, please contact Dr. Katherine Song, e-mail: k.w.song@tudelft.nl Application procedure Apply via the application button before 15 November 2026. Upload your CV and cover letter. Please do not submit AI-generated (or heavily doctored) content. For information about the application procedure, please contact Ioanna Charalampous, e-mail: secretariaat-SDE-HR@tudelft.nl Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

linkedin:4480934758.desc: The Energy Informatics lab at Technische Universität Clausthal solicits expressions of interest for a doctoral researcher (PhD student) position. The position is on-site in Clausthal-Zellerfeld (Germany), full-time, remunerated up to TV-L E13, and offered for an initial duration up until 31 December 2028 with the possibility of a later contract extension. The position is part of the project " Innovative integrated energy concepts for rural areas (INITIAL) ," in which seven departments at four universities work towards the goal of creating and integrating simulation models for generation and demand in energy parks (featuring generators, consumers, and storages for electricity, hydrogen, and/or heat). The overall goal is to find the most grid-friendly operation mode for a given set of integrated components, while fostering acceptance by the general public at the same time. linkedin:4477500750.title: Doctoral Researcher (PhD) in Protein Synthesis
linkedin:4477500750.desc: A fully funded PhD position is available to study protein synthesis in the lab of Sarah O’Keefe at the Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences, University of Helsinki, Finland. About The Position We invite applications for a doctoral researcher position at the Viikki Campus in Helsinki, Finland. The doctoral researcher will work in the project Inhibiting Protein Synthesis – Old, New, Borrowed, Blue , funded by the Research Council of Finland. The doctoral researcher will be supervised by the Principal Investigator Sarah O’Keefe and co-supervised by Brendan Battersby. The successful candidate will complete an article-based PhD thesis and 30 ECTS credits of studies that are required for a PhD degree in Finland. The position is available and funded for 44 months from January 2027 , or as agreed. Project Description Proteins are key working molecules in all cells and their synthesis is an elaborate jigsaw puzzle. The early stages of protein synthesis include translation on ribosomes and the translocation of new polypeptides across, and their insertion into, membranes via translocons or insertases. New mechanistic insights are rapidly revolutionising our textbook models and bringing previously ‘undruggable’ protein synthesis machineries to the forefront of drug development. This doctoral project combines cellular and chemical biology, cell-free protein synthesis, cryoEM, gene editing and orthogonal high-throughput screening to discover breakthrough protein synthesis inhibitors and re-purpose existing ones. By expanding the chemical and biological space of protein synthesis and its inhibition, this research will develop new tools to probe how proteins are made and unlock new ways to treat human diseases. Why Work for Us? A collaborative, innovative and inclusive research environment. Training in cell culture, cell free protein synthesis, cryoEM, gene editing, high throughput screening, molecular biology, protein expression and purification, presenting, project management and writing. Access to cutting-edge infrastructures, including working closely the local cryoEM Unit, High Throughput Biomedicine Unit and Finnish Genome Editing Centre. International collaboration with Chemists and Computational Physicists (US, Japan and Finland). International mobility including conference attendance and short-term research visits at the University of Leeds (UK) to use new approaches for cryoEM sample preparation. As the first doctoral researcher in the lab, you will benefit from close, individualised mentorship and hands-on training from the Principal Investigator. You will also play a foundational role in shaping the lab’s core culture and scientific techniques as it grows. About The O’Keefe Lab We integrate biochemistry, cell biology, cryoEM and small molecules to unlock new mechanisms, methods and drug candidates of protein synthesis for the benefit of human health. To date, the Principal Investigator has discovered new protein synthesis inhibitors with anti-infective (bacteria, viruses, parasites) and anti-cancer utility, identified new mechanisms of protein biogenesis and visualised protein synthesis in action using cryoEM. Our research is highly interdisciplinary, drawing upon the Principal Investigator’s diverse career path in Medicinal Chemistry, Biochemistry and Cellular and Structural Biology in academic and industry settings. Supported by our collaborative network, we are committed to training and equipping lab members with the multidisciplinary skills needed to take their next career step. Selection Criteria You are ambitious, collegial, proactive and motivated to pursue multidisciplinary science research. You should have a Master’s degree (or be due to complete before the start date) in biology, biological sciences, biochemistry, pharmacy or another relevant field, including medicinal chemists with strong research experience and a commitment to switch fields. Competencies in cell culture, molecular biology, protein purification/expression and cryoEM will be learned during the project. Excellent written and spoken communication skills in English. The ability to work independently, problem solve, master new skills and work in a collaborative team. Merited criteria: research experience in industry or a research-intensive academic lab or knowledge of the protein synthesis field. The successful applicant will receive support in applying for the right to pursue a doctoral degree at the University of Helsinki, which should be obtained within the six-month probationary period. Salary and working hours The position is currently funded for a maximum of 44 months (3 years and 8 months, if commenced in January 2027). The starting gross monthly salary for a doctoral researcher is around 2500-2700 EUR and is based on job demand level 2 in the salary system for teaching and research personnel of Finnish Universities. The salary depends on the appointee’s qualifications and stage of doctoral studies and includes a personal performance component. The doctoral researcher should reside in Finland while employed by the University of Helsinki. The University assists employees from abroad with their transition to work and life in Finland. Finland is a member of the European Union, has high-quality free schooling (also in English), generous family benefits and healthcare. Helsinki offers an outstanding quality of life and Finland is consistently ranked among the world’s best countries for safety, work-life balance, education and family-friendliness. linkedin:4480264603.desc: Temporary contract | 14+22(+12) months | Belval Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a Research and Technology Organization (RTO) active in the fields of materials, environment and IT. By transforming scientific knowledge into technologies, smart data and tools, LIST empowers citizens in their choices, public authorities in their decisions and businesses in their strategies. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/ How will you contribute? You will be part of the LIST Materials Research and Technology department, where you will carry out your work in the Quantum Materials Group, led by Dr. Florian Kaiser. Quantum technologies have the potential to revolutionise the world in many aspects. Quantum colour centres in in wide bandgap semiconductors have recently emerged as a promising platform, since they can incorporate quantum systems, which can be scaled up by industrial processing. Along these lines, we have recently shown that individual colour centres can be integrated into silicon carbide nanophotonic waveguides with little-to-no degradation of spin-optical coherences. These finding define the strategy for developing a scalable quantum technology architecture. Our strategy is to use multiplexed and integrated colour centres for quantum communication tasks. Key here is to generate entanglement between colour centres based on spin-photon entanglement, as well as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. With this milestone demonstration, we strive to kickstart subsequent developments towards a quantum internet architecture. The objective of this PhD thesis is to support our work towards optical interference between colour centres, i.e., Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. The initial part of this thesis comprises setting up our new optical cryostat platform, which is based on a combination of standard confocal microscopy, and interferometry. In the second step, you will benefit from our ongoing activities towards quantum photonic silicon carbide chips in which we generate colour centres in fibre-coupled waveguides. You will determine the ideal pulsed excitation schemes for colour centres, considering spectral, temporal and polarization filtering. Subsequently, you will characterise the photon quality depending on experimental parameters, and implement initial two-photon inteference experiments outside of the cryostat, followed by a fully-on-chip demonstration inside the cryostat. If time permits, this project can be further extended to the generation of entanglement between two colour centre chips located in two different cryostats. Is Your profile described below? linkedin:4480985033.desc: Join the leader in entertainment innovation and help us design the future. At Dolby, science meets art, and high tech means more than computer code. As a member of the Dolby team, you’ll see and hear the results of your work everywhere, from movie theaters to smartphones. We continue to revolutionize how people create, deliver, and enjoy entertainment worldwide. To do that, we need the absolute best talent. We’re big enough to give you all the resources you need, and small enough so you can make a real difference and earn recognition for your work. We offer a collegial culture, challenging projects, and excellent compensation and benefits, not to mention a Flex Work approach that is truly flexible to support where, when, and how you do your best work. Internship: Development and On-Device Deployment of an Autoregressive Model for Real-Time Speech Restoration and Dialog Enhancement Start: Open Duration: 3 months (full-time) or 6 months (part-time) Location: Stockholm Speech restoration and dialog enhancement are critical components in modern audio experiences, especially in noisy environments or legacy content with degraded quality. Current systems often rely on non-causal, server-side models that require full audio context, limiting their use in real-time or on-device applications. With recent advances in autoregressive language modeling and efficient deep learning deployment, there is growing potential to develop low-latency, high-quality speech enhancement systems that operate in real time and even on consumer devices. This internship aims to design and implement an autoregressive, large language model (LLM)-based architecture for speech restoration and dialog enhancement. The model will be trained to reconstruct clean speech from degraded inputs by leveraging both acoustic and linguistic context. It will be evaluated against Dolby’s current best multimodal system, focusing on perceptual quality, intelligibility, and latency. A key objective is to explore the feasibility of deploying the model on-device through techniques such as model compression, quantization, pruning, and compilation using modern inference frameworks. Candidate Requirements Master’s or Ph.D. student in Machine Learning, Signal Processing, Computer Science, or a related field. Hands-on experience with PyTorch. Interest in model optimization for edge deployment using tools such as Triton Inference Server, ONNX, TensorRT, or similar frameworks. Prior experience in this field is a plus. Experience fine-tuning LLMs is a plus. Knowledge of audio-language modeling is a plus. Dolby Hiring Entity: Gävlegatan 12A 113 30 Stockholm, Sweden
