indeed:0391bb84f0417973.title: PhD in Art-Science-Action Integration & Challenge-Based Sustainability Education
indeed:0391bb84f0417973.desc: The Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development at Utrecht University invites applications for a PhD position on the role of art-science-action integration and challenge-based learning towards transformative sustainability education. Your job The PhD candidate will investigate how higher education can prepare students to have meaningful contributions in complex sustainability challenges. Specifically, the PhD candidate will study how the integration of academic knowledge, the skills to make academic knowledge actionable in these complex challenges, and the use of artistic expressions can strengthen students’ professional impact. A specific focus in the research lies on challenge-based learning environments, in which students from different disciplinary backgrounds work with educators, artists and societal partners on real-world sustainability issues. Situated at the intersection of sustainability education, transformative learning, challenge-based learning and arts-based interventions, the project combines scientific ambitions with the wish of the research having impact within Utrecht University and beyond. It aims to advance knowledge on transformative sustainability education while contributing to the development of effective and inclusive educational practices. Your role and research As a PhD candidate, you will develop and carry out an independent research programme within a broader project. Together with an interdisciplinary supervisory team and a range of academic and societal partners, you will explore how knowledge, skills and artistic expression can be combined to support sustainability learning and help students engage with complex sustainability challenges. Your research may address questions such as: How can artistic practices contribute to cognitive, affective and action-oriented sustainability learning? How can challenge-based education connect disciplinary knowledge with the experiences and priorities of societal partners? What opportunities and tensions arise when artists, scientists, educators and societal actors collaborate? How can skills be taught so that they enable action in practice? What are the (educational or institutional) conditions that enable art-science collaborations that can have a real impact on student learning? Your work will include designing and conducting empirical research in higher-education settings, analysing qualitative and/or quantitative data, and translating findings into both academic and practical outputs. Possible methods include interviews, surveys, observations, focus groups and the analysis of student work. The precise research questions and methodological approach will be developed together with the supervisory team. You will also contribute to the evaluation and further development of sustainability skills and challenge-based courses, and help strengthen collaboration between educators, students, artists and societal partners. You will have opportunities to share your findings at conferences and workshops and to publish in international peer-reviewed journals. As part of the Copernicus Institute research community, you will also participate in relevant doctoral training activities. Your qualities We are looking for a curious, motivated and collaborative researcher with a strong interest in the role of higher education in sustainability transformation. You have: a completed Master’s degree in sustainability science, environmental sciences, educational sciences, social sciences, governance, transformation studies, arts-based research, or a related field; a clear interest in sustainability education, transformative learning, challenge-based learning, art-science collaboration or related topics; strong analytical, academic writing and communication skills; experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research methods; the ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary environment. Experience with educational research, stakeholder engagement, arts-based methods or mixed-methods research is an advantage, but is not required. Being able to collect data (using interviews or surveys) using the Dutch language is also an advantage. We welcome applicants with diverse disciplinary and professional backgrounds who can demonstrate a strong fit with the research topic. Our offer You will join the Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development, an interdisciplinary research environment addressing urgent sustainability challenges through research, education and societal engagement. You will receive supervision from an interdisciplinary team and have opportunities to participate in doctoral training, seminars, conferences and international research networks. We offer a position (0.8 - 1.0 FTE) for 1 year, with an extension to a total of four years upon a successful assessment in the first year, and with the specific intent that it results in a doctorate within this period; a working week of 32 - 40 hours and a gross monthly salary between €3.204 and €4.051 (salary scale P under the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO NU)). The salary is based on a 38-hour working week; 8% holiday pay and 8.3% year-end bonus; a pension scheme, partially paid parental leave and flexible terms of employment based on the CAO NU. In addition to the terms of employment set out in our collective labour agreement, we offer attractive additional benefits, including opportunities for personal and professional growth, flexible leave arrangements, and extra vacation days. Through the UU Terms of Employment Options Model, you can tailor your employment package to your needs. In this way, we encourage you to grow in what you do, both in your work and in your development. Read more about our terms of employment. About us A better future for everyone. This ambition motivates our scientists in executing their leading research and inspiring teaching. At Utrecht University, the various disciplines collaborate intensively towards major strategic themes. Our focus is on Dynamics of Youth, Institutions for Open Societies, Life Sciences and Pathways to Sustainability. Sharing science, shaping tomorrow. Utrecht University’s Faculty of Geosciences studies the Earth: from the Earth’s core to its surface, including man’s spatial and material utilisation of the Earth – always with a focus on sustainability and innovation. With 3,400 students (BSc and MSc) and 720 staff, the faculty is a strong and challenging organisation. The Faculty of Geosciences is organised in four Departments: Earth Sciences, Human Geography & Spatial Planning, Physical Geography, and Sustainable Development. The Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development (Department of Sustainable Development) is a vibrant international research community that aims to help accelerate the transition to a sustainable society. We do this by developing excellent and relevant knowledge, collaborating with citizens, politicians, policymakers, NGOs and firms to learn from each other and influence decision-making, and by educating the change agents of the future. Formally, we are organized as one of four departments of Utrecht University’s Faculty of Geosciences. We occupy a unique position as an interdisciplinary natural/social sciences department. While we are the only department at Utrecht University that solely focuses on sustainability research, it is a key topic for Utrecht University in general. Notably, the Strategic Theme Pathways to Sustainability strengthens our collaboration with many other groups across the university. We also actively contribute to the Strategic Theme Institutions for Open Societies, bringing in our research on the role of institutions and institutional change in understanding transformations to sustainability. We were formed in 2003 as the Department of Innovation, Environmental and Energy Sciences (IMEW), bringing together the Environmental Governance, Environmental Sciences and Innovation Studies sections. In 2012, the Science, Technology and Society section joined us from the Faculty of Science, forming what is now known as the Energy & Resources section. In 2021 the Urban Futures Studio became our fifth research section. This position will be part of the Energy & Resources section. More information For more information, please contact Karin Rebel via k.t.rebel@uu.nl. Candidates for this vacancy will be recruited by Utrecht University. Apply now At Utrecht University, we strive to be a place where everyone feels at home. We value colleagues with different backgrounds, perspectives and identities, including differences in culture, religion or ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability and age. We are committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and contribute. Read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion. If you have any questions about accessibility, for example regarding your workplace Vening Meineszgebouw A, the application process or your work, please contact us via our HR contact page. Please submit your application through the Utrecht University application portal. Interviews are planned on November 27th and December 11th. We especially encourage applications from candidates who are eager to work across disciplinary boundaries and to connect academic research with educational innovation and societal change.

linkedin:4480410154.desc: 19.10.2026, Academic staff Der Lehrstuhl für Fahrzeugtechnik sucht ab 1.10.2026 wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiter (m/w/d) aus Informatik, Robotik oder Ingenieurwissenschaften zur Promotion im Bereich Multi-Stack-Handling und hybride Sicherheitsarchitektur für autonome Fahrzeuge. Hintergrund Autonome Fahrzeuge werden zunehmend nicht mehr nur mit einem einzelnen Softwarestack betrieben: Neben klassischen modularen AV-Stacks etablieren sich End-to-End-Ansätze, die auf gelernten, integrierten Modellen basieren. Beide Paradigmen haben unterschiedliche Stärken und Schwächen. Während ein modularer Stack Nachvollziehbarkeit und etablierte Sicherheitsnachweise bietet, punktet ein End-to-End-Stack durch Flexibilität in komplexen, schwer modellierbaren Situationen. Statt sich auf einen einzelnen Stack festzulegen, erforschen wir, wie beide Ansätze redundant und parallel betrieben werden können, um die Robustheit autonomer Fahrzeuge im realen Betrieb zu erhöhen. Gestalte mit uns die hybride Fahrzeugarchitektur von morgen und forsche an spannenden Dissertationsthemen. Deine Herausforderungen Als Promovierender erforschst du, wie ein modularer AV-Stack und ein End-to-End-Stack als redundante, parallel betriebene Systeme in einer gemeinsamen Fahrzeugarchitektur integriert werden können. Im Zentrum steht die Frage, welcher Stack unter welchen Bedingungen die Steuerhoheit übernimmt: Du definierst Arbitrierungslogiken, mit denen Übergaben zwischen den Stacks initiiert, abgesichert und im Konfliktfall aufgelöst werden, und entwickelst Blending-Strategien, die einen fließenden Übergang zwischen modularem und E2E-Stack ermöglichen, beispielsweise wenn der modulare Stack an eine Situation stößt, die der E2E-Stack sicherer beherrscht. Darauf aufbauend erarbeitest du funktionale Sicherheitskonzepte in Anlehnung an SOTIF und ISO 26262 für diese hybride Architektur, die sowohl proprietäre als auch Open-Source-Softwareanteile berücksichtigen, und definierst Freigabeprozesse und Sicherheitsnachweise für den kombinierten Stack-Betrieb in Abstimmung mit Prüforganisationen und Behörden. Du entwickelst damit einen zentralen Baustein für die Sicherheit hybrider autonomer Fahrzeugarchitekturen. Dein Profil Sehr guter Masterabschluss in Informatik, Robotik, Ingenieurwissenschaften (1,x-Schnitt) an einer anerkannten Universität Erfahrung mit Autonomen Systemen und funktionaler Sicherheit Kommunikation und Organisation sind für dich selbstverständlich Deutsch und Englisch (mind. linkedin:4480280690.title: AstraZeneca-Funded Non-Clinical PhD Studentship (Fixed Term): Physics-Guided Representation Learning for Drug Discovery
linkedin:4480280690.desc: Applications are invited for a four-year, AstraZeneca-funded PhD studentship in the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics, commencing in October 2027. The successful candidate will be jointly supervised by Prof Sergio Bacallado (University of Cambridge), Dr Dino Oglic (AstraZeneca), and Dr Jon Paul Janet (AstraZeneca). The studentship offers an opportunity to conduct cutting-edge research at the interface of statistical machine learning, molecular simulation and drug discovery. Project description The project, entitled Physics-Guided Representation Learning from Free Energy Perturbation Data for Affinity Prediction and Candidate Down-Selection, aims to develop novel machine-learning methods for predicting molecular binding affinities and supporting decision-making in drug discovery. Free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations provide valuable information about how strongly candidate drug molecules bind to their biological targets, but these calculations are computationally expensive. This project will investigate how machine-learning models can extract richer information from FEP data and experimental measurements, combining physical principles with modern representation-learning techniques. The research will involve developing and evaluating new statistical and machine-learning methods, with access to both public benchmark datasets and AstraZeneca's industrial drug-discovery expertise and data. Candidate requirements Applicants should have, or expect to obtain, a first-class or upper second-class honours degree (or equivalent), normally following four years of university study. We welcome applicants with backgrounds in Mathematics, Statistics, Machine Learning, Scientific Computing, or any closely related discipline. Experience with computational chemistry would be desirable but is not essential. We particularly welcome applications from candidates with strong mathematical or machine-learning backgrounds who are interested in applying their expertise to problems in drug discovery. Funding The studentship provides funding for four years, covering a maintenance stipend and University tuition fees at the UK/Home rate. The studentship is open to candidates eligible for Home-fee status. International candidates may also be considered, provided that additional funding can be secured through scholarships or other approved funding schemes to cover the difference between Home and international tuition fees. This difference cannot be covered through student self-funding. Training and supervision The student will benefit from joint academic and industrial supervision, participating in the research activities of the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics and collaborating closely with AstraZeneca researchers to gain exposure to industrial applications of artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical development. How to apply Applications Must Be Submitted Through The University Of Cambridge Postgraduate Applicant Portal, Selecting The Course PhD In Pure Mathematics And Mathematical Statistics https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/mapmpdpms/apply Applicants should indicate Dr Sergio Bacallado as their proposed supervisor and use the following project title: Physics-Guided Representation Learning from Free Energy Perturbation Data for Affinity Prediction and Candidate Down-Selection. Applications should include the supporting documentation required by the University, including academic transcripts, a CV, two references, and the relevant research summary and reasons for applying. The deadline for applications is 6 January 2027 (23:59 UK time). Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview in January 2027. Informal enquiries about the project are welcome and may be addressed to Dr Sergio Bacallado at sb2116@cam.ac.uk. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

linkedin:4475594614.title: PhD Position Thermal Sensors based on Sigma-Delta Modulation
linkedin:4475594614.desc: Shape the future of sensor technology! Job Description We’re seeking a talented engineer to design next generation thermal sensors, such as flow sensors and temperature sensors, that are based on sigma-delta modulators. The key requirements for this position are a soild understanding of sensor physics, especially about heat transfer, and a solid background in analog circuit design. Only candidates with demonstrable experience in chip design will be considered, e.g. who have published in an IEEE conference/journal or have industrial experience in chip design. Job Requirements You hold an MSc degree in Electrical Engineering. You are an experienced chip designer. You have strong knowledge of analog and sensor-based systems. You can independently conduct experimental and simulation-based research. You have good communication skills and can write and present scientific results clearly. You are proficient in English, both written and spoken. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact Kofi Makinwa, via K.A.A.Makinwa@tudelf.nl. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 22 Oct 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: CV Motivational letter You can address your application to Kofi Makinwa. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Applying for an exemption for specific research and educational areas is an obligatory part of the selection procedure for this vacancy. This exemption must be obtained from the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (OCW) before an employment contract is agreed upon. Click here for more information. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services

linkedin:4481555330.title: PhD Position: Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation and Computational Affective Neuroscience
linkedin:4481555330.desc: Breadcrumb Home Working at Job opportunities PhD Position: Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation and Computational Affective Neuroscience PhD Position: Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation and Computational Affective Neuroscience Employment 0.8 - 1.0 FTE Gross monthly salary € 3,204 - € 4,051 Required background Research University Degree Organizational unit Faculty of Social Sciences Application deadline 09 November 2026 Apply now Are you passionate about affective neuroscience computational modelling and transcranial ultrasound stimulation? Come and join our PhD project on approach-avoidance decisions under threat, funded by the ERC Advanced Grant HEART2ADAPT, and work with a dynamic team. Why do some people remain calm and make flexible decisions under stress, while others freeze or flee? HEART2ADAPT aims to answer this question. We are developing a new model to understand how the body’s autonomic stress state shapes responses to threat and how the balance between sympathetic and parasympathetic activity supports adaptive decision making in dynamic environments. Using state-of-the-art methods to track brain and bodily signals in real time – such as heart rate, posture and advanced neuroimaging – we will investigate how stress influences decision-making. A key component of this specific PhD project is testing causal mechanisms using transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS), including both offline TUS and the development of MR-compatible online TUS. Funded by a European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant, the project HEART2ADAPT offers you the opportunity to contribute to protocol development, data collection and computational modelling of behavioural and neural data. You will apply TUS to key nodes of our model, including the amygdala, ventral striatum and dorsal ACC. You will work closely with colleagues at the Donders Institute and the Behavioural Science Institute, as well as with international collaborators. Responsibilities may also include mentoring of BSc and MSc students. Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate. A PhD track at Radboud University gives you room to follow your own interests and ambitions. Mustafa Akpinar PhD candidate at the Behavioural Science Institute and lecturer in Communication Science Mustafa Akpinar is a PhD candidate at the Behavioural Science Institute and a lecturer in Communication Science. "While studying at Radboud University, I was already teaching statistics. It started as just a side job, but I quickly discovered how much I enjoyed helping others learn. After graduating, I began working as a lecturer and researcher at a university of applied sciences. Still, that one dream kept nagging at me: pursuing a PhD. The thing is, most PhD programmes focus heavily on research, and teaching often comes second. I wanted to do both. Then a colleague pointed me to a PhD vacancy where research and teaching were given equal weight. I instantly knew: this is my chance. I really appreciate that Radboud University offers different types of PhD tracks. That way, there's room for a range of ambitions. Now, I study the relationship between culture and health communication, specifically within Turkish-Dutch communities. I mainly teach statistics and also coordinate a learning project on cultural communication practices. I can bring my own background into my teaching, as I’m a second-generation Turkish-Dutch person myself. What I also value is how Radboud University is becoming increasingly inclusive. For example, there was a lot of attention for Ramadan. We even celebrated Eid with colleagues! Things like that truly make a difference. I'm also a father, combining work with family life. That takes good planning. Fortunately, at Radboud University, I have the flexibility to shape my work in a way that fits my life. My supervisors trust that I’ll get my work done, even if I have to take my child to swimming lessons in the afternoon. That freedom gives me peace of mind." Does this sound like you? You have a Master’s degree in cognitive neuroscience or an adjacent field (psychology, biology, biomedical sciences, computer sciences, or other relevant MSc). You have a strong interest in fundamental research in cognitive and affective neurosciences and in computational psychiatry. You have experience with applying functional MRI (acquisition and analyses), including the use of Matlab, Python, SPM, FSL and/or other software tools, or you have experience with MEG (acquisition and analyses), including the use of Fieldtrip or similar. You have experience in non-invasive neuromodulation (preferably Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation) or are willing to master this technique. You have experience in the acquisition and analysis of peripheral psychophysiological data (e.g. autonomic nervous system measures). You have the capacity to participate in an interdisciplinary and translational research environment. You have interpersonal and communication skills to effectively collaborate and communicate in academia. You have a proactive and goal-directed attitude and good organisational skills. You are fluent in written and spoken English. Even if you do not meet all criteria, you are encouraged to apply if the role interests you. What we offer you We will give you a temporary employment contract (0.8 FTE 5- year contract - 1.0 FTE 4- year contract) of 1.5 years, after which your performance will be evaluated. If the evaluation is positive, your contract will be extended by 2.5 years (4-year contract) or 3.5 years (5-year contract). You will receive a starting salary of €3,204 gross per month based on a 38-hour working week, which will increase to €4,051 from the fourth year onwards (salary scale P). You will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8,3% end-of-year bonus. You will receive extra days off. With full-time employment, you can choose between 30 or 41 days of annual leave instead of the statutory 20. Additional employment conditions Work and science require good employment practices. Radboud University's primary and secondary employment conditions reflect this. You can make arrangements for the best possible work-life balance with flexible working hours, various leave arrangements and working from home. You are also able to compose part of your employment conditions yourself. For example, exchange income for extra leave days and receive a reimbursement for your sports membership. In addition, you receive a 34% discount on the sports and cultural activities at Radboud University as an employee. And, of course, we offer a good pension plan. We also give you plenty of room and responsibility to develop your talents and realise your ambitions. Therefore, we provide various training and development schemes. Where you will be working Your position will be embedded in the Affective Neuroscience group (link is external) led by Prof. Karin Roelofs at the Faculty of Social Sciences. You will be appointed by the Faculty's Behavioural Science Institute (BSI). You will be based at the Donders Centre for Cognitive Neuroimaging (DCCN) . You will also work closely with Lennart Verhagen’s group. Both BSI and DCCN are known for their successful graduate schools and strong dedication to open science and team science. Together, they create a warm, inclusive and cooperative research environment in which staff are well-supported in a work culture that promotes collaboration and respect. Behavioural Science Institute BSI is an interdisciplinary research institute where fundamental, applied and translational research takes place with the aim of understanding important societal issues and contributing to their solutions. BSI is one of the three research institutes of the Faculty of Social Sciences at Radboud University. Our researchers collaborate across the boundaries of psychology, communication science and pedagogical and educational science. Our mission for the coming years is to join forces in interdisciplinary research on the theme ’Empowering the Young’. We study the challenges that young people face in our current society and contribute to their empowerment. The institute provides excellent research facilities and has strong collaborations with non-academic partners. BSI has state-of-the-art research facilities for observational studies, experiments, eye-tracking studies, EEG measurements and GSR recording, psychobiological research, and behavioural measurements in both real and 3D virtual environments. The Donders Centre for Cognitive Neuroimaging The mission of this world class research centre is to conduct cutting-edge fundamental research in cognitive neuroscience. Much of the rapid progress in this field is being driven by the development of complex neuroimaging techniques for measuring activity in the human brain - an area in which the Centre plays a leading role. The research themes cover central cognitive functions such as perception, action, control, emotion, decision-making, attention, memory, language, learning and plasticity. The Centre also aims to establish how the different brain areas coordinate their activity with very high temporal precision to enable human and animal cognition. Our internationally renowned centre currently hosts more than 100 PhD candidates and postdoctoral researchers from more than 25 countries, offering a stimulating and multidisciplinary research environment. The centre is equipped with four MRI scanners (7T, 2x 3T), a 275-channel MEG system, an EEG-TMS/TUS laboratory, several (MR-compatible) EEG systems and high-performance computational facilities. Faculty of Social Sciences At the Faculty of Social Sciences, humanity and society are our focus; we study how people behave, think and feel. Within this context, we look at themes such as human behaviour and the human psyche, education and upbringing, communication, society and culture. The faculty provides education to 6,000 students and employs 700 staff. Education is organised into six programme clusters: Psychology; Artificial Intelligence; Pedagogical Sciences and Educational Sciences; Communication Science; Sociology; and Cultural Anthropology and Developmental Sociology, and the Radboud Centre Social Sciences as an institute for post-master education have been merged into the Social Sciences Education Institute. Our research is carried out within three research institutes: the Donders Centre for Cognition, the Behavioural Science Institute, and Radboud Social Cultural Research. Radboud University At Radboud University, we aim to make an impact through our work. We achieve this by conducting groundbreaking research, providing high-quality education, offering excellent support, and fostering collaborations within and outside the university. In doing so, we contribute indispensably to a healthy, free world with equal opportunities for all. To accomplish this, we need even more colleagues who, based on their expertise, are willing to search for answers. We advocate for an inclusive community and welcome employees with diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives. If you want to learn more about working at Radboud University, follow our Instagram account (link is external) and read stories from our colleagues. Is this the job for you? You can apply only via the button below. Address your letter of application to Karin Roelofs. In the application form, you will find which documents you need to include with your application. We look forward to receiving your application. The first interviews will take place on Thursday 26 November. Any second interview will take place on Thursday 10 December. You will preferably start your employment in January 2027. We can imagine you're curious about our application procedure. It describes what you can expect during the application procedure and how we handle your personal data and internal and external candidates. Apply now Application deadline 09 November 20

linkedin:4481564283.title: PhD Research Intern, 3D World Models
linkedin:4481564283.desc: SpAItial is pioneering the next generation of World Models, pushing the boundaries of generative AI, computer vision, and the simulation of reality. We are moving beyond 2D pixels to build models that natively understand the physics and geometry of our world. Our mission is to redefine how industries, from robotics and AR/VR to gaming and cinema, generate and interact with physically-grounded 3D environments. We're looking for bold, innovative individuals driven by a passion for pushing the boundaries of generative 3D AI. You should thrive in an environment where creativity meets technical challenge and be fearless in tackling the hardest problems in 3D world modeling. Our team is built on a foundation of dedication and a shared commitment to excellence, so we value people who take immense pride in their work and place the collective goals of the team above personal ambition. As a part of SpAItial, you'll be at the forefront of building World Models that bridge generative AI and the physical world. If you're ready to make an impact, embrace the unknown, and collaborate with a talented group of visionaries, we want to hear from you. We're seeking PhD Research Interns to work with our research team on open problems in 3D generation and reconstruction. You should have strong knowledge of at least one of our core areas, such as generative video and diffusion models, scene representations like Gaussian splats and radiance fields, or 3D reconstruction from per-scene optimization to feed-forward models. Over a 5-7 month internship, you will own a well-defined research question with the goal of publishing a paper. Responsibilities You will explore novel research directions in 3D generation, reconstruction, and world models. You will design, implement, and evaluate state-of-the-art methods, turning innovative research ideas into working systems and prototypes. You will be working closely with our research team. You will also present your findings and contribute to scientific publications targeting leading conferences in computer vision, computer graphics, and machine learning, such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, and ICLR. Key Qualifications Currently enrolled in the third year or beyond of a PhD in computer science, computer vision, computer graphics, machine learning, or a related field. 2-3 first-author papers at top-tier conferences such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, or ICLR. Knowledge of at least one of: generative models (diffusion or video models), neural scene representations, or 3D reconstruction. At SpAItial, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer and ensure all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.

indeed:913831d5901280ad.title: PhD Position in AI Methods for Participatory Design of Smart, Energy-Flexible Buildings
indeed:913831d5901280ad.desc: Offer UCLouvain is hiring a PhD Position in AI Methods for Participatory Design of Smart, Energy-Flexible Buildings Job Id : SF 38934 Internal and external job posting until the 30th of November 2026 For institute Louvain research institute for Landscape, Architecture, Built environment of Science and Technology Sector Main campus : Bruxelles (Saint-Gilles) Fixed-term, full-time contract, for 2 years Starting date : January 2027 Introduction We seek a dedicated and highly motivated PhD student to join the Architecture and Climate group at the Louvain research institute for Landscape, Architecture, Built environment (LAB), UCLouvain, based at the Brussels Saint-Gilles campus. We study multi-energy flows in and around buildings and districts through integrated passive and active systems. Our work ranges from prototyping experimental cyber-physical building systems with a focus on occupant well-being, through the development of coupled simulation, optimization and artificial intelligence models, to participatory digital tools that put this work in the hands of planners and decision makers. Our objective is to advance the renewable energy transition, as well as material and energy circularity, by tackling the gaps and barriers that currently stand in the way of a future climate-proof, sustainable built environment. The project Buildings are evolving from passive energy consumers into grid-interactive “prosumers” that generate, store, share and flexibly shift energy. Their uptake, however, is held back by technical, economic and social barriers, and by a lack of decision support tools that give non-experts, such as building owners and occupants, access to expertise from engineering (grid operation and multi-energy systems) and economics (multi-period financial optimization) to make informed decisions. This PhD will develop and test an AI-assisted recommender system for the participatory design of smart, energy-flexible buildings and energy communities. It will combine physics-informed machine learning surrogate models for building performance with energy system planning and operation models (demand response, local energy sharing, dynamic tariffs and grid emissions), and Large Language Models that provide reliable design guidance by retrieving validated knowledge (Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RAG) and by directly calling the simulation and optimization models as tools (agentic workflows, e.g. via the Model Context Protocol, MCP). The framework will be applied to a Belgian energy community case study and evaluated in co-creation workshops with real stakeholders. The objective is to understand real-world behavioral barriers relevant to sustainable building renovation and smart energy technologies, and to develop a decision support framework that addresses these barriers by empowering the stakeholders most affected by them: occupants and homeowners. Job description Review state-of-the-art ML-based surrogate models and AI recommender systems in building design Develop and integrate physics-informed ML models and a multi-energy hub into a common simulation suite (e.g. a browser-based platform) Design and prototype an LLM-based recommender system that combines RAG and agentic tool use (e.g. MCP) to query the simulation suite Organise and run participatory workshops, and analyse the results with qualitative and statistical methods Publish in international journals and present at conferences Contribute to teaching activities Required qualifications and skills Master’s degree in energy engineering, electrical engineering, energy economics, computer science, civil/building engineering, or a related field Strong interest in building energy, sustainable design and the energy transition Programming experience (e.g. Python, Julia, or other); experience with machine learning is a strong asset Familiarity with one or more of the following is a plus: building performance simulation; smart building technologies (e.g. heat pumps, PV, batteries, EV charging, home energy management systems); energy system modelling and optimization (e.g. linear/mixed-integer programming); power grids, demand response, flexibility markets or peer-to-peer energy trading; LLM frameworks (RAG, agents, tool use) Interest in interdisciplinary and participatory work with non-expert stakeholders Excellent command of English; French is an asset We offer A fully funded 2-year PhD position through a FSR doctoral scholarship for an initial period of 24 months. Progress will be reviewed during the doctoral programme and follow-up funding for additional 24 months will be sought jointly by the candidate and supervisor through relevant funding schemes. An interdisciplinary research environment at the intersection of architecture, energy and AI A network of academic and practice partners in Belgium and abroad Support for conference participation, training and research stays Remuneration and social benefits follow the applicable UCLouvain rules for doctoral scholarship holders. Application process Please submit ONLINE (submit option below) your application as a single PDF file , containing the following documents : Motivation letter (max. 1 page) CV Transcripts of records (Bachelor’s and Master’s) Contact details of two referees Relevant work sample (e.g. a code repository, a recent publication or an excerpt from your Master’s thesis) Incomplete applications or applications not following these instructions will not be considered. For questions (no applications), contact Prof. Dr. Christoph Waibel at christoph.waibel@uclouvain.be. Please apply online only, until the 30th of November 2026 Contact: Christoph Waibel - christoph.waibel@uclouvain.be

indeed:24ed01c757ff1b3e.title: PhD Position in ML-Based Interpretation of Geophysical Legacy Data for Mineral Exploration
indeed:24ed01c757ff1b3e.desc: PhD Position in ML-Based Interpretation of Geophysical Legacy Data for Mineral Exploration Develop and test new methods for deep exploration of sediment-hosted copper systems by integrating legacy seismic and well-log data with basin modelling, geochemistry and machine learning. Job description We are looking for a PhD candidate who is keen to explore how legacy seismic and well-log data acquired for petroleum exploration can be transformed into a new resource for deep mineral exploration. The candidate will combine quantitative geophysical interpretation, basin modelling and machine learning to investigate a challenging target: the thin Kupferschiefer horizon buried beneath the Netherlands and the North Sea. The Dutch subsurface offers an exceptional dataset of more than 6,000 wells, including approximately 1,700 in which the Kupferschiefer has been identified, together with extensive high-quality 2D and 3D seismic reflection data and available cores. Yet these data were acquired and interpreted for hydrocarbon exploration. Recognizing and mapping a horizon a few metres thick at kilometers depth, and identifying features associated with its mineral potential, requires methods that can extract information across datasets with very different resolution, coverage and physical meaning. The goal of this PhD project is to develop an integrated methodology for characterizing the Kupferschiefer and its geological context. You will analyse well logs to identify the target horizon and extrapolate it to wells where it has not yet been recognized. You will use seismic data for cross-well correlation and improved spatial characterization, and basin analysis to investigate the roles of stratigraphy, faulting and basin evolution. Geological, petrophysical, geochemical and mineralogical information will be integrated to identify characteristics and fingerprints associated with copper mineralization. Machine learning will be an important part of this methodological development. You will establish robust and interpretable baseline models for well-log analysis and investigate approaches designed for sequential data, including convolutional and transformer-based models. You will also contribute to multimodal methods that combine seismic, well-log, geological and geochemical information while incorporating geological knowledge and physical constraints. A postdoctoral researcher will work alongside you for one year, focusing primarily on advanced multimodal and physics-informed machine-learning developments. The research is part of the EU-funded INTELLIGENT project. Results from the Dutch basin will be combined with complementary studies by other groups working on the Kupferschiefer and related systems to develop a regional-scale mineral-system model and transferable exploration workflows. Your multidisciplinary research work will be carried out within the Applied Geophysics and Petrophysics Section and the Resource Engineering Section of GSE at TU Delft. Through close collaboration with TNO, the National Materials Observatory and partners from universities, geological surveys, research institutes and industry across Europe, you will test new methodological ideas within an international network and against a real, societally relevant exploration challenge. Job requirements Being creative and independent, you have the ability to conduct independent research and collaborate across geoscience, engineering and data-science disciplines. You also have: An MSc degree in geophysics, geology, earth sciences, geological or petroleum engineering, or a closely related discipline. Interest in applied geophysics and resource exploration and machine learning methods. Experience in scientific programming (preferably Python or Matlab). Good writing and communication skills. Experience in one or more of the fields below is considered an advantage: Basin analysis, basin modelling or sedimentary-basin evolution. Quantitative interpretation of seismic reflection data and well logs. Petrophysics, low temperature geochemistry and mineralogy. Machine Learning (deep learning and/or statistical learning methods). TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences The Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences (CEG) is committed to outstanding international research and education in the field of civil engineering, applied earth sciences, traffic and transport, water technology, and delta technology. Our research feeds into our educational programmes and covers societal challenges such as climate change, energy transition, resource availability, urbanisation and clean water. Our research projects are conducted in close cooperation with a wide range of research institutions. CEG is convinced of the importance of open science and supports its scientists in integrating open science in their research practice. The Faculty of CEG comprises 28 research groups in the following seven departments: Materials Mechanics Management & Design, Engineering Structures, Geoscience and Engineering, Geoscience and Remote Sensing, Transport & Planning, Hydraulic Engineering and Water Management. & Geosciences. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information For more information about this vacancy, please contact Valentina Socco, Geophysics (L.V.Socco@tudelft.nl), Mike Buxton, Resource Engineering (M.W.N.Buxton@tudelft.nl), or Jing Sun, Machine Learning (ing.Sun@tudelft.nl). Please apply via the website of TU Delft, unsolicited emails will not be considered or answered. #EU funded: This is an EU funded project, named INTELLIGENT: Innovative exploration technologies for deep-targeting critical mineral deposits, Horizon Europe (HORIZON) Call: HORIZON-CL4-2026-01, Project: 101345448, Coordinator Uppsala University. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 17 November 2026 upload the following documents: Motivation letter. Curriculum Vitae, including a list of relevant courses. If applicable, the topic of your MSc thesis. You can address your application to Valentina Socco. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services. Faculty/Department: Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences Salary range: €3204 - €4051 Hours per week: 32-38 FTE: 1,0 Submission is possible until: 17 Nov 2026 ID job: 3990

indeed:a4f68d670314a387.title: Promovendus 'Evaluatie van een digitale COPD-coach'
indeed:a4f68d670314a387.desc: Jouw functie Ben jij nieuwsgierig naar hoe kunstmatige intelligentie kan bijdragen aan betere zorg voor mensen met COPD? En wil je wetenschappelijk onderzoek doen dat direct impact heeft op de praktijk? Binnen het DACIL-project zoeken we een enthousiaste promovendus die de effectiviteit van een innovatieve digitale COPD-coach gaat onderzoeken. Over DACIL DACIL (Developing A digital COPD companion for Improving Lifestyle) is een meerjarig onderzoeksproject gericht op de ontwikkeling van een digitale coach voor mensen met COPD. De digitale coach maakt gebruik van spraakanalyse, sensoren en kunstmatige intelligentie om verslechteringen van de ziekte vroegtijdig te signaleren en patiënten te ondersteunen bij een gezonde leefstijl. Het project wordt uitgevoerd door een multidisciplinair consortium van zorgprofessionals, onderzoekers, data scientists, AI-specialisten en maatschappelijke partners. Jouw rol Als promovendus ben je verantwoordelijk voor het klinisch evalueren van de DACIL-app. Je onderzoekt in hoeverre de app betrouwbare en valide informatie geeft over veranderingen in de gezondheidstoestand van mensen met COPD en of het gebruik van de app leidt tot betere gezondheidsuitkomsten. Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder andere uit: Het uitvoeren en rapporteren van studies naar de validiteit en diagnostische waarde van de DACIL-app. Het opzetten en uitvoeren van een proof-of-conceptstudie. Het ontwerpen en coördineren van een gerandomiseerde gecontroleerde studie (RCT) naar de effectiviteit van de digitale coach. Het verzamelen en analyseren van gegevens van deelnemers over onder andere longaanvallen, klachten, kwaliteit van leven, leefstijl en zorggebruik. Het nauw samenwerken met patiënten, zorgverleners en andere onderzoekers binnen het consortium. Het publiceren van onderzoeksresultaten in internationale wetenschappelijke tijdschriften en het presenteren van bevindingen op conferenties. Het schrijven van een proefschrift op basis van de onderzoeksresultaten. Jouw werkplek DACIL consortium Het DACIL-project wordt uitgevoerd door een multidisciplinair consortium van onderzoekers, (long)artsen, gezondheidswetenschappers, experts op het gebied van kunstmatige intelligentie en digitale gezondheid, patiëntenvertegenwoordigers en maatschappelijke partners. Tot het consortium behoren onder meer Maastricht UMC+, Maastricht University, Radboud Universiteit, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Universiteit Twente, Longfonds, Long Alliantie Nederland, NVALT, PHAROS, Kenniscentrum Digitale Zorg en Zorginstituut Nederland, aangevuld met innovatieve technologiepartners. Voor de uitvoering van de studies wordt een projectgroep geformeerd met onderzoekers van MUMC+ en Radboudumc, die gezamenlijk verantwoordelijk zijn voor de opzet, uitvoering, analyse en rapportage van de studies. Eerstelijnsgeneeskunde De afdeling Eerstelijnsgeneeskunde loopt voorop in het vormgeven van geïntegreerde zorg op het gebied van onderwijs, opleiding, onderzoek en patiëntenzorg. Samen met anderen werken we aan mensgerichte, houdbare en duurzame oplossingen voor belangrijke vraagstukken rondom de zorg van morgen en aan blijvende inzetbaarheid van onze (zorg)professionals. Onze missie: ' Wij ontwikkelen de medisch-generalistische zorg van de toekoms t' De afdeling Eerstelijnsgeneeskunde bestaat uit de units onderzoek, onderwijs, opleidingen (voor huisarts, specialist ouderengeneeskunde, verslavingsarts, bedrijfsarts en verzekeringsarts) en patiëntenzorg. Ruim 360 eerstelijnsprofessionals werken dwars door deze units samen aan de ontwikkeling van de medisch-generalistische zorg. Daarmee is onze afdeling dé thuishaven voor medische professionals, docenten, opleiders en onderzoekers in de eerstelijnszorg. De afdeling kent een cultuur van laagdrempelig inspireren, pionieren, ontplooien en verbinden die ELG-eigen is en die we ook vragen van onze medewerkers. Geïntegreerde zorg, de ontschotting van de zorg, is een speerpunt van onze afdeling. Dat zien we in onze intensieve samenwerking met lokale, regionale en landelijke partners en netwerken – binnen en buiten het ziekenhuis. Deze eerstelijns-synergie vormt de basis voor continuatie van onze traditie van pionieren en verdere ontwikkeling van kennis rondom de eerstelijnszorg. Jouw profiel Wij zoeken een enthousiaste en analytisch sterke kandidaat met: Een afgeronde masteropleiding in Gezondheidswetenschappen, Epidemiologie, Biomedische Wetenschappen, Geneeskunde, Data Science in Health of een vergelijkbaar vakgebied. Affiniteit met COPD-zorg, klinisch onderzoek, digitale zorginnovatie en evaluatieonderzoek. Kennis van en/of interesse in onderzoeksmethoden en statistiek. Ervaring met R is een pre. Goede communicatieve vaardigheden en het vermogen om effectief samen te werken in een multidisciplinair team. Een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal. Goed om te weten De inschaling is afhankelijk van vooropleiding. Voor een basisarts (afgeronde studie Geneeskunde) is schaal 10 van toepassing. Voor overige studierichtingen geldt inschaling in schaal 10A. De eerste sollicitatiegesprekken vinden plaats op 16 november 2026. Fijn als je hier alvast rekening mee houdt. Er volgt een tweede sollicitatiegesprek waarvoor je gevraagd wordt een opdracht voor te bereiden. De datum van dit tweede gesprek wordt later gecommuniceerd. Een assessment maakt onderdeel uit van deze sollicitatieprocedure. Voor deze functie is een Verklaring Omtrent het Gedrag (VOG) vereist. Wij werven zelf voor deze vacature. Acquisitie stellen wij niet op prijs; delen in je netwerk wél. Fijne arbeidsvoorwaarden Loonsverhoging Bij ons wordt je werk gewaardeerd. Je salaris stijgt met 3,5% per 1 mei 2027. Vanaf schaal 15 wordt de stijging gemaximeerd. Werk en privé in balans Een goede werk-privébalans vinden wij vanzelfsprekend. Met inspirerende trainingen, mindfulnessactiviteiten en mantelzorgspreekuren ondersteunen we je in elke fase van je leven. Groei en ontwikkeling Onze online leeromgeving heeft een breed aanbod aan trainingen, e-learnings en opleidingen – van vakinhoudelijke verdieping tot persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Zo haal je het beste uit je talent. Goed geregeld Bij ons krijg je 8% vakantiegeld, 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering en – afhankelijk van je functie – 47% tot 72% onregelmatigheidstoeslag. Daarnaast kun je rekenen op 180 vakantie-uren per jaar (bij 36 uur/week). Vergoeding Je ontvangt € 0,21 per kilometer reiskostenvergoeding, OV-reizen vergoeden we volledig (2e klasse) en werk je (deels) thuis? Dan krijg je € 2,45 per thuiswerkdag. Zo is alles goed geregeld, waar je ook werkt. Keuze model arbeidsvoorwaarden Jij bepaalt wat bij jou past. Gebruik een deel van je arbeidsvoorwaarden bijvoorbeeld voor extra verlofuren, een fiets met belastingvoordeel of het aflossen van je studieschuld. Warm welkom Een goede start vinden we belangrijk. Door onze onboarding-app, ben je al vóór je eerste werkdag goed voorbereid. Tijdens de introductiedag maak je kennis met je collega’s en onze organisatie. Omkleedvergoeding Draag je werkkleding van het Radboudumc en kleed je je buiten werktijd om? Dan ontvang je, als het voor jouw functie geldt, een omkleedtoelage van €80,- bruto per maand bij een fulltime dienstverband. Onderzoek met impact op de zorg van morgen Werk mee aan baanbrekend onderzoek dat leidt tot innovaties in de gezondheid en zorg van de toekomst. De sollicitatieprocedure Solliciteer Vul het formulier op deze pagina in. We nemen binnen 5 werkdagen na de sluitingsdatum contact met je op over je sollicitatie. Eerste gesprek We kijken ernaar uit om je beter te leren kennen en nodigen je graag uit voor een gesprek. Assessment We ontdekken nog verder wie jij bent en wat jou drijft. Tweede gesprek Je eerste gesprek was een succes en we zijn enthousiast om verder te ontdekken of we goed bij elkaar passen. Aanbod We sturen je een voorstel met je arbeidsvoorwaarden. In dienst! We verwelkomen je graag als nieuwe collega en zorgen voor een fijne start.

indeed:0a18e49effdc6554.title: PhD Candidate - Spatial multi-omics and single cell analysis of human diseases
indeed:0a18e49effdc6554.desc: PhD Candidate - Spatial multi-omics and single cell analysis of human diseases Welcome to Maastricht University! Are you interested in developing and applying cutting-edge spatial multi-omics and single-cell technologies to study human diseases? At the Maastricht MultiModal Molecular Imaging (M4i) Institute, you will contribute to the development of next-generation technologies for biomedical research. PhD Candidate - Spatial multi-omics and single cell analysis of human diseases Our goal: We seek to advance the understanding of human disease by integrating spatial multi-omics and single-cell approaches. Combining molecular information across tissues, cell populations and local microenvironments enables us to uncover disease-driving mechanisms, identify novel biomarkers and support the development of more precise diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Your colleagues: You will join the multidisciplinary research environment of the Maastricht MultiModal Molecular Imaging (M4i) Institute, embedded within the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML) at Maastricht University. You will collaborate with experts in molecular imaging, mass spectrometry, computational biology, pathology and clinical research. You will be supervised by Dr. Eva Cuypers and become part of M4i's vibrant and internationally recognized research community. The position offers extensive opportunities for method development, translational biomedical research and participation in national and international collaborations. What you do You will develop and apply advanced spatial multi-omics and single-cell approaches to investigate the molecular architecture of human diseases. The project focuses on mapping biological processes within complex tissues by integrating complementary technologies that capture molecular information across different spatial and cellular scales. Using state-of-the-art platforms such as MALDI mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI), laser microdissection, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell omics, digital pathology and AI-driven data analysis, you will generate and integrate multidimensional datasets from patient-derived samples. In addition, you will contribute to the development of innovative workflows that combine spatially resolved molecular profiling with cellular-level characterization. By linking tissue-wide molecular patterns to individual cells and their local environments, you will help reveal how cellular interactions and molecular pathways contribute to disease development and progression. The resulting methodologies will be applied across a broad range of biomedical questions, including cancer, inflammatory diseases, metabolic disorders and environmental health research. This position offers a unique opportunity to gain expertise in spatial biology, mass spectrometry, computational analysis and translational medicine while contributing to next-generation technologies for biomedical research. Are you ready to set the course for the years ahead? Then we’d love to meet you. What you bring We’re not looking for checkboxes; we’re interested in who you are and what you bring. Do you recognize yourself in this? A master’s degree in Biomedical Sciences, Medicine, (Bio)Chemistry, Analytical Science and Technology, or a related subject Proficiency in English (C1 or higher according to CEFR) Hands-on basic laboratory experience in the molecular analysis of biological systems Interest in and ability to carry out practical research activities, including experimental work, data collection and analysis. The ability to communicate scientific information clearly and effectively, both orally and in writing in English. Other experience / skills that would be helpful for the project: Imaging technologies (example spatial mass spectrometry, spatial transcriptomics, clinical imaging techniques) Mass spectrometry (theoretical and/or practical experience in reading mass spectra and understanding the information they provide about the molecular composition of samples) Ion beams and ion optics (knowledge of the principles of ion beams and ion optics, including their role in the generation, manipulation or focusing of ions in analytical instruments) Laser based imaging systems (knowledge of or experience with laser-based imaging systems and their application in imaging or analysing biological samples)Data science and data analysis (experience with data processing, statistical analysis and interpretation of research data, as well as familiarity with programming languages such as R or Python) Biological sample preparation (experience with the preparation and handling of biological samples for analysis, including the safe handling of human biological materials in accordance with relevant laboratory procedures) What we offer At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer: A 12-month contract (1.0 FTE) with the prospect of a 3 year extension. A gross monthly salary between €3.204 and €4.051 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus. 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours. Flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home. Freedom and space to shape your work independently and develop your ideas. A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with. A solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities. An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe. Find out more about the PhD journey at Maastricht University, from starting your research to completing your PhD and beyond. As a PhD candidate, you will be automatically enrolled in one of our Graduate Schools. Find out more about our Graduate Schools. About the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML) FHML is committed to health in the broadest sense: from molecule to human, and from healthcare to prevention. We train healthcare professionals and researchers through innovative educational programmes and conduct groundbreaking research in health and well-being. As part of Maastricht UMC+ (MUMC+), our international and interdisciplinary community forms a unique collaboration between university and academic hospital, where education, research, and care come together. About the Maastricht MultiModal Molecular Imaging institute, M4i M4i is a state-of-the art international institute at Maastricht University (The Netherlands) that brings together a powerful palette of innovative molecular imaging technologies. Its mission is to develop instrumentation and perform both fundamental, methodological and applied research in molecular imaging as part of a translational, synergistic, interdisciplinary research program that attracts top researchers from across the world. The successful PhD candidate will work at the boundaries of mass spectrometry imaging and omics in the IMS dicision where we develop and apply state-of-the-art molecular imaging approaches for nanomedicine and biomedical research, including diagnostic and prognostic tools for personalized medicine in oncology, neurology and cardiovascular medicine. The institute is part of the Dutch Large Scale scientific Infrastructure and offers a plethora of advanced imaging instrumentation that are made available to regional, national and international researchers. Interested? Want to know more about this position or what it’s like to work at our university? Reach out to Dr. Eva Cuypers at e.cuypers@maastrichtuniversity.nl. The end date of the publication is 8 November 2026. Please upload the following when applying: CV Motivation letter Copies of your tertiary degrees Contact details of at least two references. The anticipated start date is in January 2027. Apply now via the button below. We look forward to getting to know you! About Maastricht University At Maastricht University, we collaboratively seek solutions to help move the world forward. We do this with 23,300 students and 5,400 employees across 5 regional locations, 6 faculties, and more than 70 research institutes. We encourage you to push boundaries and discover new opportunities for yourself and the world around you. Together, we can find the answers for tomorrow. The vacancy is open for internal and external candidates. In case of equal qualifications, internal candidates will be prioritized. At Maastricht University, we prefer to contact potential candidates directly. We therefore kindly ask that no agencies or intermediaries submit offers or approaches. Maastricht University is committed to promoting and nurturing a diverse and inclusive community. We believe that diversity in our staff and student population contributes to the quality of research and education at UM, and strive to enable this through inclusive policies and innovative projects led by teams of staff and students. We encourage you to apply for this position. indeed:3e00a18eb425de0a.title: PhD Research Intern, 3D World Models
indeed:3e00a18eb425de0a.desc: SpAItial is pioneering the next generation of World Models, pushing the boundaries of generative AI, computer vision, and the simulation of reality. We are moving beyond 2D pixels to build models that natively understand the physics and geometry of our world. Our mission is to redefine how industries, from robotics and AR/VR to gaming and cinema, generate and interact with physically-grounded 3D environments. We're looking for bold, innovative individuals driven by a passion for pushing the boundaries of generative 3D AI. You should thrive in an environment where creativity meets technical challenge and be fearless in tackling the hardest problems in 3D world modeling. Our team is built on a foundation of dedication and a shared commitment to excellence, so we value people who take immense pride in their work and place the collective goals of the team above personal ambition. As a part of SpAItial, you'll be at the forefront of building World Models that bridge generative AI and the physical world. If you're ready to make an impact, embrace the unknown, and collaborate with a talented group of visionaries, we want to hear from you. We're seeking PhD Research Interns to work with our research team on open problems in 3D generation and reconstruction. You should have strong knowledge of at least one of our core areas, such as generative video and diffusion models, scene representations like Gaussian splats and radiance fields, or 3D reconstruction from per-scene optimization to feed-forward models. Over a 5-7 month internship, you will own a well-defined research question with the goal of publishing a paper. Responsibilities You will explore novel research directions in 3D generation, reconstruction, and world models. You will design, implement, and evaluate state-of-the-art methods, turning innovative research ideas into working systems and prototypes. You will be working closely with our research team. You will also present your findings and contribute to scientific publications targeting leading conferences in computer vision, computer graphics, and machine learning, such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, and ICLR. Key Qualifications Currently enrolled in the third year or beyond of a PhD in computer science, computer vision, computer graphics, machine learning, or a related field. 2-3 first-author papers at top-tier conferences such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, or ICLR. Knowledge of at least one of: generative models (diffusion or video models), neural scene representations, or 3D reconstruction. At SpAItial, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer and ensure all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.

linkedin:4480468259.title: Promotionsstelle (100%) - Autonomous Vehicle Lab - Runtime Risk Assessment für Autonomes Fahren
linkedin:4480468259.desc: 20.10.2026, Academic staff Der Lehrstuhl für Fahrzeugtechnik sucht ab 1.10.2026 wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiter (m/w/d) aus Informatik, Robotik oder Ingenieurwissenschaften zur Promotion im Bereich echtzeitfähige Risikobewertung (Runtime Risk Assessment) für autonome Fahrzeuge. Hintergrund Autonome Fahrzeuge treffen ihre Entscheidungen unter kontinuierlich wechselnder Unsicherheit, aus der Wahrnehmung der Umgebung, der Prädiktion des Verhaltens anderer Verkehrsteilnehmer und der eigenen Planung. Ob ein Fahrzeug sicher innerhalb seiner Betriebsgrenzen (ODD) agiert, lässt sich nicht durch starre Regeln allein beantworten, sondern erfordert eine kontinuierliche, echtzeitfähige Bewertung des aktuellen Risikos. Wir entwickeln ein System, das Systemzustand, Umfeldsituation und Betriebsgrenzen laufend zu einem aggregierten Risikomaß verdichtet und so die Grundlage für automatisierte Betriebsmodus-Entscheidungen bildet. Gestalte mit uns das Risikobewusstsein autonomer Fahrzeuge von morgen und forsche an spannenden Dissertationsthemen. Deine Herausforderungen Als Promovierender entwickelst du ein echtzeitfähiges Risikobewertungssystem, das kontinuierlich Systemzustand, Umfeldsituation und Betriebsgrenzen (ODD) bewertet. Im Zentrum steht die Integration von Unsicherheitsmaßen aus Perzeption, Prädiktion und Planung zu einem aggregierten Risikomaß, das als Grundlage für Systementscheidungen dient: Erkennt das System etwa eine zunehmende Divergenz zwischen prädiziertem und tatsächlichem Verhalten anderer Verkehrsteilnehmer, muss dein Risikomaß dies zuverlässig abbilden. Darauf aufbauend entwickelst du Schwellwertlogiken und Eskalationsmechanismen, die auf Basis dieses Risikomaßes automatisiert Betriebsmodus-Entscheidungen auslösen, und validierst dein Runtime-Risk-Assessment in Simulation und Realbetrieb anhand definierter Szenarien und sicherheitsrelevanter KPIs.
