linkedin:4417713487.desc: Chez STMicroelectronics, nous sommes convaincus que la technologie est un moteur d’innovation et a un impact positif pour les entreprises, les personnes et la société. En tant qu’acteur mondial des semiconducteurs, nos technologies de pointe et nos composants électroniques sont invisibles mais au cœur du monde d’aujourd’hui. Rejoindre ST, c’est intégrer une entreprise internationale riche de plus de 115 nationalités, présente dans 40 pays, et rassemblant plus de 50 000 talents passionnés et engagés, tous unis par la volonté de créer et d’inventer la technologie de demain. Innover demande bien plus que des compétences techniques : cela nécessite des personnes inspirantes, qui savent collaborer avec respect et enthousiasme. Des collaborateurs animés par la passion, prêts à remettre en question le statu quo, à faire avancer l’innovation et à révéler leur plein potentiel. Venez vivre cette aventure avec nous et contribuez à construire un futur plus intelligent et plus durable, en alliant responsabilité et innovation. Notre technologie commence avec vous. Les transistors bipolaires à hétérojonction (HBT) sur substrat GaAs, utilisés aujourd’hui dans les amplificateurs de puissance des téléphones mobiles à des fréquences de quelques GHz, ont un gain limité aux fréquences plus élevés, notamment dans la bande 6G FR3 (7-24GHz). Les transistors bipolaires à double hétérojonction (DHBT) GaAsSb sur substrat InP représentent aujourd’hui l’état de l’art des performances en fréquence, avec une fréquence maximale d’oscillation fMAX > 1 THz, leur permettant d’adresser des applications hautes-fréquences, ainsi que les communications optiques rapides. L’utilisation d’un substrat d’InP, qui est un matériau fragile, rare et donc cher, est cependant un inconvénient de ces transistors. Cette thèse se propose d’investiguer le potentiel de DHBTs pseudomorphiques GaInP/GaAsSb sur substrat GaAs ainsi que de DHBTs métamorphiques InP/GaAsSb sur substrat GaAs. A propos de vos missions DHBTs pseumorphiques GaInP/GaAsSb/GaAs. Commencer par une cartographie de l’espace des paramètres composition GaAsSb en fonction de l’épaisseur pour la croissance pseudomorphique (la littérature donne des premières indications). Identifier les empilements de couches réalisables par épitaxie. Fabriquer des DHBTs les plus performants possibles en adaptant le procédé de fabrication du DHBT GaAsSb/InP existant et en réduisant autant que possible les dimensions. DHBTs métamorphiques InP/GaAsSb/GaAs Transférer le procédé DHBT InP/GaAsSb développé à l’ETH Zürich vers une plateforme métamorphique avec des bases et collecteurs minces et des géométries réduites. Evaluation de l’effet des dislocations résiduelles sur le rendement des dispositifs. Evaluation de l’impact du buffer métamorphique et de sa conductivité thermique sur les performances RF et comparaison avec la filière native sur InP. A propos de vous Vous disposez d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou Master 2 Vous maitrisez la physique des matériaux et composants semi-conducteurs et avez une très bonne connaissance des procédés de fabrication associés. Idéalement vous avez des connaissances dans les transistors bipolaires à hétérojonction. Vous avez un niveau minimum B2 en anglais. Vous êtes rigoureux, dynamique, motivé, ainsi qu’une très bonne capacité d’analyse pour résoudre les problèmes et une capacité à synthétiser des travaux scientifiques. Vous aimez travailler en équipe. English Version Heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) on GaAs substrates, used today in mobile phone power amplifiers at frequencies of a few GHz, have limited gain at higher frequencies, particularly in the 6G FR3 band (7–24 GHz). Gallium arsenide antimonide (GaAsSb) double-heterojunction bipolar transistors (DHBTs) on InP substrates currently represent the state of the art in frequency performance, with a maximum oscillation frequency fMAX > 1 THz, enabling them to address high-frequency applications as well as high-speed optical communications. However, the use of an InP substrate, which is a fragile, scarce and therefore expensive material, is a drawback of these transistors. This thesis aims to investigate the potential of pseudomorphic GaInP/GaAsSb DHBTs on GaAs substrates, as well as metamorphic InP/GaAsSb DHBTs on GaAs substrates. About Your Missions Pseudomorphic GaInP/GaAsSb/GaAs DHBTs. Start with a mapping of the GaAsSb composition parameter space as a function of thickness for pseudomorphic growth (the literature provides initial guidance). Identify layer stacks that can be achieved by epitaxy. Fabricate DHBTs with the highest possible performance by adapting the existing GaAsSb/InP DHBT fabrication process and reducing the dimensions as much as possible. Metamorphic InP/GaAsSb/GaAs DHBTs. Transfer the InP/GaAsSb DHBT process developed at ETH Zurich to a metamorphic platform with thin bases and collectors and fine geometries. Evaluate the effect of residual dislocations on device yield. Assess the impact of the metamorphic buffer and its thermal conductivity on RF performance and compare it with the native InP-based technology. About You You hold an engineering degree or a Master’s degree (Master 2). You have a strong command of semiconductor material and device physics and very good knowledge of the associated fabrication processes. Ideally, you have knowledge of heterojunction bipolar transistors. You have at least a B2 level in English. You are rigorous, dynamic, motivated, with strong analytical skills to solve problems and the ability to synthesize scientific work. You enjoy working in a team. linkedin:4481594389.desc: Develop and test new methods for deep exploration of sediment-hosted copper systems by integrating legacy seismic and well-log data with basin modelling, geochemistry and machine learning. Job Description We are looking for a PhD candidate who is keen to explore how legacy seismic and well-log data acquired for petroleum exploration can be transformed into a new resource for deep mineral exploration. The candidate will combine quantitative geophysical interpretation, basin modelling and machine learning to investigate a challenging target: the thin Kupferschiefer horizon buried beneath the Netherlands and the North Sea. The Dutch subsurface offers an exceptional dataset of more than 6,000 wells, including approximately 1,700 in which the Kupferschiefer has been identified, together with extensive high-quality 2D and 3D seismic reflection data and available cores. Yet these data were acquired and interpreted for hydrocarbon exploration. Recognizing and mapping a horizon a few metres thick at kilometers depth, and identifying features associated with its mineral potential, requires methods that can extract information across datasets with very different resolution, coverage and physical meaning. The goal of this PhD project is to develop an integrated methodology for characterizing the Kupferschiefer and its geological context. You will analyse well logs to identify the target horizon and extrapolate it to wells where it has not yet been recognized. You will use seismic data for cross-well correlation and improved spatial characterization, and basin analysis to investigate the roles of stratigraphy, faulting and basin evolution. Geological, petrophysical, geochemical and mineralogical information will be integrated to identify characteristics and fingerprints associated with copper mineralization. Machine learning will be an important part of this methodological development. You will establish robust and interpretable baseline models for well-log analysis and investigate approaches designed for sequential data, including convolutional and transformer-based models. You will also contribute to multimodal methods that combine seismic, well-log, geological and geochemical information while incorporating geological knowledge and physical constraints. A postdoctoral researcher will work alongside you for one year, focusing primarily on advanced multimodal and physics-informed machine-learning developments. The research is part of the EU-funded INTELLIGENT project. Results from the Dutch basin will be combined with complementary studies by other groups working on the Kupferschiefer and related systems to develop a regional-scale mineral-system model and transferable exploration workflows. Your multidisciplinary research work will be carried out within the Applied Geophysics and Petrophysics Section and the Resource Engineering Section of GSE at TU Delft. Through close collaboration with TNO, the National Materials Observatory and partners from universities, geological surveys, research institutes and industry across Europe, you will test new methodological ideas within an international network and against a real, societally relevant exploration challenge. Job Requirements Being creative and independent, you have the ability to conduct independent research and collaborate across geoscience, engineering and data-science disciplines. You also have: An MSc degree in geophysics, geology, earth sciences, geological or petroleum engineering, or a closely related discipline. Interest in applied geophysics and resource exploration and machine learning methods. Experience in scientific programming (preferably Python or Matlab). Good writing and communication skills. Experience in one or more of the fields below is considered an advantage: Basin analysis, basin modelling or sedimentary-basin evolution. Quantitative interpretation of seismic reflection data and well logs. Petrophysics, low temperature geochemistry and mineralogy. Machine Learning (deep learning and/or statistical learning methods). The lab focuses on developing innovative machine learning and statistical approaches for complex spatiotemporal environmental datasets. We are looking for a candidate to join ExtFire, an SNSF-funded project that aims to develop the first pan-European framework combining non-stationary extreme value theory (EVT), causal inference, and tail-sensitive deep learning to quantify and predict extreme wildfire risk in a reproducible and transferable way. In addition to the two PIs, the ExtFire team brings together three external partners with complementary expertise : Prof. Marco Turco (University of Murcia, Spain) contributes specialized expertise in fire-climate interactions; Dr. Paolo Fiorucci (CIMA Research Foundation, Italy) brings expertise in fire-spread simulation; and Dr. Erwan Koch (Expertise Centre for Climate Extremes, Unil) provides expertise in spatial EVT and max-stable random fields. The successful candidate will join Dr. Tonini's lab at IDYST and work closely with the postdoctoral researcher recruited within the ExtFire project, benefiting from the expretise and support of the entire ExtFire team. Your Responsibilities The successful candidate will develop research leading to a PhD in environmental sciences under the main supervision of Dr. Marj Tonini. The PhD student will contribute to ExtFire by developing the data-driven core of the project. The Main Tasks Include harmonising and integrating large open datasets on wildfires, meteorology and land surface into a consistent pan-European data infrastructure; develping statistical and spatio-temporal models to characterise extreme fire events, such as those with very large burned areas or rapid spread; building the datasets and baseline machine learning models used to evaluate predictions of extreme events; applying explainable AI methods (e.g. SHAP) to identify the main environmental drivers of extreme fires across regions; writing scientific papers, presenting results at international conferences and assisting in teaching (up to 10% of the time). Your Qualifications We are looking for a motivated candidate with the following profile : Desire to write a thesis in spatio-temporal modelling of extreme events (wildfires); Master's degree in environmental sciences, geosciences, statistics, applied mathematics, physics, computer science, or a closely related quantitative field, with a strong academic record; Hands-on experience with machine learning, ideally deep learning (e.g. PyTorch, TensorFlow), and familiarity with explainable AI; Solid background in statistics and data analysis (e.g. probability, regression, time series or spatial statistics). Knowledge of extreme value theory is an asset; Solid programming skills in Python and/or R, demonstrated by experience in processing and analysing large datasets (e.g. gridded climate or remote sensing data, NetCDF/raster formats); Fluency in English, written and spoken, with the ability to write scientific reports. Knowledge of French is an asset; Proven experience in the quantitative analysis or modelling of natural hazards (e.g. wildfires, floods, landslides, earthquakes), as shown by a thesis, project or publication, is an asset. linkedin:4480457513.desc: About The Position The Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MTP) at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) has two vacancies for PhD candidates within different disciplines of Systems Engineering/New Product Development, funded through the Centre for Research-based Innovation, SFI-CELECT (Research Centre for Effective Engineering and Learning in Complex Systems). The positions are 3-year doctoral research fellowships starting in 2026/2027. Each PhD candidate will be embedded in the research activities of SFI-CELECT and will work closely with NTNU, University of Sout-Eastern Norway (USN), University of Agder (UiA), Technical University of Denmark (DTU), and leading industrial partners in the product manufacturing, defence and aerospace, and maritime sectors. You will be supervised by Professor Torgeir Welo. About The Project SFI-CELECT (Research Centre for Effective Engineering and Learning in Complex Systems) started in 2026 and is funded by the Research Council of Norway and industrial partners. The centre is led by the University of South-Eastern Norway (USN) in close collaboration with NTNU and UiA, and involves a broad consortium of leading companies across multiple industrial sectors. Through research on new methodologies for effective engineering and learning in complex systems, we aim to accelerate innovation and value creation in industry by developing better methods and smarter tools to ‘do more with less— and faster’. SFI-CELECT runs from 2026 to 2033 and is Norway’s most ambitious research initiative within innovation in complex systems. The primary objective of SFI-CELECT is to leap the innovation and product realization capabilities in some of Norway’s leading industries by enhancing how new products are developed and managed. Operating within an integrated academic-industry ecosystem, SFI-CELECT will generate research-based methodologies, methods and tools for effective and efficient product innovation and realization, embracing the complexity and dynamics in today’s business environments where digitalization and AI tools play an increasingly important role. A key aim of CELECT is to establish an integrated academic-industry learning and educational ecosystem, where PhDs and researchers work together across disciplines to solve complex problems of high industrial importance using industry-as-a-laboratory as the research context. Education and competence building are central pillars of CELECT. The centre will educate more than 30 PhD and postdoctoral researchers and over 120 MSc students, strengthening Norway’s international position in new-product innovation. Work location for the two positions posted here is NTNU - Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, Trondheim, Norway. PhD position 1: Strategies for leveraging cross-functional knowledge flows in digitally supported NPD processes Since the outcome of NPD processes is not only the physical artifact but also the creation, acquisition and transfer of knowledge, cross-functional knowledge flows are central to NPD effectiveness in (quality of decisions and solutions) and efficiency (speed and ‘first-time-right’). This PhD will research how such cross-functional knowledge flows can be enabled, managed and leveraged in contemporary NPD settings where collaborations are increasingly mediated by shared digital tools rather than co-located interaction. Accordingly, s/he will investigate how organizations can make NPD work processes more productive by better understanding where digital tools has their limitations. Moreover, the candidate will determine which countermeasures that can be established to stimulate and improve interactions across functional boundaries to make work flows more tangible and transparent with regard to identifying potential waste sources and lack of value. PhD position 2: Optimizing product design for efficient manufacturing using digital tools throughout the New Product Development (NPD) process The aim of this PhD is to develop knowledge-based, Design for Manufacturing (DfM) strategies for improved decision support in integrated product and process development. The PhD will develop, test and verify new DfM platforms, bridging theory, practices, processes, people and digital tools, and equipping companies with the capability necessary to effectively integrate manufacturing considerations, including product-service lifecycle responsibility, early in the product development process. This Position Will Complement PhD Position 1 Above, Which Focuses More Generally On Cross Functional Knowledge Flow In Multidisciplinary NPD Teams. Some Key Research Questions Are How can manufacturing considerations and requirements be efficiently and effectively integrated into the early stages of NPD? How can we integrate AI into our digital thread to automatically retrieve DfM data, specifications, and essential knowledge for NPD? How can we design modern learning frameworks to build a digital Design for Manufacturing (DfM) knowledge base? What role does externally captured information play in design support related to DfM? How can organizations utilize formal decision-support frameworks to operationalize and leverage their strategic Design for Manufacturing (DfM) capabilities? How can organizations enable interoperability between people, processes and IT/AI tools within such frameworks? linkedin:4481706010.desc: Are you passionate about affective neuroscience computational modelling and transcranial ultrasound stimulation? Come and join our PhD project on approach-avoidance decisions under threat, funded by the ERC Advanced Grant HEART2ADAPT, and work with a dynamic team. Why do some people remain calm and make flexible decisions under stress, while others freeze or flee? HEART2ADAPT aims to answer this question. We are developing a new model to understand how the body’s autonomic stress state shapes responses to threat and how the balance between sympathetic and parasympathetic activity supports adaptive decision making in dynamic environments. Using state-of-the-art methods to track brain and bodily signals in real time – such as heart rate, posture and advanced neuroimaging – we will investigate how stress influences decision-making. A key component of this specific PhD project is testing causal mechanisms using transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS), including both offline TUS and the development of MR-compatible online TUS. Funded by a European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant, the project HEART2ADAPT offers you the opportunity to contribute to protocol development, data collection and computational modelling of behavioural and neural data. You will apply TUS to key nodes of our model, including the amygdala, ventral striatum and dorsal ACC. You will work closely with colleagues at the Donders Institute and the Behavioural Science Institute, as well as with international collaborators. Responsibilities may also include mentoring of BSc and MSc students. Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate. Profile You have a Master’s degree in cognitive neuroscience or an adjacent field (psychology, biology, biomedical sciences, computer sciences, or other relevant MSc). You have a strong interest in fundamental research in cognitive and affective neurosciences and in computational psychiatry. You have experience with applying functional MRI (acquisition and analyses), including the use of Matlab, Python, SPM, FSL and/or other software tools, or you have experience with MEG (acquisition and analyses), including the use of Fieldtrip or similar. You have experience in non-invasive neuromodulation (preferably Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation) or are willing to master this technique. You have experience in the acquisition and analysis of peripheral psychophysiological data (e.g. autonomic nervous system measures). You have the capacity to participate in an interdisciplinary and translational research environment. You have interpersonal and communication skills to effectively collaborate and communicate in academia. You have a proactive and goal-directed attitude and good organisational skills. You are fluent in written and spoken English. Even if you do not meet all criteria, you are encouraged to apply if the role interests you. We offer We will give you a temporary employment contract (0.8 FTE 5- year contract - 1.0 FTE 4- year contract) of 1.5 years, after which your performance will be evaluated. If the evaluation is positive, your contract will be extended by 2.5 years (4-year contract) or 3.5 years (5-year contract). You will receive a starting salary of €3,204 gross per month based on a 38-hour working week, which will increase to €4,051 from the fourth year onwards (salary scale P). You will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8,3% end-of-year bonus. You will receive extra days off. With full-time employment, you can choose between 30 or 41 days of annual leave instead of the statutory 20. Additional Employment Conditions Work and science require good employment practices. This is reflected in Radboud University's primary and secondary employment conditions. You can make arrangements for the best possible work-life balance with flexible working hours, various leave arrangements and working from home. You are also able to compose part of your employment conditions yourself, for example, exchange income for extra leave days and receive a reimbursement for your sports subscription. And of course, we offer a good pension plan. You are given plenty of room and responsibility to develop your talents and realise your ambitions. Therefore, we provide various training and development schemes. We are Your position will be embedded in the Affective Neuroscience group led by Prof. Karin Roelofs at the Faculty of Social Sciences. You will be appointed by the Faculty's Behavioural Science Institute (BSI). You will be based at the Donders Centre for Cognitive Neuroimaging (DCCN) . You will also work closely with Lennart Verhagen’s group. Both BSI and DCCN are known for their successful graduate schools and strong dedication to open science and team science. Together, they create a warm, inclusive and cooperative research environment in which staff are well-supported in a work culture that promotes collaboration and respect. Behavioural Science Institute BSI is an interdisciplinary research institute where fundamental, applied and translational research takes place with the aim of understanding important societal issues and contributing to their solutions. BSI is one of the three research institutes of the Faculty of Social Sciences at Radboud University. Our researchers collaborate across the boundaries of psychology, communication science and pedagogical and educational science. Our mission for the coming years is to join forces in interdisciplinary research on the theme ’Empowering the Young’. We study the challenges that young people face in our current society and contribute to their empowerment. The institute provides excellent research facilities and has strong collaborations with non-academic partners. BSI has state-of-the-art research facilities for observational studies, experiments, eye-tracking studies, EEG measurements and GSR recording, psychobiological research, and behavioural measurements in both real and 3D virtual environments. The Donders Centre for Cognitive Neuroimaging The mission of this world class research centre is to conduct cutting-edge fundamental research in cognitive neuroscience. Much of the rapid progress in this field is being driven by the development of complex neuroimaging techniques for measuring activity in the human brain - an area in which the Centre plays a leading role. The research themes cover central cognitive functions such as perception, action, control, emotion, decision-making, attention, memory, language, learning and plasticity. The Centre also aims to establish how the different brain areas coordinate their activity with very high temporal precision to enable human and animal cognition. Our internationally renowned centre currently hosts more than 100 PhD candidates and postdoctoral researchers from more than 25 countries, offering a stimulating and multidisciplinary research environment. The centre is equipped with four MRI scanners (7T, 2x 3T), a 275-channel MEG system, an EEG-TMS/TUS laboratory, several (MR-compatible) EEG systems and high-performance computational facilities. In the application form, you will find which documents you need to include with your application. We look forward to receiving your application. The first interviews will take place on Thursday 26 November. Any second interview will take place on Wednesday 2 December. You will preferably start your employment in January 2027. We can imagine you're curious about our application procedure. It describes what you can expect during the application procedure and how we handle your personal data and internal and external candidates.

Self-driving cars, autonomous delivery and construction vehicles, mobile manipulators, and other robotic systems are moving closer to widespread deployment. However, fundamental research challenges remain before these systems can operate safely, reliably, and autonomously in complex, unfamiliar environments. For Example, How Can We Develop new training paradigms that use perception and interaction to train autonomous vehicle and robot policies in closed loop? Equip autonomous systems with online and offline assurances that meet the requirements of safety-critical applications? Enable vehicles and robots to navigate across new environments, tasks, and embodiments? Build systems that reason under uncertainty and interact safely and naturally with people and other agents? These are some of the exciting questions being explored by NVIDIA’s Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research (ASPIRE) group. Our diverse, interdisciplinary team conducts foundational research spanning foundation model design, embodied reasoning, safety, closed-loop training and evaluation, and agentic workflows for Physical AI development. We also investigate related areas including decision-making under uncertainty, deep learning, reinforcement learning, simulation, and the verification and validation of safety-critical AI systems. Our focus is on fundamental research, and lab members are encouraged to publish their work and open-source their code. NVIDIA is known for its collaborative culture, and our researchers work closely with experts across the company in autonomous vehicles, robotics, perception, simulation, and machine learning. This creates opportunities to influence real-world products while retaining the freedom and bandwidth to conduct groundbreaking, publishable research. What You’ll Be Doing Designing and implementing cutting-edge techniques for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI. Conducting original research and publishing your results. linkedin:4480474507.title: Stage Research Engineer : synthèse de programmes pour la génération 3D (PFE / M2 Recherche)
linkedin:4480474507.desc: Chat3D travaille sur la représentation paramétrique de la forme 3D par le langage : décrire un objet par du code plutôt que par une soupe de polygones. Cela repose sur deux chantiers : • l'entraînement de grands modèles de langage, en supervision puis en apprentissage par renforcement ; • la construction de juges 3D, capables d'estimer la justesse d'un objet produit et de servir de signal d'apprentissage. C'est un domaine où presque tout reste à établir : ce qu'un modèle doit émettre, ce qu'on sait mesurer d'une forme, et ce qui constitue un bon signal d'apprentissage pour s'en approcher. Le stage de recherche se focalise sur la contribution au pipeline d'apprentissage par renforcement qui permet à nos modèles de coder de la 3D. Le cadrage précis se discute à l'arrivée, selon ton profil et tes goûts, et nous sommes ouverts à une proposition personnelle alignée avec cette question. Dans tous les cas, le travail est pensé pour produire une contribution scientifique défendable : un protocole expérimental propre, des résultats falsifiables, un mémoire, et une publication possible. En pratique : • Encadrement : la supervision scientifique est assurée directement par le CTO (plus de 10 ans en ML appliqué, ex-CTO d'une startup de computer vision, publications ICCV / BMVC, un brevet US en estimation de profondeur, ancien encadrant de thèse CIFRE). • Durée : 5 à 6 mois, négociable jusqu'à 8. • Début : entre février et avril 2027, selon ton calendrier d'école. • Mois 1 et 2, cadrage : revue de littérature ciblée, définition du protocole expérimental, reproduction d'une première baseline. • Mois 2 à 4, expérimentation : itérations, mesures, ablations, analyse honnête des résultats y compris quand ils ne vont pas dans le sens attendu. • Mois 4 à 6, consolidation : rédaction du mémoire, restitution interne, démonstration. • Tout au long : un point hebdomadaire avec le CTO, des revues techniques régulières, et l'accès aux réunions produit et aux artistes pour comprendre le contexte d'usage réel. • Un vrai sujet de recherche, avec une contribution scientifique attendue, mesurable et défendable. Pas un stage « mets ce modèle en prod » déguisé. • Un encadrement scientifique serré par le CTO, en direct et chaque semaine. • Des moyens de calcul réels : tu auras du GPU pour tes expériences. • Lyon, ambiance startup, équipe tech resserrée où ton travail se voit. • 1 jour de télétravail par semaine. • Gratification de 1 200 à 1 400 € / mois selon profil. • Possibilité d'embauche en CDI à la fin du stage si le fit est bon. Indispensable : • Formation : dernière année d'école d'ingénieur (3A), M2 recherche, ou doctorant·e en césure, en CS / ML / vision / computer graphics. • Une vraie culture 3D. Tu sais ce que tu manipules : maillages, nuages de points, voxels, champs de distance signés ; topologie, normales, UV, matériaux. Tu as déjà ouvert un fichier 3D pour comprendre pourquoi il était cassé. C'est le point le plus discriminant de cette offre. • Rigueur expérimentale. Tu sais isoler une variable, construire une baseline, choisir ce que tu mesures, et tirer une conclusion honnête de résultats qui ne vont pas dans ton sens. Tu donnes toujours la taille de ton échantillon. • Solides bases en deep learning : tu as implémenté, entraîné et débuggé des modèles non triviaux, tu lis des papiers récents sans lutter. • Pratique sérieuse de PyTorch (ou équivalent), Python propre. • Une première expérience R&D tangible : stage en labo, projet de recherche encadré, contribution open source ML, publication étudiante. • Autonomie scientifique : tu creuses un sujet seul·e, tu identifies les bons papiers, tu sais quand demander de l'aide. • Bon niveau d'anglais scientifique. Les atouts qui font la différence : • un background geometry processing ou computer graphics académique (paramétrisation, remeshing, géométrie digitale, analyse de formes) ; • une expérience du post-training de LLM : apprentissage par renforcement, conception de fonctions de récompense, instrumentation d'évaluation ; • une expérience des métriques apprises et de leur validation contre du jugement humain ; • la pratique personnelle d'un outil DCC (Blender, Houdini, Maya) ; • une publication antérieure, ou une contribution open source significative ; • une sensibilité artiste, ou une pratique personnelle de la 3D, du jeu vidéo, de l'animation. • Étape 1, candidature : CV, et si tu en as, un lien vers tes travaux (dépôt de code, mémoire, publication, projets 3D). • Étape 2, premier échange : 30 minutes sur ton parcours et ce qui t'intéresse dans le sujet. • Étape 3, entretien scientifique : une heure de discussion sur un papier que tu as lu et un projet que tu as mené. Pas de test technique chronométré. On décide à l'issue de la troisième étape.

linkedin:4473511101.title: PhD Candidate in Access, Actors and Accountability: The Role of Researchers in AI Governance
linkedin:4473511101.desc: What is the role of researchers in the governance of AI systems and digital platforms? What legal exceptions and safeguards do researchers need to be able to play that role? And how can we organise productive interactions between researcher, policy makers, regulators, civil society and companies? Research and expertise have critical role in making sure that AI and digital technologies are safe, respectful of fundamental rights and beneficial to society, but we have yet to develop the legal and organisational frameworks to enable their work, while protecting their safety and academic freedom. If you want to help doing so, this position might be for you. Working at the UvA Join Us! Access, Actors and Accountability: The Role of Researchers in AI Governance Governing AI systems and digital platforms, identifying systemic risks and developing adequate policy responses is complex and requires research and expertise. In the new European Digital Framework, researchers are central stakeholder ins AI and platform governance, and regulations like the DSA and the AI Act, define prominent roles for them to produce evidence, audit big tech companies and public bodies, monitor the way AI technology impacts society and help to ensure transparency and accountability. At the same time, this role comes with new challenges for academic freedom, navigating dependencies on regulators and large technology companies, being meaningfully involved and heard, and sometimes even having to navigate issues around safety against personal attacks and threats to their safety. At the same time, the ability of independent researchers to study platforms and AI systems often depends on research exemptions and access rights, and so does the evidence base available to regulators. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do This doctoral project examines the legal position of researchers under the DSA and AI Act, and the research exemptions, safeguards and policy processes needed to allow independent researchers to generate evidence for regulatory learning and anticipatory governance without eroding legality or academic freedom. This research combines doctrinal, normative and comparative research with interviews (with academics, policy makers, civil society and other societal stakeholders) and participatory research to co-design how research exemptions and researcher-regulator feedback loops can be designed and operationalised. The work will build an evaluative analysis of exemption scope and adequacy, a typology of enablers and obstacles to researcher–policy engagement, and concrete proposals how to enable policy research while protecting academic freedom. You will work on a legal PhD thesis at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Amsterdam Law School, University of Amsterdam, as part of the REGULAIRE project. The PhD will provide the opportunity to contribute to the activities of the DSA Observatory, the AI, Media & Democracy Lab and the Amsterdam Law School Sectorplan initiative Democratic Digital Transformation (2026-2031) and offers a focused route into information law, platform and AI regulation. About REGULAIRE REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn to govern transformative technologies such as AI, quantum computing and neurotechnology. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions. Across the network, regulatory learning means treating regulation as a learning architecture that generates, tests and refines knowledge about what works, rather than as one-off rulemaking. Each researcher joins an international cohort, receives supervision across institutions and takes part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment. The network is coordinated by Prof. Urs Gasser at the Technical University of Munich (TUM). More specifically, you are expected to: Refine the research questions and design with the supervision team, and prepare ethics, data-management and open-science materials. Collect, manage and analyse research data using the approved project-specific methods. Complete a doctoral thesis and related research outputs under the doctoral programme and the REGULAIRE plan. Take part in local and network-wide training, cohort activities, network reviews, dissemination and practitioner engagement, including three residential summer schools and monthly paper development seminars. Undertake the planned three-month intersectoral secondment with EDMO – The European Digital Media Observatory (EDMO), Florence, Italy. Contribute to the research and activities of the AI, Media & Democracy Lab and the DSA Observatory. Contribute to research integrity, equality and diversity, open science and FAIR data practices. What We Ask Of You A Master's degree (or an equivalent qualification giving access to doctoral studies) in law, political science, media and communication studies, or related legal, social science and interdisciplinary fields, completed by the start date. A demonstrable interest in studying the relationship of law to digital technologies and services; Skills or a demonstrable interest in qualitative research, such as interviews and participatory design. Excellent command of written and spoken English. Willingness to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities. Fulfilment of the MSCA eligibility conditions listed below. A creative mind and strong critical and analytical skills; Collegial attitude and capacity to work not only independently but also in teams; Ability and willingness to organize workshops, lectures, and similar events (demonstrable experience with these activities a plus). If the vacancy appeals to you, but you are doubting whether you might be THE person we are looking for, please do apply? We encourage all qualified applicants, including minorities, women, people with disabilities, and members of other groups underrepresented in academia. We wish to create a research group that consists of persons who each contribute in their unique way to the team. Complementarity and not homogeneity is what we are looking for. Supervision, training and mobility Your supervision team will consist of Supervision team: Prof. Natali Helberger (University of Amsterdam), Prof. Joris van Hoboken (University of Amsterdam), an external supervisor from the REGULAIRE project network, and a sectoral mentor at the anticipated secondment host. The secondment enables the candidate to observe how a research-based civil society organisation engages in policy research, challenges involved and possible best practices. The candidate will be part of a supervisory team consisting of the primary supervisor at the host institution, an academic co-supervisor at a partner institution in another country, and a sectoral mentor at the secondment host. Candidates meet the primary supervisor at least monthly and the full team at least four times per year; progress and training are recorded in a personal Career Development Plan. Network-wide training includes three residential summer schools (regulatory learning and foresight at TUM; methods and analytics at BI Norwegian Business School; academic writing and impact at the University of St. Gallen), monthly paper development seminars, and annual network reviews aligned with major community events. Candidates obtain a minimum of twenty ECTS through local and network-wide training, of which at least ten from network-wide provision. This Is What We Offer You A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 12 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is January 1st 2027. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3.204 to € 4.051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile 'PhD student' is applicable. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable. The UvA offers excellent possibilities for further professional development and education. What Else Do We Offer a position where own initiative and input are highly valued; an enthusiastic and dynamic team that is open to new colleagues; an inspiring academic and international working environment in the heart of Amsterdam. Your place at the UvA You will work in this team The University of Amsterdam is the largest university in the Netherlands, with the broadest spectrum of degree programmes. It is an intellectual hub with 39,000 students, 6,000 employees and 3,000 doctoral students who are all committed to a culture of inquiring minds. With over 5,000 students and more than 500 staff members, the Amsterdam Law School is one of the larger law faculties in the Netherlands. We educate lawyers who know how to apply the law effectively with the aim of making a real contribution to solving social problems. The Amsterdam Law School stands for progressive and trail-blazing education and research, for stronger legal institutions, solutions to social problems and a better and juster society. The Institute for Information Law (IViR), officially established in 1989, is one of the largest research centers in the field of information law in Europe, and one of the largest of its kind in the world. The Institute engages in cutting-edge research into fundamental and topical aspects of information law, and provides a forum for critical debate about the social, cultural and political aspects of regulating information markets. This is how we at the Amsterdam Law School view the role of law in a constantly changing (international) society. Ihr Arbeitsort wird das Fraunhofer IWM in Freiburg sein. Ihre Aufgaben Im Fokus dieses Teilprojektes steht die mikrostrukturbasierte Modellierung und numerische Analyse von Hochgeschwindigkeits-Scherschneidprozessen (HGSS) für hochfeste Blechwerkstoffe und deren Übertragung auf Prozessebene. Die im Werkstoff auftretende adiabatische Scherbandbildung spielt hier eine entscheidende Rolle. Für die Beschreibung der Wechselwirkung zwischen der Mikrostruktur, dem Prozess und der adiabatischen Scherbandbildung sollen geeignete Modellansätze weiterentwickelt und implementiert werden. Auf Basis umfangreicher Simulationsstudien werden zudem Methoden des maschinellen Lernens eingesetzt, um die Prozess-Struktur-Eigenschafts-Beziehungen zu korrelieren. Die Validierung der Modellansätze erfolgt durch den Abgleich anhand von experimentellen Daten auf der Mikroskala des Werkstoffs und auf Prozessebene. Ihr Profil Abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master) in Maschinenbau, Materialwissenschaften, Computational Engineering oder eines vergleichbaren Fachgebiets Fundierte Kenntnisse in der Kontinuumsmechanik, Werkstoffmodellierung und finite Elemente Simulation Grundlegendes Verständnis der Zusammenhänge zwischen Mikrostruktur, plastischer Deformation und Werkstoffeigenschaften Kenntnisse in den Bereichen Kristallplastizität, mikrostrukturbasiere Materialmodellierung oder maschinellen Lernens sind von Vorteil Gute Programmierkenntnisse (z. B. Python, Fortran) inkl. ML-Bibliotheken sowie erste Linux-Erfahrung Erfahrung mit FEM-Solvern, vorzugsweise LS-DYNA HPC-Erfahrung von Vorteil Erwartet werden ein hohes Maß an Eigeninitiative zur Lösung komplexer wissenschaftlicher Fragestellungen, sowie das Interesse zur interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit in einem experimentell und numerisch ausgerichteten Forschungsverbund Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sowie verhandlungssichere Englischkenntnisse Wir bieten Forschung mit Wirkung : Arbeiten Sie an Themen von gesellschaftlicher Relevanz – in einem exzellenten wissenschaftlichen Umfeld, das Veränderungen möglich macht. indeed:c73f3515b96139c9.title: PhD in Safe Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints
indeed:c73f3515b96139c9.desc: Ledig stilling PhD in Safe Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints Aalborg Ansøgningsfrist: 29.11.2026 Afdeling: Department of Electronic Systems Ref. nummer: 2026/1218 Ansættelsestype: Fuldtid Aalborg Ansøgningsfrist: 29.11.2026 Afdeling: Department of Electronic Systems Ref. nummer: 2026/1218 Ansættelsestype: Fuldtid Ledig stilling PhD in Safe Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints Aalborg Ansøgningsfrist: 29.11.2026 Afdeling: Department of Electronic Systems Ref. nummer: 2026/1218 Ansættelsestype: Fuldtid Aalborg Ansøgningsfrist: 29.11.2026 Afdeling: Department of Electronic Systems Ref. nummer: 2026/1218 Ansættelsestype: Fuldtid The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a PhD stipend in the field of Safe Learning Based Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints within the general study programme Electrical and Electronic Engineering; starting on 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The PhD Fellow will be based at the Automation and Control Section in Aalborg. In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk. Description of the position How can a team of autonomous robots operate safely and make progress when communication deteriorates, the environment is only partially known, and the team must continually reorganise? This PhD position addresses this challenge through research on safe and resilient planning, control, and coordination of heterogeneous robotic systems in demanding underground environments. The position combines scientific research with substantial hands-on engineering. You will develop and analyse new algorithms, implement robotic software, build realistic simulation and digital-twin environments, and carry out systematic experiments with physical robot platforms. We are looking for a researcher who enjoys connecting mathematical ideas to reliable real-world robotic systems. Description of the project The ROX6G EU Horizon project aims to develop autonomous robotic systems for exploring and collecting data in hazardous, poorly documented underground mines. Its heterogeneous robot teams combine exploration, mapping, sensing, and sampling with mobile, multi-hop 5G/6G connectivity. Because robots also act as communication nodes, they must adapt their movement and team roles to sustain communication without relying on fixed infrastructure installed throughout the mine. The project is coordinated by AAU. In addition, within ROX6G, AAU leads the activities on learning based multi-robot coordination and reconfiguration for connectivity preservation and on digital-twin generation and multimodal visualisation. The PhD candidate will contribute to both activities, collaborating with international partners across robotics, communications, sensing, and geological modelling. The main core of the PhD will focus on developing theoretical, algorithmic, and real-time implementation framework for on the fly autonomy of multi-robot control systems in uncertain and limited environments. In addition, methods will be evaluated through simulation, laboratory experiments, and project-level system integration and validation, with attention to safety, connectivity, and practical mission performance. Your work tasks The PhD fellow will be responsible for: Conducting research on safe and resilient learning based planning, control, and coordination of multi-robot systems operating under constraints and uncertainty. Actively contributing to the formulation and refinement of research questions within the doctoral project. Taking an active role in planning, implementing, and, when necessary, adapting the research plan. Designing, implementing, and evaluating the developed algorithms in realistic robotic simulation environments and on physical robotic platforms. Contributing to the development and implementation of digital twins by integrating robotic sensor data, to support real-time visualization, monitoring, and autonomous decision-making. Publishing research results in leading international journals and conferences, and presenting findings at project meetings and international scientific venues. Your competencies The successful candidate will hold a Master’s degree in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Control Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field, with a strong foundation in robotics, autonomous systems, planning, and/or control theory. We particularly value strong programming skills in Python and/or C++, familiarity with robotic software frameworks such as ROS/ROS 2, and demonstrated ability to implement, integrate, test, and troubleshoot robotic systems. Motivation for hands-on work with physical robot platforms, sensors, simulation, and experimental setups is important for this position. Experience with one or more of the following areas will be an advantage: multi-robot systems and graph-based coordination; safety-critical, robust, or optimisation-based control; autonomous navigation, localisation, simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM), or sensor fusion; simulation and digital-twin development using tools such as Gazebo, Isaac Sim, or Webots. indeed:4e363bcef68c9ea4.title: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
indeed:4e363bcef68c9ea4.desc: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology. We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1 st , 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences. Research environment The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research. The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad. The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology. Project description The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez . The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1 st , 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists. The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset. In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties. The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available. Qualifications Before the start date of September 1 st , 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study. The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required. The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required. For further information about the project, please contact: Anthony Vincent Fernandez Department of Psychology University of Southern Denmark (SDU) E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided. Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation): A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”. Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1 st , 2027. Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read. A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview. At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan. Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities. Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process. For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center. Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University . Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply. Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated [AF1] . Closing date January 15 th , 2027 We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date. Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students. The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order) Salary and Working Conditions at SDU PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement. Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98 per year. The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future. As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital. The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background. indeed:5b38493aa2dc7171.desc: The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a PhD stipend in the field of Safe Learning Based Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints within the general study programme Electrical and Electronic Engineering; starting on 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk. Description of the position How can a team of autonomous robots operate safely and make progress when communication deteriorates, the environment is only partially known, and the team must continually reorganise? This PhD position addresses this challenge through research on safe and resilient planning, control, and coordination of heterogeneous robotic systems in demanding underground environments. The position combines scientific research with substantial hands-on engineering. You will develop and analyse new algorithms, implement robotic software, build realistic simulation and digital-twin environments, and carry out systematic experiments with physical robot platforms. We are looking for a researcher who enjoys connecting mathematical ideas to reliable real-world robotic systems. Description of the project The ROX6G EU Horizon project aims to develop autonomous robotic systems for exploring and collecting data in hazardous, poorly documented underground mines. Its heterogeneous robot teams combine exploration, mapping, sensing, and sampling with mobile, multi-hop 5G/6G connectivity. The project is coordinated by AAU. In addition, within ROX6G, AAU leads the activities on learning based multi-robot coordination and reconfiguration for connectivity preservation and on digital-twin generation and multimodal visualisation. indeed:e0e164140fbadd54.title: Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), 3 positions, Development of Data Science and AI for Spatial Data
indeed:e0e164140fbadd54.desc: The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in the field of Development of Data Science and AI for Spatial Data at the School of Computing on the Kuopio campus. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). Please find more information below and submit your application by 17 November 2026. Role and salary The demand for minerals required for energy transition and digitalisation is expanding mining faster than our ability to understand its impacts. MINE-THE-GAP (website), funded by the European Research Council (ERC), combines satellite imagery, mining data reports, and AI to map mining activities and their impacts worldwide and provide the information needed for more transparent and sustainable mining. We are seeking three motivated Doctoral Researchers (PhD Students) to join the project, each leading their own thesis on mapping different aspects of mining. As part of the MINE-THE-GAP team, you will, as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), have the opportunity to apply your data science and programming skills to a global sustainability challenge and to become an expert in handling large Earth observation datasets and scalable AI. We offer three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in a research group with strong international visibility. You will receive hands-on training in the processing of large Earth observation and spatial datasets, as well as in scalable AI methods, developing highly sought-after skills for careers in academia, industry, government, and non-governmental organizations. The position provides opportunities for international collaboration and research visits abroad through an extensive network of partner institutions, including the German Aerospace Center (DLR), GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Monash University Indonesia, and the University of Melbourne. You will benefit from close supervision, mentoring, and a supportive team environment, along with dedicated funding for conference participation, workshops, and scientific publications. One Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) will be recruited for each of the following three research topics: mining land use: semantic segmentation of satellite images to map mining areas (e.g., open pits, waste rock piles, tailings dams) mining waste: predicting terrain height changes from radar and optical satellite image time series to estimate mining waste minerals and commodities: image classification with multispectral and hyperspectral data to identify the minerals and commodities of mining sites. Within your chosen research topic, you will build, train, and validate scalable deep learning and computer vision models using large, multi-modal Earth observation data (e.g., Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, LiDAR, hyperspectral). You will work closely with the principal investigator, Victor Maus, postdoctoral researchers, and international collaborators, publish your results in international journals, present them at conferences, and contribute to open science. Your main duty as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) is to conduct research for the doctoral dissertation and to complete postgraduate studies. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). The positions will be filled for a fixed term due to the Doctoral Researcher’s (PhD Student’s) own doctoral dissertation work and studies. A trial period is applied to all new members of the staff. The salary of the position is determined in accordance with the salary system for Finnish universities. The salary comprises two components: a job-related salary element and a personal salary element. For a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), the job-related salary element is based on levels 2–4 of the job requirement level chart for teaching and research staff depending on the stage of the applicant’s doctoral research and postgraduate studies. The personal salary element is 6–50% of the job-related salary element. At the beginning of the employment, the total salary will be approximately EUR 2,710–2,845 /month. Our requirements and expectations We require you to be eligible for postgraduate studies; i.e., to hold a Master’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Geoinformatics, Statistics, or a related field) awarded by a university or by a university of applied sciences, or to have completed an applicable study programme abroad which in the awarding country gives eligibility for corresponding postgraduate education meet the student admission criteria for the LUMETO doctoral programme (Doctoral Programme in Science, Forestry and Technology, website) have a good command of written and spoken English. Students in the final stages of their Master’s degree may also apply provided that they complete their degree and deliver a copy of their degree certificate to the faculty by 15 December 2026. Applicants who do not yet have the right to pursue postgraduate studies at the University of Eastern Finland are not required to apply for study rights at the application stage. If the applicant is selected for the position and applies for postgraduate study rights, the selection will be conditional until the right to pursue postgraduate studies in the faculty’s doctoral programme has been granted. The application for postgraduate study rights is submitted through the Studyinfo (Opintopolku) service. Other requirements good programming skills (e.g., Python/R) interest in machine learning and spatial data. The following will be considered an advantage experience with machine learning or deep learning (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) or strong motivation to learn these skills experience with Earth observation or geospatial data, desirable, but we encourage anyone with a strong willingness to learn to apply experience with cloud computing or collaborative software development (e.g., GitHub) is also welcome. Your benefits You will have access to the university’s staff benefits, including the opportunity for flexible multi-location work excellent opportunities for professional development and continuous learning extensive occupational health care a broad selection of staff training staff discount on lunch in our campus restaurants, as well as on a range of other services affordable sports services. Please read more in the Work at UEF section on our website. You will have an opportunity to work in meaningful as part of our international, creative, participatory and inclusive academic community. Enjoy your life in Finland! Known for its cleanliness, welfare know-how, modern technology and superb education system, Finland is an exotic and safe country to work in. Please visit the Life in Finland section on our website to learn more. How to apply? Submit your application by using our electronic application form no later than 17 November 2026 by 23:59 (midnight) Finnish time (UTC+2). Please note that you must include the following appendices in your application CV (Template for CV, TENK web page) a list of publications (Instructions, Research Council of Finland Web page) copies of your academic degree certificates / diplomas, and copies of certificates / diplomas relating to your language proficiency, if not indicated in the academic degree certificates/diplomas a transcript of records a motivation letter (max. 1 page) describing your interest in the position and research project, your background, as well as your career aspirations and your motivation for engaging in doctoral-level research. In the cover letter, indicate your preferred topic(s), for example, by ranking the topics in order of preference or specifying whether you are applying for one or multiple topics. External evaluation will be used in the recruitment process. If your degree certificate is not in English, Finnish, or Swedish, you must provide official English translations of your degree certificate documents. All translations must be issued by the awarding educational institution or an authorized translator. Each page of the official translation must bear the translator's stamp and/or signature. Official translations must be accurate translations of the original documents. Translations made by the applicants themselves will not be accepted. Questions? For further information on the position, please contact Professor Markku Tukiainen, email: markku.tukiainen@uef.fi, tel. +358 29 445 3653. For further information on the application procedure, please contact HR Specialist Iiris Korhonen, email: iiris.korhonen@uef.fi, tel. +358 29 4458161 or HR Specialist Noora Hämäläinen, email: noora.hamalainen@uef.fi, tel. +358 29 4458302. Haemme kolmea väitöskirjatutkijaa Itä-Suomen yliopistolle. Tehtävät sijoittuvat luonnontieteiden, metsätieteiden ja tekniikan tiedekuntaan tietojenkäsittelytieteiden laitokselle Kuopion kampukselle. Tehtävät alkavat 1.2.2027 (tai sopimuksen mukaan) ja ne täytetään kolmen vuoden määräajaksi. Tehtävissä tehtäväkohtainen palkanosa on vaativuustasoluokittelussa tasoilla 2–4. Lisäksi maksetaan henkilökohtaiseen suoriutumiseen perustuvaa palkanosaa, joka on 6–50 % tehtäväkohtaisesta palkanosasta. Tehtävissä edellytetään hyvää englannin kielen taitoa. Lue tarkemmat tiedot tehtävistä ja hakuohjeet yllä olevasta englanninkielisestä ilmoituksesta. Jätäthän hakemuksesi englanniksi. Hakuaika tehtäviin päättyy 17.11.2026. The Faculty of Science, Forestry and Technology operates on the Kuopio and Joensuu campuses of the University of Eastern Finland. The mission of the faculty is to carry out internationally recognised scientific research and to offer research-education in the fields of natural sciences, forestry and technology. The faculty invests in all of the strategic research areas of the university. The faculty’s environments for research and learning are international, modern and multidisciplinary. The faculty has approximately 2,650 Bachelor’s and Master’s degree students and some 440 postgraduate students. The number of staff amounts to 650. The University of Eastern Finland (UEF) is the most multidisciplinary university in Finland. Our university employs approximately 3,200 employees, and our community includes approximately 17,000 degree students and 16,000 adult education students. Our campuses are located in Joensuu and Kuopio. We represent the world’s cutting edge of research in many fields and produce research-based knowledge, which is made openly available to benefit everyone. Learn more about our university at www.uef.fi/en. Read also about UEF as a working community and employer and the career stories of our employees. indeed:8dd8c05708d7c59b.title: PhD Researcher (m/f/d): Understanding climate risks to global food security
indeed:8dd8c05708d7c59b.desc: Tasks Investigate feedback mechanisms and processes behind acceleration in extreme weather trends Design targeted climate model experiments and analyse large ensembles to test conditions under which tail-specific feedbacks are triggered Apply explainable AI (XAI) and other advanced statistical methods to uncover non-linear interactions between physical drivers of extremes Evaluate how well climate models represent these tail processes against observations and reanalysis Investigate drivers, statistics and impacts of record-breaking events in current and future climates, in collaboration with the other group members Publish in leading journals, present at international conferences Help organise group events Co-supervise PhD students Profile Essential Master's degree (or equivalent) in climate science, atmospheric science, physics, geosciences, environmental science, statistics or a related field Programming skills (e.g. Python, R) and experience handling gridded or time-series data Strong motivation for independent, interdisciplinary research Good command of written and spoken English Advantageous Experience with climate model output, reanalysis data or extreme event analysis Knowledge of extreme value statistics, compound events or time-series methods Experience with agricultural modelling and agricultural datasets Experience with machine learning or causal methods Previous research experience, e.g. a Master's thesis in a related topic Our offer The position will begin on the 1st of January 2027 though some flexibility in start date is possible. Remuneration will follow the standard PhD salaries given in the Max Planck Society which correspond to 65% of EG 13 TvöD (Bund). The position includes 31 days of annual leave. We also offer attractive and family-friendly flextime and options for remote work. Additional benefits include an employer subsidy for public transport, access to training opportunities within the Max Planck Society, as well as language and health courses. The successful candidate can apply for admission to our graduate school “International Max Planck Research School for Modeling the Anthropocene”. The Max Planck Society is committed to employing more individuals with disabilities and especially encourages them to apply. We are also committed to encouraging diversity and actively challenging biases based on gender, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion and other components of identity. We were honored with the TOTAL E-QUALITY award for the first time in 2023 for our commitment. The Max Planck Society supports the compatibility of family and career and is certified according to the "berufundfamilie" (“job and family”) audit. Your application should include: A cover letter A CV of no more than 3 pages A summary of research interests with max. 2 pages If applicable a list of relevant scientific, peer-reviewed publications related to the position or a copy of the candidate’s MA/MPhil/MSc thesis Contacts of two referees Any relevant certificates Position remains open until filled. About us The Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology (MPI-GEA) was founded in summer 2022 and is a dynamically growing, highly-interdisciplinary and international research institution. The research focuses on modeling and analyzing the interrelationships between biophysical and human-made systems, looking from the deep past to the future. The institute examines how humanity has driven the emergence of the Anthropocene – the period in which human activities began significantly impacting our planet’s climate and ecosystems – and identifying potential intervention points towards a more sustainable future. The Carl Zeiss Stiftung Independent Research Group on High-End Climate Risks (CZS-HECR) at MPI-GEA works towards an end-to-end understanding of worst-case climate outcomes, from unprecedented and compounding extremes to their societal impacts. The group combines fundamental physical process understanding rooted in climate physics and Earth System analyses, targeted climate model experiments, advanced statistics, including machine-learning- and explainable AI to deliver usable climate risk estimates under current and future climates for core societal sectors such as health, food, energy and finance. Doctoral researchers join an interdisciplinary team, and a broad international network are provided with highly competitive research conditions including generous support for travel and research visits.
