indeed:a5a5bbbac06f6c05.title: PhD Position: Biodiversity for Nature-Inclusive Dairy Farming
indeed:a5a5bbbac06f6c05.desc: Employment 0.8 - 1.0 FTE Gross monthly salary € 3,204 - € 4,051 Required background Research University Degree Organizational unit Faculty of Science Application deadline 22 November 2026 In this PhD position, you will develop integrated and innovative biodiversity monitoring and data analysis techniques to aid in the decision-making of businesses within the dairy sector for the benefit of biodiversity. Biodiversity recovery is essential to sustain resilient food systems, robust businesses and healthy societies. A transition to a more nature-inclusive dairy sector in the Netherlands would be pivotal to biodiversity recovery, because of its influence in shaping landscapes through land use and management, and because of its socio-economic relevance. To properly assess the suitability and effectiveness of key performance indicators and the effects of management practices on local biodiversity, it is crucial to monitor, for example, breeding birds, bats, insect communities and soil life (depending on the KPI). By adapting and developing biomonitoring techniques programmes at dairy farms that are in line with long-running or recently developed monitoring schemes, you will utilise the full potential of datasets and methods to quantify biodiversity gains resulting from nature-inclusive farming as well as the potential for further biodiversity recovery. Novel instruments such as DIOPSIS smart insect cameras, LED buckets and bat loggers generate huge amounts of biodiversity data from across the Netherlands and can be used to detect and identify biodiversity automatically. National schemes like the breeding bird monitoring project, the butterfly monitoring scheme and the dragon fly monitoring scheme (standardised and coordinated by NGOs such as Sovon and Dutch Butterfly Conservation, and powered by thousands of citizen scientists) generate standardised long-term trends based on thousands of plots around the country. You will design novel, integrated analyses to quantify the effects on biodiversity from existing and new data while accounting for factors such as observers' bias, weather and surrounding landscape configuration. In this project you will: Bring coherence across the diverse monitoring systems and KPI developed so far and adapt sets of KPI's suited to peat soils. Document the relationships between different nature-inclusive measures taken by heterogeneous farm types, and the different aspects of biodiversity and ecosystem services considered. The precise type of monitoring and the number and locations of monitoring points will be decided in collaboration with stakeholders. Further develop effective and integrated monitoring to guide decision-making in businesses and develop reward schemes. Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time. Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate . At Radboud University, I can fully focus on expanding my expertise while learning from my peers and mentors. Noemí Segura-Solé PhD candidate in Microbial Ecology Read Noemí's story Does this sound like you? You have an MSc degree in Biology, Ecology, Environmental Sciences or a related discipline with an interest in social sciences. You have good communication and writing skills in both English and Dutch. You have designed scientific studies, and it would be advantageous if you have experience with writing scientific and non-scientific manuscripts for publication. You have an affinity for, and proven experience with, computer programming, statistical modelling and large datasets, and you know how to perform qualitative analyses based on quantitative data. You have an understanding of field work in practice, have a passion for biodiversity and are keen to absorb and share knowledge with others. You are a team player, eager to work on a truly interdisciplinary project. What we offer you We will give you a temporary employment contract (0.8 FTE 5- year contract - 1.0 FTE 4- year contract) of 1.5 years, after which your performance will be evaluated. If the evaluation is positive, your contract will be extended by 2.5 years (4-year contract) or 3.5 years (5-year contract). You will receive a starting salary of €3,204 gross per month based on a 38-hour working week, which will increase to €4,051 from the fourth year onwards (salary scale P). You will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8,3% end-of-year bonus. You will receive extra days off. With full-time employment, you can choose between 30 or 41 days of annual leave instead of the statutory 20. Additional employment conditions Work and science require good employment practices. Radboud University's primary and secondary employment conditions reflect this. You can make arrangements for the best possible work-life balance with flexible working hours, various leave arrangements and working from home. You are also able to compose part of your employment conditions yourself. For example, exchange income for extra leave days and receive a reimbursement for your sports membership. In addition, you receive a 34% discount on the sports and cultural activities at Radboud University as an employee. And, of course, we offer a good pension plan. We also give you plenty of room and responsibility to develop your talents and realise your ambitions. Therefore, we provide various training and development schemes. Where you will be working The Department of Ecology at Radboud University is a dynamic, collaborative and interdisciplinary team. We are a young and ambitious group of ecologists committed to preserving and promoting biodiversity and ecosystem health. Our department brings together aquatic and terrestrial ecologists who focus on plants, animals and microorganisms and their interactions in a changing world. We are dedicated to conducting timely and innovative research that addresses both scientific and societal challenges. Your research will be integrated into ongoing studies in biodiversity research and applied ecology, with opportunities to collaborate with colleagues across departments. Dr Eelke Jongejans will be one of the two main supervisors for the project. The Radboud Institute for Biological and Environmental Sciences (RIBES) is committed to equality of opportunity, fairness and inclusivity, striving to be a place where everyone feels respected and valued, and creativity and innovation are fostered and encouraged. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ethnicities, sexual orientations, abilities and backgrounds, and particularly encourage those from underrepresented groups to apply. SoortenNL is an umbrella for organisations that collect and interpret biodiversity data from surveys and large monitoring schemes carried out by citizen scientists. It is both a social network and an information landscape. Dr Sander Turnhout of SoortenNL will be the co-supervisor of this project. In this interdisciplinary research project (DECISION: Dairy and Ecology: Co-Innovating buSIness Operations for Nature) you will closely collaborate with three other PhD candidates and a postdoctoral researcher working in animal sciences and social sciences at Wageningen University and Erasmus University. The research consortium also includes agribusinesses, financial businesses, farmer associations and governmental organisations. Faculty of Science The Faculty of Science (FNWI), part of Radboud University, engages in groundbreaking research and excellent education. In doing so, we push the boundaries of scientific knowledge and pass that knowledge on to the next generation. We seek solutions to major societal challenges, such as cybercrime and climate change and work on major scientific challenges, such as those in the quantum world. At the same time, we prepare our students for careers both within and outside the scientific field. Currently, more than 1,300 colleagues contribute to research and education, some as researchers and lecturers, others as technical and administrative support officers. The faculty has a strong international character with staff from more than 70 countries. Together, we work in an informal, accessible and welcoming environment, with attention and space for personal and professional development for all. Radboud University At Radboud University, we aim to make an impact through our work. We achieve this by conducting groundbreaking research, providing high-quality education, offering excellent support, and fostering collaborations within and outside the university. In doing so, we contribute indispensably to a healthy, free world with equal opportunities for all. To accomplish this, we need even more colleagues who, based on their expertise, are willing to search for answers. We advocate for an inclusive community and welcome employees with diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives. If you want to learn more about working at Radboud University, follow our Instagram account and read stories from our colleagues. Is this the job for you? indeed:0945708fa5b3f4d8.desc: The Department of Biomedical Engineering offers top-level education and research in one of the most relevant and exciting scientific disciplines of the 21st century: engineering health. In combining engineering and life sciences, through challenge-based learning and a multidisciplinary approach in collaboration with hospitals, industry and others, the department addresses the great challenges of the future, striving to improve healthcare and society as a whole. Introduction Do you want to make cardiac MRI safer for patients and the environment? Join PRIMA-CMR, a EuroTech Universities Alliance project between TU/e and the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and help to develop trustworthy generative AI that makes it possible to scan with far less contrast agent. Job Description Cardiac MRI gives unmatched insight into heart disease, but some of its most important exams depend on gadolinium-based contrast agents. Gadolinium can build up in the body, cannot be given to all patients, and is now an environmental pollutant. A large reduction in the dose would make cardiac MRI safer and available to more patients. At low doses, however, the images no longer contain enough signal for a reliable diagnosis. Current AI methods can make images that look realistic, but they cannot guarantee that what they show is real. We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop new generative AI methods that recover diagnostic information from low-dose cardiac MRI in a reliable and trustworthy way. Your work will combine knowledge of MR imaging physics, patient-specific clinical information, and uncertainty quantification. The aim is a model whose outputs clinicians can trust, and which tells them when it is not certain. You will validate the methods on real clinical data together with our clinical partners. This PhD position is part of PRIMA-CMR, a collaborative project within the EuroTech Universities Alliance programme. You will be based at TU/e and spend six months at TUM in the group of prof. Julia Schnabel, which is a world leader in generative and multimodal AI. You will also work with international clinical and academic partners across Europe. Julia Schnabel (TUM). In this project you will push the limit of spectroscopic analysis by developing novel photonic chips working at ultralow light levels (down to femtowatts). These chips will form the core of sensors which are crucial for advancing healthcare and the energy transition. Job Description Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) allows characterizing materials and tissues, and it is widely used in industry. indeed:2577cc9168b6a6c5.desc: The Department of Applied Physics and Science Education is a research-driven department housing high-quality educational programs, all featuring strong connections between research and education. Our research is clustered in three focal areas: Fluids, Bio and Soft Matter (FBSM); Plasmas and Beams (PB); and Nano, Quantum and Photonics (NQP). Introduction Are you excited to solve technical challenges with a real-world application? Are you eager to build something truly unique in the world? Job Description Development of a pulsed electron source with extreme transverse bunch brightness, based on photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms, for time-resolved protein crystallography. Context: ERC-funded project “Cool T-ReX” Goal: Develop a unique and innovative instrument to enable time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons (and be the first in the world in doing so). Scientific relevance: Understanding how proteins function is crucial to improving medicine and unraveling processes that are fundamental to life. Time-resolved protein crystallography uniquely allows following the conformational change of a protein with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, yielding a “molecular movie” of how the protein performs its function. This is currently only possible on large-scale X-ray facilities. In this project we will build the very first instrument that can make such movies through time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons rather than X-rays, on a laboratory-scale setup. Next, through collaboration with leading research groups in time-resolved protein crystallography, we will demonstrate the instrument’s capabilities in time-resolved crystallography experiments on photo-active proteins with medical relevance (and used in the field of optogenetics, awarded this year’s Nobel Prize in Medicine!). Your role: Drive the development of this unique instrument. You will build on our research group’s two decades of experience in building electron sources based on the photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms. This technique has demonstrated electron pulses with record-low transverse temperatures, corresponding to a high transverse coherence, as needed for protein crystallography. In this project we will push this transverse coherence even further, making use of some of the unique capabilities of this source technology. The result will be an electron beam with a “transverse bunch brightness” that is three orders of magnitude beyond the current state of the art. To reach this ambitious goal, you will work with a team of experienced technicians, a second PhD student, a PostDoc, and the PI (Julius Huijts). We are part of the larger Coherence and Quantum Technology group in the Department of Applied Physics. You can work in a team, are open to new ideas, can communicate with people outside your own field. You take initiative, are able to organize your own work load. linkedin:4471905926.title: 2 Doctoral Researchers in Reinforcement Learning
linkedin:4471905926.desc: Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 16 000 students and 5 200 employees, including 446 professors. Our campus is in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland. Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community. We are currently seeking two highly motivated doctoral researchers to join the Cyber-physical Systems Group at Aalto University’s School of Electrical Engineering for an ERC Starting Grant-funded project focused on continual reinforcement learning for real-world systems. The grant provides a stable, well-resourced four-year research environment to tackle a problem that classical RL theory is not built for: real systems don’t reset, failures can be irreversible, and the real world keeps changing. Standard RL finds policies by optimizing over many hypothetical futures. Under non-ergodic dynamics, such an average may differ arbitrarily from what the individual agent experiences as it lives out one trajectory over time. Furthermore, RL typically seeks a time-invariant policy that cannot adapt to a changing environment. This project addresses both challenges simultaneously, combining trajectory-centric objectives with adaptive, context-dependent policies. This enables autonomous vehicles to adapt to seasonal changes over years, manufacturing systems to evolve with production demands without downtime, and medical monitoring to personalize to patients over decades. The successful candidates will develop fundamental theory and practical algorithms that move reinforcement learning closer to real-world systems. Position 1 will focus on trajectory-centric optimization, Position 2 on adaptive policies, and both will work jointly to integrate the two approaches into a single RL algorithm. While the work is mainly methodological and theoretically focused, our Aalto robot lab offers the possibility to evaluate the algorithms through practical experiments, e.g., on robot arms or quadruped robots. Research focus This project sits at the intersection of two problems: connecting ergodicity theory to reinforcement learning is a very recent development, and enabling RL agents to safely detect and adapt to a changing environment is a timely and active research area. Combining trajectory-centric objectives and adaptive, context-aware policies is new territory. The two doctoral researchers will drive this forward from these two complementary angles and will work closely together to integrate both into a single algorithm: Developing theory for trajectory-centric stochastic optimization under non-ergodic dynamics; Implementing practical RL algorithms that optimize long-term performance of individual agents; Developing change detection algorithms to infer when a policy is no longer valid and needs to be adapted; Implementing efficient policy-adaptation algorithms with safety guarantees; Integrating those advances into state-of-the-art RL algorithms; Validating the algorithms in relevant simulation environments and hardware experiments. Requirements Eligible candidates should have Master’s degree in computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or related fields; Fluent written and verbal communication skills in English; Ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a research team. If you are chosen for this position, you will apply for the study right in doctoral studies at Aalto University School of Electrical Engineering. Thus, please see the student information and admission criteria at https://www.aalto.fi/en/study-options/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-electrical-engineering. Desired background We are looking for candidates with a strong background in one or more of the following areas: Stochastic processes, ideally including a background in ergodicity theory; Reinforcement learning, dynamic programming, and Markov decision processes; Programming skills (Python). What We Offer Fully funded doctoral researcher’s position at Aalto University, which is consistently ranked among the top universities in Europe; The position is fixed term and follows the school’s standard 2+2 model. It will be made initially for two years, with a six-month probationary period, and extended by two further years after a successful mid-term review, giving a total duration of four years; The position starts in January 2027 or as mutually agreed; The starting salary for a doctoral researcher is 3143 €/month; Opportunity to work on a high-impact research project; You will join a young and dynamic research group with ample opportunities for collaboration and exchange of ideas. The group is well connected internationally, with active research ties to institutions including RWTH Aachen University, KTH Stockholm, and the London Mathematical Laboratory, among others, and there is potential for research visits to these and other partners over the course of the PhD. Join PRIMA-CMR, a EuroTech Universities Alliance project between TU/e and the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and help to develop trustworthy generative AI that makes it possible to scan with far less contrast agent. Job Description Cardiac MRI gives unmatched insight into heart disease, but some of its most important exams depend on gadolinium-based contrast agents. Gadolinium can build up in the body, cannot be given to all patients, and is now an environmental pollutant. A large reduction in the dose would make cardiac MRI safer and available to more patients. At low doses, however, the images no longer contain enough signal for a reliable diagnosis. Current AI methods can make images that look realistic, but they cannot guarantee that what they show is real. We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop new generative AI methods that recover diagnostic information from low-dose cardiac MRI in a reliable and trustworthy way. Your work will combine knowledge of MR imaging physics, patient-specific clinical information, and uncertainty quantification. The aim is a model whose outputs clinicians can trust, and which tells them when it is not certain. You will validate the methods on real clinical data together with our clinical partners. Julia Schnabel (TUM). linkedin:4482069109.desc: The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in the field of Development of Data Science and AI for Spatial Data at the School of Computing on the Kuopio campus. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). Please find more information below and submit your application by 17 November 2026. Role and salary The demand for minerals required for energy transition and digitalisation is expanding mining faster than our ability to understand its impacts. MINE-THE-GAP (website), funded by the European Research Council (ERC), combines satellite imagery, mining data reports, and AI to map mining activities and their impacts worldwide and provide the information needed for more transparent and sustainable mining. We are seeking three motivated Doctoral Researchers (PhD Students) to join the project, each leading their own thesis on mapping different aspects of mining. As part of the MINE-THE-GAP team, you will, as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), have the opportunity to apply your data science and programming skills to a global sustainability challenge and to become an expert in handling large Earth observation datasets and scalable AI. We offer three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in a research group with strong international visibility. You will receive hands-on training in the processing of large Earth observation and spatial datasets, as well as in scalable AI methods, developing highly sought-after skills for careers in academia, industry, government, and non-governmental organizations. The position provides opportunities for international collaboration and research visits abroad through an extensive network of partner institutions, including the German Aerospace Center (DLR), GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Monash University Indonesia, and the University of Melbourne. You will benefit from close supervision, mentoring, and a supportive team environment, along with dedicated funding for conference participation, workshops, and scientific publications. One Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) will be recruited for each of the following three research topics: mining land use: semantic segmentation of satellite images to map mining areas (e.g., open pits, waste rock piles, tailings dams) mining waste: predicting terrain height changes from radar and optical satellite image time series to estimate mining waste minerals and commodities: image classification with multispectral and hyperspectral data to identify the minerals and commodities of mining sites. Within your chosen research topic, you will build, train, and validate scalable deep learning and computer vision models using large, multi-modal Earth observation data (e.g., Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, LiDAR, hyperspectral). You will work closely with the principal investigator, Victor Maus, postdoctoral researchers, and international collaborators, publish your results in international journals, present them at conferences, and contribute to open science. linkedin:4482083127.title: PhD scholarship in fungal genomics and predictive modelling - DTU Food
linkedin:4482083127.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
linkedin:4482083127.desc: Job Description Fungi are increasingly causing health issues globally. Such infections are not only increasing in humans and animals, but also in crops and as contamination of food products with mycotoxins. We have recently been awarded funding to develop online webservices for genomic characterization of all pathogens capable of infecting animals, humans and plants, which includes fungi. However, genomics methods and workflows have so far not gained enough attention in relation to plant infecting or mycotoxin producing fungi. Databases of genomes of known fungal species have already been developed, as has gene databases of mycotoxin producing gene clusters, but an extensive linkage to fungal taxa is poorly described. Furthermore, it is known that a number of fungi including some used in food production have the gene cluster for mycotoxin production but do not express them. There is an urgent need to improve our understanding of the genomics of fungi, as well as to translate this into online services. Thus, as part of our GPAP project ( www.gpap.global ) and our responsibilities as advise provider to the Danish Food Administration we are seeking a PhD-candidate in fungal genomics with a focus on correlating genomes to phenotypes and developing webservices. This will include whole genome sequencing of fungi, culturing and phenotypic characterization and implementing tools in our widely used online webservice. Responsibilities And Qualifications Your main responsibility will be to create a webservice for identifying fungal taxa, mycotoxin-producing gene clusters and predict phenotypes under different growth conditions. You will perform complete genome sequencing (including the analyses) of a selected range of fungal to create an improved database of reference genomes. linkedin:4482076252.desc: The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in the field of Development of Data Science and AI for Spatial Data at the School of Computing on the Kuopio campus. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). Please find more information below and submit your application by 17 November 2026. Role and salary The demand for minerals required for energy transition and digitalisation is expanding mining faster than our ability to understand its impacts. MINE-THE-GAP (website), funded by the European Research Council (ERC), combines satellite imagery, mining data reports, and AI to map mining activities and their impacts worldwide and provide the information needed for more transparent and sustainable mining. We are seeking three motivated Doctoral Researchers (PhD Students) to join the project, each leading their own thesis on mapping different aspects of mining. As part of the MINE-THE-GAP team, you will, as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), have the opportunity to apply your data science and programming skills to a global sustainability challenge and to become an expert in handling large Earth observation datasets and scalable AI. We offer three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in a research group with strong international visibility. You will receive hands-on training in the processing of large Earth observation and spatial datasets, as well as in scalable AI methods, developing highly sought-after skills for careers in academia, industry, government, and non-governmental organizations. The position provides opportunities for international collaboration and research visits abroad through an extensive network of partner institutions, including the German Aerospace Center (DLR), GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Monash University Indonesia, and the University of Melbourne. You will benefit from close supervision, mentoring, and a supportive team environment, along with dedicated funding for conference participation, workshops, and scientific publications. One Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) will be recruited for each of the following three research topics: mining land use: semantic segmentation of satellite images to map mining areas (e.g., open pits, waste rock piles, tailings dams) mining waste: predicting terrain height changes from radar and optical satellite image time series to estimate mining waste minerals and commodities: image classification with multispectral and hyperspectral data to identify the minerals and commodities of mining sites. Within your chosen research topic, you will build, train, and validate scalable deep learning and computer vision models using large, multi-modal Earth observation data (e.g., Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, LiDAR, hyperspectral). You will work closely with the principal investigator, Victor Maus, postdoctoral researchers, and international collaborators, publish your results in international journals, present them at conferences, and contribute to open science. Your main duty as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) is to conduct research for the doctoral dissertation and to complete postgraduate studies. The following will be considered an advantage experience with machine learning or deep learning (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) or strong motivation to learn these skills experience with Earth observation or geospatial data, desirable, but we encourage anyone with a strong willingness to learn to apply experience with cloud computing or collaborative software development (e.g., GitHub) is also welcome. linkedin:4482055568.title: PhD in Safe Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints
linkedin:4482055568.desc: The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a PhD stipend in the field of Safe Learning Based Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints within the general study programme Electrical and Electronic Engineering; starting on 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The PhD Fellow will be based at the Automation and Control Section in Aalborg. In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk. Description of the position How can a team of autonomous robots operate safely and make progress when communication deteriorates, the environment is only partially known, and the team must continually reorganise? This PhD position addresses this challenge through research on safe and resilient planning, control, and coordination of heterogeneous robotic systems in demanding underground environments. The position combines scientific research with substantial hands-on engineering. You will develop and analyse new algorithms, implement robotic software, build realistic simulation and digital-twin environments, and carry out systematic experiments with physical robot platforms. We are looking for a researcher who enjoys connecting mathematical ideas to reliable real-world robotic systems. Description of the project The ROX6G EU Horizon project aims to develop autonomous robotic systems for exploring and collecting data in hazardous, poorly documented underground mines. Its heterogeneous robot teams combine exploration, mapping, sensing, and sampling with mobile, multi-hop 5G/6G connectivity. Because robots also act as communication nodes, they must adapt their movement and team roles to sustain communication without relying on fixed infrastructure installed throughout the mine. The project is coordinated by AAU. In addition, within ROX6G, AAU leads the activities on learning based multi-robot coordination and reconfiguration for connectivity preservation and on digital-twin generation and multimodal visualisation. The PhD candidate will contribute to both activities, collaborating with international partners across robotics, communications, sensing, and geological modelling. The main core of the PhD will focus on developing theoretical, algorithmic, and real-time implementation framework for on the fly autonomy of multi-robot control systems in uncertain and limited environments. In addition, methods will be evaluated through simulation, laboratory experiments, and project-level system integration and validation, with attention to safety, connectivity, and practical mission performance. Your work tasks The PhD fellow will be responsible for: Conducting research on safe and resilient learning based planning, control, and coordination of multi-robot systems operating under constraints and uncertainty. Actively contributing to the formulation and refinement of research questions within the doctoral project. Taking an active role in planning, implementing, and, when necessary, adapting the research plan. Designing, implementing, and evaluating the developed algorithms in realistic robotic simulation environments and on physical robotic platforms. Contributing to the development and implementation of digital twins by integrating robotic sensor data, to support real-time visualization, monitoring, and autonomous decision-making. Publishing research results in leading international journals and conferences, and presenting findings at project meetings and international scientific venues. Your competencies The successful candidate will hold a Master’s degree in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Control Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field, with a strong foundation in robotics, autonomous systems, planning, and/or control theory. We particularly value strong programming skills in Python and/or C++, familiarity with robotic software frameworks such as ROS/ROS 2, and demonstrated ability to implement, integrate, test, and troubleshoot robotic systems. Motivation for hands-on work with physical robot platforms, sensors, simulation, and experimental setups is important for this position. Experience with one or more of the following areas will be an advantage: multi-robot systems and graph-based coordination; safety-critical, robust, or optimisation-based control; autonomous navigation, localisation, simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM), or sensor fusion; simulation and digital-twin development using tools such as Gazebo, Isaac Sim, or Webots. Experience with data processing and visualisation, real-time robotic experiments, and research publications will also be considered positively. Applicants are not expected to have expertise in all these areas, but should be willing to learn and work across disciplines. You should be able to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment, approach technical challenges in a structured and self-driven manner, and communicate clearly in written and spoken English. Qualification requirements PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1039 of August 27, 2013 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. Who we are The Department of Electronic Systems at Aalborg University (AAU) conducts internationally recognised research and education across digital technologies, including robotics, AI, control systems, communications, sound, and cybersecurity. Within the department, the Advanced Robotics & AI research group advances self-learning autonomous robotic systems for reliable operation in extreme environments. Our research strengthens robotic autonomy and resilience, enabling systems to operate safely and with minimal supervision in challenging settings. How to apply Your application must include the following: Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position Curriculum Vitae (CV) Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) Master thesis and/or relevant publications, if any Other relevant documents( e.g. one or two recommendation letters) The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. Job Description Join the frontier of innovation in 6G: the future of mobile networks technology! In the Netherlands, a unique alliance of 60 top-notch ICT companies, semiconductor firms, and research institutions has united to spearhead specific aspects of 6G: (1) software antennas, (2) AI-driven network software, and (3) groundbreaking 6G applications. Join us as a PhD student in this prestigious Future Network Services (FNS) flagship project, where research and entrepreneurial pursuits converge. Future 6G infrastructures will involve multiple specialized AI agents that manage radio, transport, computing, and service resources across different domains and vendors. Although individual agents may optimize local objectives, their actions can interact, conflict, or compete for shared resources. This PhD will develop learning methods for coordinating such agentic systems under changing network conditions, incomplete information, and operational constraints. The research will build on constrained and optimistic online learning, distributed learning, and online game-theoretic methods. The developed framework will be studied in two main application areas: multi-domain resource management for AI-enabled services, and resilient network operation, including fault diagnosis, root-cause analysis, and autonomous remediation. The methods will be validated through FNS use-cases, network data, and experimental infrastructure in collaboration with industrial partners. You’ll be joining an internationally diverse and thriving team, providing ample opportunities for riveting sparring and knowledge sharing. fully-funded PhD programme Full Time Edinburgh Posted 7 hours ago Website CDT in Machine Learning Systems, University of Edinburgh About The CDT Machine Learning has a dramatic impact on our daily lives built on the back of improved computer systems. Systems research and ML research are symbiotic. Modern systems research targets the ubiquitous need for efficient ML. ML research, conversely, is directly affected by how methods will be deployed. Furthermore, systems research increasingly explores ML methods to improve systems, and ML research develops such methods. Major gains are made when the development of ML and systems are symbiotic and co-optimized. This is relevant across a broad spectrum of industries: in-car systems, medical devices, phones, sensor networks, condition monitoring systems, high-performance compute, and high-frequency trading. This CDT develops researchers with expertise across the systems-ML stack. This makes a cohort-based programme vital, treating ML Systems as a holistic discipline. Cohort interaction, and integration, give students real experience across multiple systems, approaches and methodologies. Company engagement is an integral part of the programme with built-in internships alongside entrepreneurship training. The PhD programme in Machine Learning Systems positions students for strong, ethically aware technical careers, developing the next generation of leaders. Students will develop foundational research skills in Computer Systems, Machine Learning, Hardware, Sensors and Control, Programming and Integrated Machine Learning Environments, AI Ethics, and Leadership and Entrepreneurship. At the end, all students will have extensive experience of real-world deployment and optimization of machine learning methods. Candidate’s profile An Ideal Candidate Would Typically Have a strong degree or higher qualification in a relevant field (e.g. computer science, mathematics, engineering, physical sciences, economics or any other field where evidence is provided of sufficient computing and mathematical background) solid experience of programming, machine learning methods and ideally deep learning environments (e.g. pytorch) or a computer systems background CDT studentships The CDT has a minimum of 10 fully-funded studentships available for September 2027 entry. Studentships include stipend, fees and research costs for 4 years. Home students will receive an enhanced stipend thanks to the Government TechFirst Scheme, in return of some additional requirements around widening participation and wider engagement with the TechFirst programme. As a UKRI-funded CDT, application is open to all UK/EU/non-EU citizens providing they meet the University PhD entry requirements. However, the number of students with international fees status that can be recruited is restricted (about 3 per year). An indication of the fees status categories, entry requirements and further details on eligibility criteria can be found on our website. Why Edinburgh? The University of Edinburgh is one of the best research-intense Universities in the world. The School of Informatics that hosts the CDT is consistently ranked among the world’s top 30 computer science departments. In 2026 QS World University Ranking by Subject, it is ranked 22nd for Computer Science and Information System, and 30th for Data Science and AI. The CDT students will be hosted in the state-of-the-art Informatics Forum in the heart of Scotland’s capital, consistently considered one of the most desirable places to live in the world. linkedin:4482130616.desc: Introduction Are you excited to solve technical challenges with a real-world application? Are you eager to build something truly unique in the world? Job Description Development of a pulsed electron source with extreme transverse bunch brightness, based on photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms, for time-resolved protein crystallography. Context: ERC-funded project “Cool T-ReX” Goal: Develop a unique and innovative instrument to enable time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons (and be the first in the world in doing so). Scientific relevance: Understanding how proteins function is crucial to improving medicine and unraveling processes that are fundamental to life. Time-resolved protein crystallography uniquely allows following the conformational change of a protein with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, yielding a “molecular movie” of how the protein performs its function. This is currently only possible on large-scale X-ray facilities. In this project we will build the very first instrument that can make such movies through time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons rather than X-rays, on a laboratory-scale setup. Next, through collaboration with leading research groups in time-resolved protein crystallography, we will demonstrate the instrument’s capabilities in time-resolved crystallography experiments on photo-active proteins with medical relevance (and used in the field of optogenetics, awarded this year’s Nobel Prize in Medicine!). Your role: Drive the development of this unique instrument. You will build on our research group’s two decades of experience in building electron sources based on the photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms. This technique has demonstrated electron pulses with record-low transverse temperatures, corresponding to a high transverse coherence, as needed for protein crystallography. In this project we will push this transverse coherence even further, making use of some of the unique capabilities of this source technology. The result will be an electron beam with a “transverse bunch brightness” that is three orders of magnitude beyond the current state of the art. To reach this ambitious goal, you will work with a team of experienced technicians, a second PhD student, a PostDoc, and the PI (Julius Huijts). We are part of the larger Coherence and Quantum Technology group in the Department of Applied Physics. Job Requirements A MSc degree in Applied Physics, Engineering Physics, Mechatronics with a strong physics component, or similar. You can work in a team, are open to new ideas, can communicate with people outside your own field. You take initiative, are able to organize your own work load. You have an affinity with the goal of this project. You have a background or a proven affinity with at least two of the following (please highlight this in your application): Mechanical and optical design Complex optical setups Charged particle optics Cold atoms High vacuum High voltage Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). A research-oriented attitude Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In Addition, We Offer You Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Starting date is somewhat flexible, but ideally Feb 1 2027. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). The Health Sciences unit provides a collaborative setting with multidisciplinary and multimethodological strengths in population health, supporting rigorous and impactful doctoral research. Our doctoral programs in Health Sciences, Epidemiology and Public Health (IPPE), and Medicine offer a strong methodological and research environment for completing an ongoing doctoral project within established research groups at the Health Sciences Unit. The programs provide advanced training in key areas of population health, supporting high-quality publication-oriented research and researcher training. Job Description The doctoral researcher will join the research project “The Nordic Occupational Exposome and Cancer: Decades of Change, Mixtures, and Inequalities” (NordExCan) , led by Principal Investigator Dr. Subas Neupane. The project examines how occupational exposures change over working life and how these exposures, individually and in combination, are associated with cancer incidence, mortality, and inequalities in the Nordic countries. The research builds on the Nordic Occupational Cancer (NOCCA) cohort and Nordic job-exposure matrices, using occupational histories and population and cancer registry data from Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, and Iceland. The doctoral researcher will mainly work on Work Package 1 , focusing on occupational exposure histories and their associations with cancer incidence. The work includes harmonising occupational and registry data, estimating cumulative and time-varying exposures, and examining the effects of exposure mixtures and changes in exposure over working life. The doctoral researcher will use epidemiological and statistical methods to investigate cancer risks, including differences by sex and socioeconomic position. Depending on the research needs, the doctoral researcher may also contribute to other work packages covering rare cancers, cancer survival, and causal pathways. The doctoral researcher will conduct research leading to a doctoral dissertation and contribute to scientific publications and conference presentations. The position also involves participating in project meetings and working closely with the Nordic research team. The research will be based on registry data analysed in secure environments using reproducible statistical methods. Qualifications A Master's degree in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, health sciences, data science, or a related field is required. The selected candidate must also meet the requirements for admission to a relevant doctoral programme at Tampere University. Applicants may be required to provide proof of English proficiency, such as IELTS or TOEFL scores, in accordance with the university's admission requirements. We are looking for a candidate with an interest in occupational and cancer epidemiology and good skills in quantitative research and statistical analysis. The candidate should be able to work independently and as part of a research team. Good written and spoken English skills are required. The selected candidate must also meet the requirements for admission to a relevant doctoral programme (Doctoral Programme in Health Sciences or International Doctoral Programme in Epidemiology and Public Health) at Tampere University. Previous experience in statistical programming, particularly R, and working with large-scale registry or longitudinal data will be considered an advantage. Experience in exposure assessment, survival analysis, or other epidemiological methods is also valuable. Familiarity with job-exposure matrices, time-varying exposures, multilevel models, or causal inference would be beneficial, but is not required. Previous experience with Nordic registry data is not required. We offer The position is fixed-term for 3 years starting in January 2027. Most of the research will take place physically in Tampere, Finland. The appointee is expected to reside in Finland while employed by Tampere University. linkedin:4482113481.desc: Job Description Are you passionate about using atomistic simulations and machine learning to accelerate the green transition? Do you want to understand, atom by atom, why electrolysers degrade, and design materials that make them last longer? Do you have a background in computational chemistry, physics, materials science or chemical engineering? Then this PhD opportunity at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) might be the perfect fit for you. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for the project ATOMIZE: Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells , a collaboration between DTU Physics and Topsoe, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF). Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC) are among the most efficient technologies for producing green hydrogen, but their long-term stability remains a key challenge for large-scale deployment. In this PhD project, you will use density functional theory and state-of-the-art machine-learning interatomic potentials to study SOEC electrode materials at the atomic scale and at length scales that were previously out of reach. The aim is to understand what governs electrode stability and how it can be improved. You will validate your simulations against advanced experimental characterization data. In practice, you will be hired at DTU Physics and join the Computational Catalysis group led by Associate Professor Alexander Bagger. The group has a long-term goal to develop predictive models and schemes for new reactions and materials in close connection with experiments. The group is part of the Catalysis Theory Center (CatTheory), which provides a strong infrastructure and computational facilities, including the Niflheim supercomputer with GPU nodes at DTU Physics. Responsibilities And Qualifications The successful candidate must have an MSc in physics, chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science or related areas, as well as a strong interest in atomistic modelling and machine learning for sustainable energy solutions. The candidate must display good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, be innovative and able to work both independently and in cross-disciplinary teams, as well as with international academic collaborators and industrial partners. Successful candidates must document: Experience with atomistic simulations & density functional theory (e.g. GPAW, VASP, ASE) Python programming skills Preferably, experience with machine-learning interatomic potentials (e.g. MACE, NequIP, or similar) Preferably, knowledge of solid oxide cells, oxide materials, electrochemistry or catalysis Preferably, experience with high-performance computing and Linux environments Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . Assessment You will be assessed against the responsibilities and qualifications stated above and the following general criteria: Atomistic modelling and DFT experience Python programming experience Machine learning experience Knowledge of materials science, electrochemistry or catalysis Communication skills We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. linkedin:4473525644.desc: Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain. The Biointerfaces Laboratory at Empa in St. Gallen is offering a PhD position in the field of antimicrobial biomaterials, microbiology, and bacteriophage therapy. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary research team developing innovative living hydrogel systems for the treatment of wound infections caused by antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) bacteria and biofilms. This project aims to create a new generation of injectable therapeutic hydrogels that combine beneficial probiotics and bacteriophages to simultaneously eradicate bacterial infections and promote tissue regeneration. With a strong translational focus, the project seeks to advance these living therapeutic systems toward clinically relevant solutions for wound infections and antimicrobial resistance. Your tasks You will contribute to the development of injectable, self-healing biomaterial-based hydrogels for the local delivery of probiotics and bacteriophages to wound sites. Your work will involve: Design and synthesis of injectable hydrogel systems Encapsulation and controlled delivery of probiotics and bacteriophages Engineering and characterization of phage-based antimicrobial strategies against pathogenic bacteria and biofilms Characterization and optimization of hydrogel properties and biological functionality Evaluation of tissue regeneration and the therapeutic potential of living therapeutics Elucidation of mechanisms of action and investigation of antimicrobial resistance evolution Your profile We are looking for a highly motivated and curious candidate with: A Master's degree in Biomaterials, Biomedical Engineering, Biotechnology, Microbiology, Molecular Biology, Chemistry, or a related field Strong interest in antimicrobial resistance, biomaterials, microbiology, or phage therapy Experience in one or more of the following areas: Microbiology and bacterial culture / Biofilm research / Biomaterials and hydrogels / Molecular biology or synthetic biology / Bacteriophages Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to an interdisciplinary team Previous experience with phages, hydrogels, wound healing models, or antimicrobial testing is advantageous. linkedin:4482112695.desc: Högskolan Väst drivs av att göra skillnad. Genom vår utbildning och forskning vill vi bidra till innovation, en positiv samhällsutveckling och en hållbar värld. Projektet fokuserar på hur digitala lärmiljöer kan stödja kompetensutveckling och bidra till att stärka personalens förmåga att möta komplexa vårdsituationer i den dagliga verksamheten. Det kan exempelvis handla om: • Hur VR och AI kan användas vid utbildning i palliativ vård för personer med demens inom kommunal vård- och omsorg. • Hur lärande inom palliativ vård påverkar vård och omsorg för personer med demens. • Hur utbildning med stöd av VR och AI påverkar bemötande av personer i livets slut. • Hur ett vetenskapligt förhållningssätt påverkar personal i kommunal vård och omsorg. Doktorandens vetenskapliga arbete i projektet Doktorandens vetenskapliga arbete kommer att genomföras inom ramen för ett forskningsprojekt med fokus mot palliativ vård i demensvård, inom kommunal vård och omsorg. Projektet tar sin utgångspunkt i de förändrade villkor som kommer med en åldrande befolkning och en pågående förskjutning av vården från slutenvård till kommunal vård och omsorg. Projektet undersöker hur virtual reality i kombination med en avatar kan stödja lärande och kompetensutveckling hos personal på ett särskilt boende för personer med demenssjukdom. En central fråga är hur denna form av lärande kan integreras i personalens arbete och hur erfarenheter från vårdpraktiken kan tas till vara. Doktorandprojektet syftar till att bidra till utvecklingen av framtidens utbildningsinsatser inom kommunal vård och omsorg, med särskilt fokus på palliativ vård och demensvård. Genom forskning med hög samhällsrelevans förväntas projektet generera kunskap som kan stärka kvaliteten i vården för äldre personer med komplexa vårdbehov. Projektet ska också bidra med kunskap om förutsättningarna för arbetsintegrerat lärande när ny teknik används för kompetensutveckling inom vård och omsorg. linkedin:4480771705.desc: Job description: Research Associate / Doctoral Candidate (m/f/d) at Psychosomatic Medicine and Developmental Neuroscience This position is available starting January 1, 2027, on a part-time basis (30 hours per week) for a fixed term of 3 years. Remuneration is based on the collective agreement for the public service of the federal states (TV-L) and, depending on personal qualifications, may be up to pay grade E13 TV-L. The position is affiliated with the Research Group Applied Developmental Neuroscience (Head: Prof. Dr. med. Stefan Ehrlich, PhD) as well as the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy (Head: Prof. Dr. med. habil. Vjera Holthoff-Detto). It is funded within the framework of the International Research Training Group (IRTG) 2773, in subproject P3, led by PD Dr. habil. Fabio Bernardoni, Dr. Delia Fuhrmann, and PD Dr. med. habil. Eva Mennigen. The International Research Training Group “Risks and Pathomechanisms of Affective Disorders” (IRTG 2773) is funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). It is a structured international graduate program conducted in cooperation between the Technical University (TU) Dresden and the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience at King’s College London. The successful candidate will receive comprehensive supervision by an experienced scientific team, including participation in a structured curriculum. This curriculum covers topics from developmental neuroscience, child and adolescent as well as adult psychiatry, clinical and cognitive psychology, and in particular computational science. The program is complemented by training in key transferable skills, such as data management and the presentation of scientific results. A six-month research stay at King’s College London under the supervision of Dr. Delia Fuhrmann is planned as part of the curriculum. Subproject P3 focuses on identifying multimodal markers of psychopathology and analysing their topological and network-based longitudinal structure. Using repeated clinical, neuroimaging, genetic, immunological, and behavioural data, we will model latent dimensions of risk and resilience and examine their developmental trajectories in relation to the clinical manifestation of affective disorders. The project will employ advanced machine learning and multivariate data analysis methods, including canonical correlation analysis (CCA), topological data analysis, longitudinal network analysis, and other data-driven approaches. The long-term goal is to advance targeted prevention strategies and personalized interventions. The successful candidate will work in an interdisciplinary team of researchers and clinicians. Responsibilities also include supervising and mentoring research interns, student assistants, and medical students within the project. The results generated in the project are expected to be presented at international conferences and published in peer-reviewed scientific journals. Your profile: an excellent Master’s or Diploma degree in cognitive, computational, and/or affective neuroscience, psychology, psychiatry, or a related field; applicants from quantitatively oriented disciplines such as computer science, physics, statistics, data science, biometrics, or machine learning are explicitly encouraged to apply prior scientific experience, e.g., in statistical methods; ideally, initial efforts toward scientific publications as first or co-author basic programming skills (e.g., Linux/Unix shell scripting, Python, or MATLAB) and/or experience in the analysis of imaging data (FSL, SPM, FreeSurfer, or comparable tools) are advantageous but not mandatory strong interest in mental disorders excellent organizational skills good command of German (B1), both written and spoken very good command of English (C1), both written and spoken We offer: work in a leading medical environment in research, teaching, and clinical care, combined with a highly specialized workplace the opportunity to implement your own ideas and work in an innovative, interdisciplinary team Compensation: Based on the TV-L collective bargaining agreement in pay grade E13, plus an annual bonus, provided you meet the personal requirements Vacation: 30 days of paid vacation Professional Development: Extensive internal and external training and development opportunities to continuously strengthen your skills Company Culture: We value transparency, team spirit, and shared success. Celebrate with us at company gatherings or sporting events like the Rewe Team Challenge Mobility: A subsidy for a job ticket to make your commute eco-friendly and convenient Health: We promote your well-being with modern fitness and exercise programs at our health center, mental health programs, and a comprehensive workplace health management program Shopping benefits: Take advantage of employee discounts at our clinic pharmacy, exclusive corporate benefits, and other shopping portals Work-life balance: Our Family Office supports you with questions regarding daycare spots, vacation programs, and caring for family members. We also offer flexible work arrangements Please include the following documents with your application: Cover letter, CV including publication list, a copy of your degree certificate, and a transcript of records (i.e., the official list of completed courses including grades), as well as your secondary school leaving certificate (e.g., Abitur). If available, please also include letters of recommendation and proof of English and German language proficiency. For further information, please contact PD Dr. habil. Fabio Bernardoni by phone at +49 351 458-15245 or via email at fabio.bernardoni@ukdd.de .

Position PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on ML-methods in climate modelling Employer The Department of Meteorology, Stockholm University The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain. We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic. The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment. You can read more about us here: the Department of Meteorology. Homepage: https://www.su.se/english/divisions/department-of-meteorology Location Stockholm, Sweden Sector Academic Relevant divisions Atmospheric Sciences (AS) Ocean Sciences (OS) Type Full time Level Student / Graduate / Internship Salary Open Preferred Education Master Application deadline 3 November 2026 Posted 21 October 2026 Job Description Project description Clouds and their responses to varying environmental conditions are particularly important determinants of current climate and future climate change. However, the resolution of a typical climate model is far too coarse to explicitly represent processes of relevance to cloud formation. Those processes therefore need to be parameterized, or represented as functions of large-scale state variables. Such sub-grid scale parameterizations are associated with large uncertainties, and are also computationally expensive. This project focuses on novel ways to bridge between micro- and global scales, to improve climate model accuracy, efficiency and generalizability, and leverage modern computer architecture. We will explore the use of machine learning (ML) models trained on combinations of observational data and high-resolution simulations, as alternatives to empirical parameterizations of essential, unresolved sub-grid scale processes related to turbulence, cloud formation and aerosol-cloud interaction. The tasks will include deriving and training data-driven models, coupling them to a large-scale climate model, evaluating the results against observations and traditionally parameterized models, and using the ML-enhanced model to estimate climate-relevant quantities like cloud radiative effects and forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with data scientists within the Swedish e-Science Research Centre, and contribute to development of methods with applicability also beyond climate science. The successful candidate will thereby develop their skills in atmospheric science and climate modelling, but also in data science and machine learning, and in communicating and collaborating within and across disciplines. Qualification Requirements In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be fulfilled before admission to the programme. You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. The specific entry requirements additionally require a minimum of 90 higher education credits in any of the fields of meteorology, oceanography, physics or chemistry; and at least 15 higher education credits in mathematics as well as a degree project of at least 15 higher education credits. At least 60 higher education credits of these courses must be on the second-cycle level. In addition, proficiency in English language, equivalent to English B in Swedish high school, is required. The specific entry requirements may also be fulfilled by a person who has otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. General syllabus for doctoral studies in atmospheric science and oceanography. Selection The selection between candidates who meet the entry requirements will be made with reference to their ability to benefit from the training. However, the fact that an applicant is deemed able to transfer credits from previous training or professional experience may not alone give the applicant priority over other applicants in the selection process. Admission decisions are made in accordance with current delegation policies. The assessment criteria for admission to the postgraduate programme in atmospheric sciences and oceanography are familiarity with the theory and applications of the subject, subject knowledge relevant to the research project, the ability to express oneself orally and in writing, proficiency in English, analytical ability, creativity, initiative, independence and the ability to work collaboratively. The assessment of the applicant’s ability in these respects are based on the relevance and results of completed higher education courses, the quality and scope of the independent project, references, interviews and a personal statement from the applicant describing their expectations of, and intentions regarding, the programme. Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University. About The Employment Starting date as per agreement. We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %). A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. Stockholm University strives to be a workplace free from discrimination and with equal opportunities for all. For more information about the PhD programme, please contact the study director, Associate Professor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se.
